News.title: Brothers who raped & groomed teenage girl in Rotherham 20 years ago go on the run – with one ‘fleeing to Pakistan’
News.content:
RAPISTS ESCAPE Brothers who raped & groomed teenage girl in Rotherham 20 years ago go on the run – with one ‘fleeing to Pakistan’







Next

TWO brothers who raped and groomed a teenage girl in Rotherham 20 years ago have gone on the run – with one allegedly fleeing to Pakistan.

Brothers Mudasar Hussain, 37, and Ghazanfar Hussain, 42, were convicted at Sheffield Crown Court along with Kamir Ifzal Khan, 37, on Thursday, the National Crime Agency confirmed.



Mudasar Hussain and Khan absconded ahead of their trial, and at least one of them has fled abroad.

The NCA said its officers working to locate the two men and are appealing to the public for any information that could help.



Mudasar Hussain was on conditional bail awaiting trial and had surrendered his passport to the NCA as one of those conditions.

An NCA spokesman said that, while he may still be in the UK, it is also possible that he has left the country illegally.



Khan, who was also on unconditional court bail ahead of his trial, is known to have fled the country on a flight to Qatar on September 22.

Investigators believe he travelled on to Pakistan.



Of the three defendants, only Ghazanfar Hussain was in court to hear Thursday’s verdicts, the NCA said.

The agency confirmed that Mudasar Hussain was found guilty on Thursday of 12 counts of rape.

Khan was found guilty of two counts of rape and one count of trafficking for sexual exploitation, and Ghazanfar Hussain was found guilty of one count of rape.

The CPS said Mudasar Hussain and Khan separately targeted the girl when she was 13 and 14 years old.

The complainant, who is now in her 30s, was groomed and sexually abused first by Mudasar Hussain, then separately by Ghazanfar Hussain and Khan between 2008 and 2010.



Mudasar Hussain, who she knew as “Muddy”, was around 20 at the time.

He plied the girl with drugs and alcohol and, after a few months, took her to a house in Rotherham where he raped her for the first of many times.

The NCA said the girl was abused by Mudasar Hussain “countless times over the course of around 18 months, at the house, in local public spaces and in his car”.

She told officers that Hussain used violence to coerce her, including threatening her with a baseball bat.

The agency said Ghazanfar Hussain – nicknamed “Gucci” – raped the girl when his brother left the UK for a period.



She did not know they were related.

The NCA said the girl met Khan, who was about 20 at the time, when she began frequenting a local takeaway where he worked.

Khan – nicknamed “Kammy” – gave her food, money and cigarettes, and took her out on deliveries, leading her to believe that they were in a relationship.

But he raped her during the abuse which lasted around seven months.

According to the NCA, there were a number of times when Khan took her to a house where he asked her to have sex with other men who were present.



She always refused, but Khan took her to a different address where he left her alone with a man, who raped her.

The NCA said that, when Khan returned and found the girl in distress, he told her that he had owed the man a favour.

Ghazanfar Hussain has been remanded in custody ahead of his sentencing at Sheffield Crown Court on Friday.

Mudasar Hussain and Khan will also be sentenced on Friday in their absence.

The trio were arrested as part of Operation Stovewood, the huge NCA investigation set up in 2014 in the wake of the Rotherham child exploitation scandal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The NCA says Stovewood is the largest law enforcement operation of its kind undertaken in the UK and has identified and supported around 1,150 potential victims, securing 60 convictions against 55 people.

Head of Operation Stovewood Philip Marshall said: “The victim has shown tremendous courage in reporting the predatory grooming, exploitation and sustained sexual abuse these men subjected her to as a child.”

News.title: Horror as 16 primary school children rushed to hospital after eating muffins filled with BATTERIES at bake sale
News.content:
POISON PANIC Horror as 16 primary school children rushed to hospital after eating muffins filled with BATTERIES at bake sale







Next

SIXTEEN schoolchildren have been rushed to hospital after biting into muffins laced with toxic battery buttons.

The terrifying scare unfolded at a primary school in Germany on Thursday during an event where attendees had brought in homemade baked treats.

A team of 35 emergency responders raced to Frobel Elementary School in the region of Saxony-Anhalt after the potentially lethal metal discs were discovered hidden inside the muffins.

The Johanniter rapid response team and several fire department units were initially placed on alert but then stood down.





One pupil was rushed to hospital in an ambulance, while 15 other children were driven to A&E by their parents.

The condition of the children is currently unknown.

It also remains unclear whether one or more of the children actually swallowed the small batteries.

However, local officials warned that swallowed batteries can rapidly become lodged in the gullet and inflict severe internal burns.

German health chiefs have urged parents not to wait for symptoms – such as vomiting, coughing, fever or loss of appetite – as dangerous side effects can take hours to appear.

Three children have already complained of symptoms, according to local reports.

It is currently unclear how the hazardous batteries ended up inside the mixture or what the motive behind the move could be.

Police officers in the town of Coswig have launched a probe to clarify the circumstances surrounding the scare.



District Administrator Christian Tzygch praised emergency services for their rapid response.

He said: “My thoughts are with the children and their families who are now waiting for the results of the investigations.

“Now it is up to the police to investigate how this incident occurred.”

City officials said all affected parents have been notified.

Classes at the school continued as normal following the incident.



The horror discovery comes after needles, nails and screws were found hidden inside Halloween treats after parents spotted suspicious puncture holes in the sweets.

A nine-year-old girl cut her tongue after biting into a chocolate bar containing a metal pin at least 5cm long.

Meanwhile, two children aged 11 and 12 discovered metal staples concealed in chewing gum collected while trick-or-treating.

Police feared the sharp objects were deliberately planted to harm children, sparking urgent warnings to parents across Germany.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officers urged families to “check sweets for possible puncture marks” and contact police immediately if “anything suspicious” was found.



The girl was injured in the northern town of Bremervörde as several other children narrowly escaped harm after biting into tampered treats.

News.title: Four schoolgirls die after eating ‘poisoned oranges’ handed out by student, 12, as cops seal off school & launch probe
News.content:
Next

FOUR schoolgirls have died after allegedly eating poisoned oranges which were handed out by another pupil.

Three of the girls, aged 9 to 11, died at home after reportedly complaining of stomach pain as the fourth was rushed to hospital and died just an hour later.



The shocking deaths took place on November 10, in Uganda.

Eight pupils had eaten the suspected laced oranges, which had been handed out by a 12-year-old pupil, according to the school.



The school in the Ugandan capital of Kampala has since been shut down as police homicide detectives investigate the tragedy.

The head teacher of the Ta’aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre, has since been detained as part of the police probe.

Rashid Musa, a local resident and neighbour of one of the schoolgirls said the oranges were given out in a green polythene bag to the girls.

Kampala Metropolitan Police spokesperson, Rachel Kawala, said detectives will visit the village where the oranges came from as part of their investigations.

Postmortem examinations are also currently being conducted to establish the exact causes of death, according to Kawala.

Ugandan media shared footage of grieving parents describing their children’s final moments.



Some dismayed family members have accused the school of failing to provide information quickly enough, before the health of their children deteriorated irreversibly.

One of the girls, 11-year-old Mariam Nakitende, daughter of Hassan Magumba of Kiwatule, was brought home at around 1pm after eating the orange.

Her father said she was foaming at the mouth and semi-conscious.



She was rushed to hospital but was sadly pronounced dead an hour later.

The parent said the school had not provided adequate information and that the family were not allowed to meet with a school administrator.

Allegedly, the parent only received phone calls from the school asking after the child’s condition.

Police have offered their condolences to the affected community and will provide more information following progress in the investigation.

The deaths follow growing anxiety concerning health and safety in Ugandan schools.



Previous incidents involving suspected contaminated food have previously left Ugandan students hospitalised with stomach pain and vomiting.

'DEVIL' CAGED Gangster who abused model girlfriend until she suffered brain damage in suicide attempt & strangled her sister is jailed







Next

A NOTORIOUS gangster known as “Mr Big” abused his model girlfriend until she was left brain damaged in a suicide attempt.

John Gizzi subjected Natasha Farah to a campaign of bullying by trying to control what she wore and repeatedly abusing her.



The mixed martial arts fighter also punched her in a car park, hit her at a busy gym and threw a “heavy dumbell” at her in a string of attacks that left her suicidal.

His abuse culminated in mum-of-one Natasha attempting to take her own life – causing her to suffer severe brain damage.



Gizzi, who has a string of convictions, also strangled her sister Samantha Farah when she tried to help her sister.

The thug later rammed her in a 4X4 and threatened to “put her in a hole” as she defended Natasha.

Gizzi admitted to using coercive and controlling behaviour against Natasha Farah between March 1, 2025 and April 8, 2026.

He also pleaded guilty to failing to disclose a mobile phone’s PIN to police on April 27, 2026.

Gizzi further admitted intentional strangulation against Natasha’s sister – Samantha Farah – on April 3 this year for grabbing her neck in a pub.

He was jailed for four years and 11 months and made subject of restraining orders and Domestic Abuse Protection Orders spanning 15 years.



Judge Simon Mills said he could not sentence Gizzi for Natasha’s current condition but if “further evidence came to light” a police investigation could begin.

He added: “This is one of the worst cases of coercive control, in the context of domestic abuse, that can be contemplated.

“You would use dreadful, misogynistic, and sexist language towards her on a frequent basis.



“Language like this is serious, because it’s part of the process of humiliating and belittling a person, destroying their sense of self-worth.”

Natasha’s mum Denise described Gizzi as a “smiling devil monster” as she begged the judge to “make an example” of him.

She said: “My daughter has been left brain damaged because of this man, because of this monster, who won’t stand before us today.

News.title: Mum told mule son ‘don’t go for a s**t now’ before he died in hotel when bag of cocaine burst in his stomach, court told
News.content:
DRUG DEATH Mum told mule son ‘don’t go for a s**t now’ before he died in hotel when bag of cocaine burst in his stomach, court told







Next

A WOMAN has been accused of manslaughter after her son was found dead in a hotel room with a burst package of cocaine in his stomach.

Jensen Westhead, 20, swallowed the packages before flying from Manchester to Dubai in December 2024.



The man from Thornton-Cleveleys in Lancashire was found dead the day after in his room at the Avalon Hotel after he arrived, December 5.

Westhead’s mother, Rebecca Hatch, has been accused of manslaughter and drugs offences in connection with his death.



The 45-year-old is currently on trial, alongside four others including Jensen’s stepfather, Glenn Hatch, 51.

Prosecutors allege that Rebecca and Glenn Hatch were accomplices in Jensen’s drug muling, having helped him to renew his passport and taking him to the airport.



Prosecutor Jacob Hallam KC presented the court with mobile phone messages between Westhead and his mother as he travelled to the UAE.

On the flight, Westhead told his mother: “Need a s**t real bad.”



Hatch allegedly replied: “FFS don’t go for a s**t now son. Do it as soon as you land. Don’t say nothing at all till you land there to no one x.”

The prosecution has said that this shows Rebecca Hatch’s knowledge of her son smuggling drugs in Dubai.

Other texts between the pair show Westhead sending images of laxatives to his mother, to which she replied talking about duty-free purchases, jurors heard.

Following Westhead’s death, Lancashire Police officers visited the Hatches’ home to inform them of his death.

Officers reported that Hatch said to her husband: “I told you this would happen, they f*****g left him.”



When asked what she meant, she reportedly didn’t answer.

The couple allegedly said Westhead was travelling alone and meeting friends in Dubai, and that they had FaceTimed him when he got to his hotel.

Mr Hallam said: “The prosecution say they weren’t being candid about their knowledge of, or involvement in Jensen’s travels, nor their knowledge of or involvement in the purpose behind them.

“He travelled to Dubai in order to smuggle drugs out of this jurisdiction and import them into Dubai. He did that, we say, with the knowing assistance of Rebecca Hatch, Glenn Hatch and the other defendants in the dock.”

They are on trial alongside Alexander Tofton, 33 and of Lytham St Annes, accused of being the UK arm of the smuggling operation, Joseph Watson, 32 and of Wednesbury, accused of being the Dubai arm, and Steven Stephenson, 48 and of Denton, accused of having given Westhead the drugs.



During the post-mortem investigation into Westhead’s death, Stephenson’s fingerprints were found on the package of drugs, the court was told.

Rebecca Hatch’s phone was allegedly in contact with Tofton’s and Glenn Hatch allegedly Googled ‘drug mule meaning’ on his phone.

Five days after Westhead’s death, Tofton allegedly changed his phone and Stephenson did a factory reset on his.

Police also recovered writing from Tofton’s home, which they believe refers to Westhead, that said: “Feel sorry, feel responsible for death.”

Messages were reportedly recovered from Watson’s phone that read: “I don’t know if I can come back to the UK because of that thing with that kid. Like there’s a chance I would get nicked.”



Rebecca and Glenn Hatch, Tofton, Watson, and Stephenson all deny manslaughter as well as being concerned in exporting a class A drug.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tofton has also pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose his phone PIN to police.

The trial continues.

News.title: At least four dead after helicopter crashes and explodes in massive fireball in Turkey
News.content:
Next

AT least four people have been killed after a military helicopter crashed and erupted into a terrifying fireball in Turkey, its defence ministry says.

The S-70 chopper smashed to the ground in the eastern province of Malatya on Thursday.



The ministry said the reason for the crash is not yet known, with rescuers attending the scene.

Dramatic footage shows the fiery wreck of the helicopter as sparks fly from a nearby electrical line.



Horrified onlookers can be seen watching the chopper burn.

Ambulances and firefighters rushed to the scene in Samanköy.



The defence ministry said in a statement: “One S-70 type helicopter crashed in Malatya for an unknown reason.

“The wreckage has been reached, and search and rescue operations have commenced immediately.”

The number of people onboard the S-70, known as a Black Hawk, is not yet known.

Officials have not released what the military chopper was doing at the time of the crash.



It comes just days after two helicopters collided in Nepal, killing one tourist and injuring three people.

Terrifying footage showed the two choppers smashing together mid-air before spiralling out of control.

Hikers watched in horror as the tragedy unfolded just metres above them ​near the Mount Everest base camp on Tuesday.



An Indian national who had been onboard the Fishtail Air helicopter, died from his injuries after the crash.

He has been named by authorities as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu.

Shailesh Krishna Patel, 49, a New Zealand national who was a passenger on the same aircraft, suffered injuries.

He was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu via a Prabhu Air helicopter, Inspector Mausam Tamang said.

Both helicopter pilots were also injured and transported to Kathmandu for further medical treatment.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Both helicopters attempted to land at Pheriche helipad simultaneously.

CCTV footage showed the two choppers drifting dangerously close together before their rotor blades made contact.

News.title: Boy, 4, dies after being found unconscious in water tank in Spanish holiday hotspot
News.content:
HOLIDAY TRAGEDY Boy, 4, dies after being found unconscious in water tank in Spanish holiday hotspot







Next

A FOUR-YEAR-OLD boy has died after falling into a water tank in southern Spain.

The youngster initially went missing but was later found unconscious in the water, according to reports.

The horror incident unfolded at a farmhouse in Ugíjar, Granada on Thursday.

During the morning, his panicked family went door-to-door alerting neighbours that they had lost sight of their child, local reports say.





Shortly after midday, emergency services received a call about a young boy who had drowned in a water tank.

Paramedics rushed to the scene in an attempt to save the child but were tragically unable to save him.

The boy, who has not been named, is understood to have been staying with his family in the area for a few days when tragedy struck.

Reports say the family were foreign and struggled to communicate in Spanish with emergency services.

However, the nationality of the victim is yet to be confirmed.

Ugíjar Town Hall have announced a day of official mourning in light of the youngster’s death.

In a statement, local officials said: “In light of the tragic death of a minor visiting our municipality, it is deemed appropriate to declare a day of official mourning as a heartfelt expression of the general condolences of Ugíjar, from 00:00 hours on November 13, 2026, until 23:59 hours on November 13, 2026.

“During this period, flags will fly at half-mast outside all municipal buildings.



“We are suspending all municipal events as a sign of respect and express our deep sorrow for the incident that occurred in our municipality.”

The tragedy comes after a British boy died in hospital after being pulled unconscious from a hotel swimming pool in Lanzarote.

The five-year-old was airlifted to hospital after suffering a cardiac arrest in September.

Medics and a hotel lifeguard desperately tried to resuscitate the youngster – and managed to restore his pulse at the scene.

The child was then flown by air ambulance to the Materno University Hospital on the neighbouring island of Gran Canaria.



He was placed in intensive care – before passing away in hospital.

It came just days after a Brit pensioner reportedly drowned after wading out to sea in Lanzarote.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His wife raised the alarm after she lost sight of her husband in the water, sparking a major search operation.

Helicopters and firefighters scoured the beach – before finding the unnamed man’s body in the water.

News.title: Glam RAF veteran stole £37k from struggling GP surgery she worked at then splurged cash on online shopping
News.content:
CON THE ROB Glam RAF veteran stole £37k from struggling GP surgery she worked at then splurged cash on online shopping







Next

A GLAMAROUS RAF veteran nabbed £37,000 from the cash-strapped GP surgery she worked at then splurged it on online shopping.

Rachel Pompa, 46, became a practice manager at the surgery in Ammanford, Wales, after 12 years working as a paramedic with the RAF.



The mum-of-two had served in Kosovo, Afghanistan and Iraq before she started at the practice, Swansea Crown ourt heard.

However, the deceitful veteran managed to swindle £37,000 from the surgery, which was already on its knees.



Tasked with paying suppliers and sorting bills, Pompa oversaw all the practice’s financial transactions.

It was only when a doctor spotted some “irregular” exchanges on the business bank account that the alarm was raised.



Statements showed Pompa had been using surgery money to buy goods and subscriptions, including one from Amazon.

The mum was interviewed by police in Febrary 2023, where she denied stealing thousands of pounds from the practice.



Pompa later failed to show up to two follow-up meetings in 2024, sending police a GP letter stating it was not in her best interests to attend.

Her colleagues at the practice said her behaviour and spending had had an “enormous detrimental impact” on the surgery’s management and staff morale.

In a statement, they said the theft was a “major insult, financially and personally” carried out by someone they had trusted.

They added staff were left “deeply shocked and distressed” at what she did.

Pompa, of Morriston, Swansea, pleaded guilty to fraud by abuse of position between 2019 and 2022.



The plea was on the basis that she stole £37,000.

Defending, Owen William said she had been diagnosed with complex PTSD and depressive disorder, “directly attributable” to her time as a paramedic.

He said the offending took place when her mental health was at its worst.

Judge Huw Rees said the small practice had been buckling under huge financial pressures when she took the money.

Pompa was sentenced to 14 months in prison suspended for 18 months.



A proceeds of crime investigation will now be launched with a £37,000 compensation order to be made from a confiscation once her marital home is sold.

News.title: Israeli airstrike hits Gaza hospital surgical wing — killing six including doctor and injuring 28
News.content:
Israeli airstrike hits Gaza hospital surgical wing — killing six including doctor and injuring 28

Gaza's health officials say Israel bombed a Gaza hsospital causing more death destruction in the Palestinan enclave — as the military says it attacked a Hamas terror cell

View 4 Images Israel air-strike hits vehicle near al-Shifa hospital (Image: Getty Images)

An Israeli airstrike hit the surgical wing of a major hospital in southern Gaza on Thursday, killing six people, including a doctor, and wounding at least 28 others, local medical officials said.

‌



‌



The Israeli military said it struck a Hamas commander and other militants, contradicting the claims made by Gaza's Health Ministry.

‌



Nasser Hospital in the city of Khan Younis is one of the few functioning medical facilities left in Gaza, whose infrastructure has been decimated.

‌



The Israeli military has raided or laid siege to hospitals across the territory, accusing Hamas of using them as command centers and to hide fighters. It has also destroyed medical equipment and supplies and killed or detained hundreds of healthcare workers.

‌

The Gaza Health Ministry said Thursday's strike killed general surgeon Rizk Abu Shaira. Inside the building, parts of several floors were either severely damaged or destroyed.

Debris was scattered across hospital beds and equipment, and rebar dangled from the ceiling. British surgeon Goher Rahbour, who is volunteering at Nasser Hospital, said that the strike occurred just after midnight and shook the whole building.

‌



He said: "It was extremely smoky.”

View 4 Images Vehicle catches fire in Gaza City ater Israeli strike (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



He added that he had been operating alongside Abu Shaira just hours before the strike, saying: "Lovely guy, happy and smiling.” Ahmed al-Farra, a doctor and the general director of the hospital, said no warning came before the attack.

He said surgeries had been suspended, as had work in the radiology department and the laboratory, because of damage to the building where medical personnel were already struggling to provide care due to supply shortages and "miserable" conditions.

‌



He said other nearby medical facilities were not equipped to do the type of "specialized surgeries" that Nasser Hospital had been providing, leaving patients in need of them to "face an unknown fate."

He added: "Imagine if this event happened in another country in the world. Would the world fall silent about it? No, by God, no. No one's safe here.”

‌



In armed conflict, hospitals and their staff are protected under international humanitarian law. But a hospital can lose its protected status if it is used for military purposes.

View 4 Images Vehicle catches fire in Gaza after Israeli strike (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



The Israeli Defence Force said Hamas had "established a presence within the hospital complex" and that the commander had turned it "into a headquarters."

The war in Gaza started on October 7, 2023, when Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel, killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 others hostage.

‌



Since then, Israel's retaliatory offensive has killed more than 74,600 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.

The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, maintains detailed records and its figures are seen as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and independent experts.

Article continues below

It does not distinguish between civilians and militants in its toll but says women and children make up around half the dead. Israel has continued to strike Gaza despite a U.S.-backed ceasefire and controls at least 60% of the enclave.

Since the truce went into effect in October 2025, Israeli strikes and gunfire have killed 1,622 people, health authorities say. Five Israeli soldiers have also been killed during that period.

News.title: Asda sparks fuel price war by slashing pump costs by average 4p per litre
News.content:
Asda sparks fuel price war by slashing pump costs by average 4p per litre

Supermarket giant Asda has cut petrol and diesel prices by average 4p a litre at more than 320 forecourts across the country, bringing savers for motorists reeling from the sky high cost of filling up

View 2 Images Asda says pump prices have been cut by an average 4p a litre at 321 of its forecourts (Image: Getty Images)

Asda has launched a pump price war by knocking an average 4p a litre off petrol and diesel.

‌



‌



The supermarket giant has implemented immediately at 321 forecourts next to its large stores across the country. Drivers filling a typical 55-litre family car could save up to £2.20 per tank.

‌



The move will put pressure on rivals to follow suit, bringing welcome savings for drivers who have been pummelled by punishingly high pump prices for much of this year. Fuel prices have soared since the start of US President Donald Trump’s war with Iran.

‌



Figures from the RAC show Asda’s national average was 165.8p a litre for petrol ahead of the cut, but ranging from 155.9p to 172.9p across the country. This was already cheaper than Morrisons’ average 166.1p, 167p at Sainsbury’s, and 167.7p at Tesco.

View 2 Images Asda's 4p off fuel could lead to a new price war if rivals follow suit (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Save up to 25 per cent on petrol by removing this one item from your car READ MORE :

RAC and AA give new updates as experts say when petrol and diesel prices will fall READ MORE :

New Asda boss steps up fight for shoppers

Asda was also cheapest for diesel, at an average 194.5p per litre, compared with next lowest Sainsbury’s at 195.6p, Tesco’s 195.8p, and Morrisons’ 196p.

‌



Asda’s announcement is part of efforts by the chain to revive flagging grocery sales. The Leeds-based giant has been weighed down by heavy debts since a private quality led takeover, and has lost ground to competitors on all sides.

Asda is keen to be seen as a key destination for drivers looking for fuel savings. The cut is one of the first to be announced by new boss David Potts since the former Morrisons’ chief took over earlier this month.

‌



It comes hot on the heels of the changes announced earlier this week for store managers to open more full-service checkouts, spend more time on the shop floor and getting more product on shelves.

Mr Potts said: “When we get the fundamentals right, customers notice. Earlier this week, I set out a renewed focus on making the shopping trip better for our customers, and that means getting it right at the pumps too.

Article continues below

“With Christmas upon us, 4p off every litre helps families where they’re feeling it most, alongside the value we are offering across our food and clothing range online and in store.”

Asda is hoping to win over value conscious families after it was named the cheapest supermarket for branded groceries by consumer group Which?

News.title: Washington DC shooting live: Suspect takes own life as one dead and four wounded
News.content:
A gunman has taken his own life in Washington DC after shooting five people close to the White House, killing at least one and leaving another in critical condition

Washington DC shooting live: Suspect takes own life as one dead and four wounded

A man who shot five people in Washington DC, killing one before barricading himself inside an apartment, has taken his own life.

The shootings were reported in Logan Circle, around one mile north of the White House.

Shots were fired inside a gym - Vida Logan Circle - with representatives for the business saying the premises will remain closed until further notice "following a shooting".

Police were negotiating with the suspect over the phone, after he barricaded himself in the apartment, when they heard a shot. He has since died.

Police chief Jeffery W Carroll told reporters the shooter is believed to have been involved in a dispute with the homeowners' association of the building.

A major emergency response followed and nearby schools were placed into lockdown. The scene is now safe, police said, but road closures remain in place.

News.title: Russell Myers: 'Prince William's big looming question that we have a right to be answered'
News.content:
When Prince William inherited the Duchy of Cornwall in 2022, he spoke of transforming a 700-year-old estate into a force for social good.

Four years on, that transformation is under way, but it has been dogged by controversy at almost every turn, and too often it has looked as though the Prince was reacting to headlines rather than leading from the front. The first storm broke in 2024, when a joint investigation by the Mirror and Channel 4's Dispatches found scores of Duchy rental homes blighted by damp and mould.

In the same year, the Sunday Times and Dispatches revealed the estate was earning millions from public bodies, including a £37million deal to lease Dartmoor Prison to the Ministry of Justice and hundreds of thousands of pounds from leases with state schools. For a prince who has made homelessness his signature cause, the optics were nothing short of dreadful.

Prince George’s incredible artwork unveiled for the first time by dad Prince William READ MORE :

View 3 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales at the Festival of Remembrance (Image: Getty Images)

‌



William's response came the following summer, when the Duchy announced it would waive rent for grassroots groups and cut charges for local charities by up to half.

This move was certainly welcomed, and while I have sympathy for William taking the time to “get under the hood” of the organisation, as his aides continually point to, there is an argument that it took a television expose to bring it about.

Granted, investigative journalists are worth their weight in gold in unearthing wrongdoing and scandal, but if your name is above the shop, surely you need to apply yourself to the minute detail needed when CEOs are brought in to change a business from the ground up.

View 3 Images William in Rio, where last year's Earthshot Prize Awards were held (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



This year has brought fresh trouble. In May, William unveiled plans to sell around a fifth of the estate over the next decade to fund more than £500million of investment in affordable housing, nature recovery and renewable energy.

A bold vision, but one that landed badly with tenant farmers on the 3,000-acre Bradninch estate in Devon, some of whose families have worked that land for generations. Possession notices gave them six months to buy or leave. After a furious backlash, the Duchy's rural director met tenants last week, apologised for underestimating how long the process would take and agreed to independent valuations.

I understand William has been unhappy at how it was handled and this may well be the catalyst for further changes in how he, and the Duchy operates from now on.

Then there is tax. A dirty word historically for the royals, but again under pressure, they have been forced to change their ways. However, unlike his father, William has declined to reveal how much he pays on an income of around £23million a year, and this month an anti-corruption tsar urged him to make clear whether the Duchy is a private estate or a public asset. It is a question that will not and should not be dismissed.

‌



View 3 Images The Waleses during the state visit to the UK of the Sultan of Oman (Image: Mark Cuthbert/Getty Images)

None of this means William lacks good intentions. He clearly wants the Duchy to do more for the communities it touches. But good intentions and good management are not the same thing, and the pattern of acting only once the criticism mounts is one he needs to break.

The same question of public versus private hangs over his work abroad. Next week William flies to Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize, his environmental awards and arguably the project closest to his heart. I will be there and can tell you first hand from reporting from London, to Rio to Boston, that it actually does matter and yields results.

Yet this is not a royal tour in the traditional sense and sources in government tell me there is growing frustration of a lack of engagement with the Foreign Office build a programme around Britain's relationship with our partners abroad, which the heir to the throne would usually be considered a great asset.

‌



If you take the King’s recent nine-day trip to the Caribbean as an example, which was planned with the country's diplomatic interests at its core. For all its difficulties, it showed what a royal visit can do for Britain abroad.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

So here is the question. Is it acceptable for the future King and Queen to build their diaries around personal projects, from Earthshot, to early years, and a bit of football chat thrown in (see William's guest edit of Country Live this week) however worthy, while the traditional work of representing the nation overseas is left to a monarch approaching his eighties?

William and Catherine are public servants, funded and housed by virtue of their position. The public and the government have a right to expect that position is used for the country's benefit as well as their own causes.

‌



New episodes of the Mirror's award-winning royal podcast Pod Save The King are available each week on YouTube. Subscribe to the Pod Save The King YouTube channel to make sure you don’t miss an episode www.youtube.com/@podsavethekingmirror . And keep in touch on Instagram @podsave .

News.title: Jason Manford told off by Michael Ball over backstage theatre superstition
News.content:
Tomorrow is Friday 13 and comedian Jason Manford isn’t taking any chances on the unluckiest date on the calendar. He won’t be leaving his house - in fact, he may be hiding in the airing cupboard. Superstitious Jason, 45, says: “You can’t be too careful on Friday 13.”

Friday 13 has been considered unlucky for hundreds of years as Judas - the disciple who betrayed Jesus - was the 13th guest to arrive at The Last Supper, and Friday was once being known as ‘Hangman’s Day,’ because it was the usual day for hangings.

But Jason doesn’t restrict his superstitions to this one unlucky day. He says: “I won’t walk under ladders, I'm a bit funny about the cracks in the pavement and I always say ‘touch wood’.”

Convinced that empty pockets improve his live performance, the comedian adds: “If I've had a weird gig, I come off, check my pockets and go, ‘ah, it was this receipt!’”

‌



View 5 Images Salford-born Jason Manford supports Manchester City (Image: Manchester City FC via Getty Images)

And the Manchester City supporter, who lives in Stockport, also has lucky underpants that he wears to matches. “When you’ve worn the same boxer shorts or whatever for the last three wins, you think, ‘It's on me. It's not Haaland, it's my boxers.’” he says.

Actors and performers are notoriously superstitious, so Jason, who has two children with his second wife, TV producer Lucy Dyke, and four from his first marriage, is in good company. He says: "Within my industry, there's so many superstitions. You can’t whistle backstage in a theatre, it’s bad luck. I got a telling off from Michael Ball when we appeared in Sweeney Todd together.

“I heard this booming voice - ‘who's whistling?’ I had to go to his dressing room. He said, ‘right, you need to turn around three times.’ I said, ‘give over.’ He went, ‘do it.’ So I did. He went, ‘okay, the curse is gone.’

‌



View 5 Images Alfie Boe, Jason Manford and Michael Ball (Image: ITV)

“Back in the day, you had sandbags that would drop to pull the curtains back. You would tell the guy in the flies to drop them by whistling. So you can't be wandering around a theatre whistling in case a sandbag drops on your head.”

But performers are far from the only superstitious Brits. New research produced as part of the Lloyds Insurance Don’t Bank on Luck campaign - which stresses the need to be prepared for the unexpected - revealed that 7.2 million Brits dodge Friday 13, to avoid bad luck.

Fifty four per cent of Brits say they’re superstitious - escalating to 73% of people in their 20s. Belfast is the UK's superstition capital, followed closely by Birmingham, Edinburgh, Manchester, and Nottingham.

‌



View 5 Images Jason Manford and Prince William during the Royal Variety Performance 2025 at the Royal Albert Hall (Image: Matt Crossick/ITV/Shutterstock)

Jason, who is hosting the Royal Variety Performance 2026 at the Royal Albert Hall on November 20, in the presence of King Charles and Queen Camilla - a gig he describes as being like a comedian’s “Wembley Cup Final,’ will certainly be ensuring he has empty pockets on the night.

The funnyman, who says Prince William and Princess Kate are “really good fun and very good sports,” will also be playing Dick Whittington in panto at Manchester’s Opera House from December 5. Meanwhile, recounting more theatrical superstitions, Jason says: “You'll never hear an actor say ‘Macbeth.’ They always say ‘the Scottish play.’"

View 5 Images Millions of Brits are terrified of Friday the 13th, refuse to walk under ladders and avoid crossing the path of a black cat

‌



UK’s top five superstitions

Broken mirrors - said to bring 7 years of bad luck, as ancient cultures believed it would damage or trap the soul. Walking under a ladder - due to safety risk and association with execution Opening an umbrella indoors - due to safety concerns and thought to be disrespectful to God The groom seeing the bride on the wedding day before the ceremony - stems from arranged marriages. Putting new shoes on the table - shoes were once placed on tables after a death, so seen as tempting fate

*Source: YouGov

*Lloyds Insurance ‘Don’t Bank on Luck’ campaign, in partnership with comedian Jason Manford explores the nation’s superstitions this Friday 13th. The campaign highlights the importance of being prepared for the unexpected, reminding homeowners that, while a little luck never hurts, it’s always better to be protected than to leave things to chance. News.title: Strictly's Craig Revel Horwood: 'I've been living in a caravan for 18 months'
News.content:
All Strictly judge Craig Revel Horwood wants for Christmas is a house to celebrate in. The ’Mr Nasty’ of the glitterball says: “I've been living in a caravan for the last year and a half, because my house isn't ready. I can only fit three people in it comfortably. Hopefully, my house is going to be ready - at least the dining room - because I have invited people over for Christmas Day.”

Engaged to horticulturalist Jonathan Myring, Craig, 61, has been living in temporary accommodation while renovating a historic £2million, seven-bed mansion in King's Cliffe, Northamptonshire, which he bought in 2021. He says: “People have been so generous with me over the time that I've been renovating my property. They've invited me into their homes.”

Making a few additions to his Christmas list, he continues: “A removal service to help me move into my home. I'd love someone to buy me a tennis court, that'd be nice, but that's not on the cards anytime soon.”

Once settled into his house, he wants to repay people’s hospitality, saying: “For people that haven't got a home or are struggling to find somewhere to go for Christmas, I always say, ‘please come to my house’.” Craig, who basked in 40 degree heat during the festivities until he moved to the UK from his native Australia, aged 23, says: “All our chocolates and stockings melted.”

‌



View 5 Images Craig Revel Horwood and Jonathan Myring pictured at their new home in Northamptonshire. (Image: Oliver Dixon/REX/Shutterstock)

But one constant in his life - and that of the nation - for the last 22 years in the countdown to Christmas has been the BBC’s Strictly Come Dancing. The only original judge remaining on the show, he says: “Like panto, Strictly is home for me at Christmas. It’s like the ritual of putting the Christmas tree up, isn't it? It's that thing. When Strictly does start, it feels like, ‘oh wow, it's going to be Christmas soon.’”

Very much the panto villain of the Strictly family, he says: “I've been in everyone's front living room for 22 years. So people are very familiar with me - whether they love or hate me on the programme. There's something quite homely about that and something comforting.”

Drawing in up to 5 million viewers for its 2026 run, Craig is keen to explain Strictly’s success, saying: “It's won the hearts and minds of the nation.The three-year-olds and the 93-year-olds all love it.” And he sings the praises of the new presenting team, with Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe, and Johannes Radebe taking over from Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.

‌



Keenly defending the new format, which has received some criticism from fans, he says: “I really love the presenters. I think the new series is great, too. I love it. Every year it's completely different for me, because there's different celebrities. And every year someone will say, ‘oh, I don't know who that YouTuber is,’ because they're of another generation.

View 5 Images Craig has been a judge on Strictly since its inception 22 years ago (Image: BBC/Guy Levy)

“But people fall in love with them and celebrate and that's the beauty of it. It's about community. It's about getting people talking, reacting together and giving people a common ground on which to form a conversation.”

Craig is speaking after turning on the Christmas lights in Grey Street, Stalybridge, east Manchester, as part of a community campaign with Fox’s biscuits. He says: “My three times great-grandfather was born here. Ashton-under-Lyne, just next door, is where he started his clog dancing career. He was born in 1840, right round here. He then went to Australia of his own accord, unlike my other great-great-great-grandfather who was a convict.”

‌



Craig discovered his relative’s dodgy past when he appeared on Who Do You Think You Are in 2017 and was told that Moses Horwood had been a petty criminal from England, convicted at the Gloucestershire Assizes and transported to Van Diemen's Land - present day Tasmania - in 1841.

But his Ashton grandfather was Harry. He continues: “My clog dancing grandad was called Harry Shaw. He named his son, who was born in Australia, Harry Shaw as well, so it was Harry Shaw Jr. And it was that Harry that became Australasian clog dancing champion in 1871.”

View 5 Images Craig switches on the Grey Street lights for Fox's biscuits community campaign (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Remarking at how local people have come together to admire the 20,000 strong light display on Grey Street, he says: “Community spirit is a good thing. Christmas can be a very lonely time for some people, so it's nice to try and alleviate that.”

‌



For the past 20 years, Craig has starred in Christmas pantos and he will be playing the vengeful villain, Carabosse, in Sleeping Beauty at the Bristol Hippodrome this year. He says: “I’ve never been lonely, because I do panto. In fact, I'm wishing to be lonely! Two thousand 200 screaming kids a day, just give me at least two hours' respite.”

When he does get a break, he likes to plan. Craig says: “I have two hours between shows every day, I have quite a bit of time in my dressing room to think about what gift I might want to buy someone, so I enjoy that part of it - trying to find something quirky.”

And he thinks about his bucket list, revealing roles he would love to play one day. He says: “Mama Rose from Gypsy. I would love to play her. I would also love to play King George in Hamilton. They told me I was too old. I might have to have some work done. I might have to have Botox before I go for the audition. I got a face-lift because I want to play King George.”

View 5 Images Craig in Stalybridge with the Mirror's Hannah Britt (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



But Craig, whose debut album Revelations, Songs Boys Don't Sing was released in 2024, has no plans to release another record any time soon. He says: “I'm going to wait until I'm 70 to release my next one!”

And, despite his extravagant wishlist, he admits he’s already found a priceless present. He says: “The best gift I've ever been given is the gift of love. When someone says that they love you. Honestly, you don't need anything else.”

*Fox's Biscuits is giving one lucky homeowner the chance of a festive makeover, designed to transform their property into a show-stopping Christmas wonderland. Please see entry details HERE

News.title: Every food item that will contain 'synthetic' ingredient from December 13
News.content:
Every food item that will contain 'synthetic' ingredient from December 13

The new rules will impact food staples such as bread, pasta and cakes

View 3 Images Millions of supermarket products will now require one extra ingredient by law (stock image) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Millions of items in UK supermarkets are about to change based on an upcoming law. Food products, including bread, pasta and cakes, will be required to include one specific 'synthetic' ingredient from December as part of a Government-backed health boost.

‌



‌



The UK Government will legally require certain types of bread, pasta, and baked goods made with wheat flour to be produced or sold in the UK to contain a man-made vitamin called folic acid. The law will include a variety of items in the supermarket.

‌



Under the updated Bread and Flour Regulations, millers and food producers must meet this legal requirement within a matter of weeks. It will become legally required from December 13, 2026.

‌



The decision was made in a bid to help reduce the incidence of neural tube defects (NTDs), such as miscarriages, stillbirths and spina bifida, in pregnancies. NTDs are serious birth defects of the brain, spine, or spinal cord that tend to happen very early in pregnancy, usually within the first four weeks.

Folic acid is the synthetic, man-made form of vitamin B9. Natural alternatives include foods that are rich in folate, such as dark leafy greens, certain fruits and vegetables, as well as sunflower seeds and flaxseed.

View 3 Images UK millers and food producers must meet this legal requirement within a matter of weeks (stock image) (Image: Getty)

‌



What items in the supermarket will be affected by this change?

To check if a specific item contains fortified flour, look at the ingredients list on the packaging. Under labelling rules, folic acid must be listed alongside calcium, iron, niacin, and thiamin inside the brackets following "Wheat Flour".

Breads, rolls, buns, wraps and flatbreads: Standard white bread, half-and-half loaves, and regular brown bread.

Standard white bread, half-and-half loaves, and regular brown bread. Breakfast items: Certain crumpets, English muffins, bagels, croissants, and pancakes that use wheat flour.

Certain crumpets, English muffins, bagels, croissants, and pancakes that use wheat flour. Bagged flour: Standard plain flour, self-raising flour, and strong white bread flour from major mills.

Standard plain flour, self-raising flour, and strong white bread flour from major mills. Baking mixes: Packet cake mixes, pancake mixes, scone mixes, and Yorkshire pudding mixes.

Packet cake mixes, pancake mixes, scone mixes, and Yorkshire pudding mixes. Biscuits: Digestives, rich tea, custard creams, shortbread, and chocolate chip cookies.

Digestives, rich tea, custard creams, shortbread, and chocolate chip cookies. Cakes and pastries: Sponge cakes, muffins, doughnuts, fruit pies, and sausage rolls

Sponge cakes, muffins, doughnuts, fruit pies, and sausage rolls Pasta and noodles. Dried and fresh wheat pasta, spaghetti, and wheat-based noodles.

Dried and fresh wheat pasta, spaghetti, and wheat-based noodles. Sauces and thickeners. Gravy granules, packet sauces, and tinned or packet soups that use wheat flour as a thickening agent.

Gravy granules, packet sauces, and tinned or packet soups that use wheat flour as a thickening agent. Frozen and chilled savoury foods. Ready meals, battered or breaded fish and poultry, pies, pasties, and frozen pizzas

‌



Many fortified items are already on UK supermarket shelves today, ahead of the legal December deadline. Because mills and manufacturers are updating recipes and packaging at different speeds, supermarket shelves currently hold a mix of fortified and unfortified stock. After December 13, all newly produced non-wholemeal wheat flour products must comply

‌



View 3 Images Items like bread, biscuits, pasta and cakes will need a minimum amount of folic acid added (stock)

Will I be able to tell the difference?

Folic acid is completely colourless, odourless, and flavourless, and it is added in microscopic amounts. Under UK regulations, millers add only 0.250 milligrams (250 micrograms) of folic acid per 100 grams of non-wholemeal wheat flour.

‌



That is equal to roughly one-quarter of a grain of salt spread across an entire bag of flour. With this in mind, it is a trace amount that ends up in your food.

The NHS recommends 200 micrograms of folate per day for adults. Eating two slices of fortified toast provides roughly half of your baseline daily requirement.

‌



What foods will be exempt from the mandate?

The legislation specifically excludes certain flours and products, meaning they will not be required to contain added folic acid:
