The company, listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker NVDA, is a major supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence systems and accelerated computing.

World.title: Zoning: Atiku violating North-South arrangement he agreed to, says SGF
World.content:
George Akume

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, has accused the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar of going against the North-South rotational presidency arrangement he was party to, saying the North must wait until 2031.

Akume spoke on Thursday in Abuja while receiving a delegation of the Miyetti Allah Fulaku Yesoyeso, led by its National President, Alhaji Abubakar Suleiman.

In a statement by his Special Adviser, Media and Publicity, Yomi Odunuga, the SGF recalled that the agreement was brokered in 1999 at a Kaduna meeting of governors-elect of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, held under the late Chief Solomon Lar, with the late Adamu Ciroma as deputy party chairman.

The understanding provided for eight years of presidential power in the South, followed by eight years in the North.

“I was surprised that Atiku, who was in that meeting, and agreed, is now running for president after Buhari did eight years from the north. This is not the time for the north, the north will come in to contest in 2031,” Akume said.

He said the arrangement had been largely observed through successive administrations, up to the emergence of President Bola Tinubu.

“Obasanjo did eight years, Yar’adu’a took over, unfortunately he died, Jonathan took over and did almost six years. After Jonathan, Buhari from the north did eight years. Bola Ahmed Tinubu took over from Buhari. He has just done four years, therefore he has four years left,” he said.

The SGF warned against disrupting the understanding for personal gain. “Let’s not make any mistake. Don’t do anything that will destroy this country, because we will suffer more. Personal ambition should not destroy our country. Wait for your turn,” he said.

Drawing on his own opposition to the Third Term agenda, Akume urged political actors to be patient. He said that in 2031 the North would be well placed to field any qualified candidate of its choice.

He praised the association for mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election, and assured its members that the President was committed to consolidating on ongoing infrastructure projects.

Earlier, Suleiman reaffirmed the association’s support for the President and commended him for creating the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development. He described it as a significant milestone in addressing the problems facing pastoral communities.

He disclosed that the association had started mobilising in Kaduna, Yobe and Borno, and was using technology and professionals in ranching and information technology to reach members in rural communities.

In a separate engagement, Akume told a delegation of the Northern Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) Chairmen, led by Rev. Joseph Hayab, that the Tinubu administration was committed to equal belonging for all Nigerians, irrespective of religion or ethnicity.

He said competence, capacity and the ability to deliver results, rather than religious or tribal considerations, guided appointments. He cited the religious and ethnic mix of the Federal Executive Council as evidence.

Hayab had pledged the Church’s prayers and support for the administration, and said his team would help communicate the government’s achievements to Nigerians. He said the Church would use the December and January religious celebrations to sensitise its members.

Akume also met promoters of the Renewed Hope Electric Transportation Initiative (RHETI), a private-sector plan to deploy affordable electric mass transit across the six geo-political zones.

The meeting followed a September 16 letter to his office signed by the initiator of RHETI, Dr. Madisca Achile. Akume said the proposal stood out because it did not ask for money from the federal budget.

He told the promoters that the endorsement was not yet an approval. “Good intentions do not move buses. Electricity moves them. Maintenance keeps them on the road. Sound management keeps fares within reach and passengers safe,” he said.

He demanded clear answers on power supply and charging infrastructure, standards and safety, how fares would be kept affordable, and the role of state governments hosting pilot routes.

Akume said a team from his office, working under the Permanent Secretary, Political and Economic Affairs, had been constituted to work with the promoters. He said he expected an implementable framework covering pilot cities, timelines, funding and measurable outcomes.

Eaiwr, Achile said the initiative would add value to the President’s agenda. “We are doing this without asking a kobo from the Federal Government,” he said.

World.title: ‎$1 trillion economy: Nigeria needs double-digit growth, massive investments – Soludo
World.content:
‎… Says Tinubu rescued economy from collapse, but 4% growth insufficient to fight poverty

‎–Urges FG to consider connecting Onitsha Onitsha coastal highway, port infrastructure around Onne.

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎

‎ABUJA– THE Governor of Anambra State and former Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has cautioned that Nigeria’s goal of becoming a $1 trillion economy will remain out of reach unless the country records double-digit economic growth and attracts substantially greater investment from both government and the private sector.

‎

‎The Governor said that while President Bola Tinubu’s administration had successfully pulled the economy back from the brink of collapse and restored some stability, the current growth rate of about four per cent was far too low to drive rapid industrialisation, meaningfully reduce poverty, or create enough jobs for the country’s fast-growing population.

‎

‎He therefore advocated a new phase of bold economic transformation, supported by investment of more than 30 per cent of GDP, sustained industrialisation, competitive exchange-rate policies, and reforms that continue beyond electoral cycles

‎

‎This is as the Governor has urged the Federal Government to consider the potential economic benefits of connecting Onitsha to the coastal highway and the port infrastructure around Onne.

‎

‎Prof. Soludo stated the above on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the presentation of a book titled “Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: The Past, The Present, The Future”, written by a member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Abdulmumini Jibrin Kofa, at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

‎

‎Speaking on the theme, “Speeding Up and Building to Last,” Soludo observed that Nigeria had forfeited considerable time in its economic development journey, and emphasised the need to pursue structural transformation with unprecedented urgency.

‎

‎According to him, the country could not afford another cycle of ambitious economic plans that failed to produce sustained growth, particularly with its population projected to reach about 400 million within the next three decades.

‎

‎He said: “The administration has done very well, rescued the economy. As I previously described it, the economy when this government came in was like a dead horse that was still standing.

‎

‎”It sprayed some oxygen to it. Growth has begun to come back, and we are now on the right trajectory. But acceleration, speed and building to last become important considerations going forward.”

‎

‎The Anambra State Governor contended that the country’s current economic growth, though an improvement over previous years, was insufficient to meet its development aspirations.

‎

‎He said: “Four per cent growth rate for the economy so far is an improvement over the recent past, but very moderate growth for the requirement for significant poverty reduction or accelerated transformation.

‎

‎”Such growth that will be required to be able to have a $1 trillion economy in the next few years will require this economy growing at a minimum of double digit.

‎

‎”And to grow at double digit, you require huge investments in excess of 30 per cent of GDP. Currently, we are doing about 17-point-something per cent”, he explained.

‎

‎Soludo said the challenge was particularly urgent because Nigeria’s population was expanding rapidly, with approximately 70 per cent of its citizens aged 30 years and below.

‎

‎He warned that millions of young Nigerians would require employment, education, healthcare, housing and other essential services in the coming decades.

‎

‎”We have lost time and must now run at the speed of 1,000 kilometres per hour if we want to leapfrog, catch up and surpass our peers in this increasingly competitive and disruptive world.

‎

‎”The current foundations by this administration are in the right direction. The road ahead towards structural transformation will require dozens more disruptive but progressive agendas”, he declared.

‎

‎He noted that the manufacturing sector had remained largely stagnant, accounting for about eight per cent of GDP over the past 56 years.

‎

‎”There is a major missing link. Nigeria transited from the primary to the tertiary services sector.

‎

‎”Our economic diversification and transformation have happened with a missing middle. There is a middle that is missing, which is the secondary sector.

‎

‎”Bypassing the secondary sector under a phenomenon of premature deindustrialisation and incomplete industrialisation, the share of manufacturing has remained flat at about eight per cent for the last 56 years, since 1970.

‎

‎”The manufacturing sector is still less than 10 per cent, and that is where the jobs are for the 400 million Nigerians coming. They need manufacturing jobs.

‎

‎”Industrialisation must happen if we are to have a sustainable economy that creates jobs and widespread prosperity”, Soludo said.

‎

‎He also stressed the importance of a deliberate exchange rate strategy in promoting export-led industrialisation, saying Nigeria had historically undermined its productive capacity by maintaining an overvalued currency.

‎

‎The former CBN governor commended Tinubu for confronting longstanding distortions in the foreign exchange market, arguing that a competitive real effective exchange rate was essential to improving Nigeria’s international competitiveness.

‎

‎He recalled resisting pressure from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to revalue the naira during his tenure at the Central Bank, explaining that his administration deliberately pursued a competitive exchange rate policy.

‎

‎According to him, this strategy, alongside banking consolidation and the accumulation of substantial external reserves, helped Nigeria withstand the 2008 global financial crisis.

‎

‎”Having an overvalued real effective exchange rate and expecting industrial competitiveness was one of Nigeria’s greatest mistakes on the road to transformation.

‎

‎”During my time at the Central Bank, I resisted the IMF advice to revalue the naira. We targeted a real effective exchange rate undervaluation.

‎

‎”There can be no sustained diversification and competitiveness of the economy without an exchange rate strategy”, he said.

‎

‎Soludo argued that the administration’s exchange rate reforms had contributed to improvements in non-oil exports, foreign reserves and capital inflows.

‎

‎The governor said the country’s limited fiscal capacity reinforced the need for stronger revenue mobilisation, private investment and a development strategy capable of attracting substantial capital.

‎

‎Turning to infrastructure, Soludo commended the Tinubu administration’s major transport projects, particularly the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, which he said could help unlock new economic corridors and connect emerging industrial centres.

‎

‎He advocated the deliberate integration of major Nigerian cities, including Lagos, Onitsha, Port Harcourt, Ibadan and Kano, into interconnected engines of industrial and commercial growth.

‎

‎He particularly urged the Federal Government to consider the potential economic benefits of connecting Onitsha to the coastal highway and the port infrastructure around Onne.

‎

‎According to him, such connectivity could dramatically improve access to maritime trade for manufacturers and traders in the South-East.

‎

‎Soludo also called for greater attention to demographic changes, technological disruption, climate change and rapid urbanisation in the formulation of long-term development policies.

‎

‎On the political sustainability of reforms, Soludo cautioned against abandoning long-term development programmes in pursuit of short-term electoral popularity.

‎

‎With the 2027 general elections approaching, he said political leaders must resist the temptation to sacrifice economic reforms for immediate political advantage.

‎

‎Soludo argued that the challenge of sustaining development programmes was particularly pronounced in multiparty democracies operating short electoral cycles.

‎

‎He said Nigeria must find a way to reconcile political competition with a shared commitment to long-term economic transformation.

‎

‎Soludo also challenged Nigerians to demonstrate greater confidence in locally manufactured products, arguing that consumer preferences could play a significant role in industrial revival.

‎

‎He said a nationwide commitment to purchasing Nigerian products would stimulate domestic production, attract investment and generate millions of employment opportunities.

‎

‎”Imagine for a moment if all Nigerians only eat and wear made-in-Nigeria products. Imagine the millions of jobs and the foreign direct investment that will relocate to exploit the Nigerian market”, he said.

‎

‎President Tinubu was represented at the event by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, while other dignitaries included the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, ministers, lawmakers and senior government officials.

‎

World.title: NDC threatens legal action over Imo billboard fees, LGA elections
World.content:
By Chinonso Alozie

OWERRI — The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Imo State has threatened legal action over what it described as excessive campaign billboard fees imposed by the state government, while challenging the legality of the local government elections scheduled for Saturday, November 14.

The party’s Director of Legal Services, Eze Eluchie, disclosed this while speaking to journalists in Owerri on Thursday, accusing the Imo State Signage and Advertising Agency (ISAA) of imposing prohibitive  rates that could restrict opposition parties’ political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Eluchie said the party had submitted a Freedom of Information (FOI) request to the General Manager of ISAA, seeking information and evidence of payments made by political parties for campaign billboards and other s.

According to him, the request is intended to establish whether the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has complied with the agency’s  rates for the numerous billboards and campaign posters displayed across the state.

He said, “With a view to challenging the obnoxious, undemocratic, offensive and prohibitive  rates levied on political parties in the course of the 2027 general elections by ISAA, a Request for Information under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) was earlier sent to the General Manager of ISAA, demanding proof of payment by any political party of the signage and  rates for political campaigns.

“Amongst other things, the request will reveal if indeed the ruling party in the state, the APC, did indeed pay for the multiple billboards and campaign posters they have littered all over the state.”

Eluchie said the NDC would consider approaching the courts if it emerged that the APC had failed to pay the prescribed rates for its campaign s.

“The National Democratic Congress (NDC) intends to challenge this obnoxious practice via litigation, in the event that it is established that the adverts being placed by the APC have not been paid for in line with the rates demanded by the ISAA,” he said.

He argued that the rates imposed by the agency infringed on constitutionally guaranteed freedoms of expression and association, as well as citizens’ rights to participate in the governance of their state.

He called for a level playing field for all political parties, saying it was necessary to safeguard democracy in Imo State.

On the November 14 local government elections, the NDC legal director questioned the legality of the exercise, alleging that the state government had failed to conduct elections following the expiration of the tenure of the local government council executive committees in September 2026.

He claimed that rather than conduct fresh elections, the governor appointed Development Area Governors (DAGs) to oversee local government affairs.

According to him, the arrangement had continued and raised questions about the constitutional basis of the forthcoming elections.

“What Imo State Independent Electoral Commission (ISIEC) appears to be planning is indeed a coronation of selected persons as chairmen and councillors and not a democratic election as envisaged by Section 7 of the Nigerian Constitution,” he alleged.

Eluchie maintained that anyone who emerged from the November 14 exercise would have gained access to the offices of chairmen and councillors in the state’s 27 local government areas and 305 electoral wards through a process he considered inconsistent with the Constitution.

He consequently called on the Federal Government to ensure that funds due to the 27 local government councils were not released to individuals who might emerge from the election.

“We therefore urge the Federal Government to ensure that all funds due to the 27 local government councils of Imo State are not in any way handed over to these characters who emerge from this charade on November 14.

“It is our position that all such funds be placed in interest-yielding accounts with the Central Bank of Nigeria, to be released to the said 27 LGAs at any time when proper democratic elections to elect chairmen and councillors take place,” he said.

World.title: US withdraws from FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The United States has withdrawn its men’s Under-17 team from the FIFA World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns after a State Department advisory warned Americans to reconsider travel because of the risk of armed conflict.

In a letter to players seen by Reuters, US Soccer said it had cancelled the team’s pre-tournament camp and participation “in light of current circumstances”. The federation cited the State Department’s Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar, updated last month, as well as related directives for embassy staff and their families.

The advisory referred to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, and warned that hostilities could escalate. US Soccer said it would notify players’ clubs and asked players not to comment publicly until FIFA announced the withdrawal.

The 48-team tournament is scheduled to run from November 19 to December 13. The United States had been due to open against Montenegro on November 21, before facing Chile and Algeria in Group J.

FIFA told Reuters it had been informed of the decision and would follow the tournament regulations. The governing body said its security assessments remained unchanged and that no new developments had affected the security situation around the tournament.

FIFA added that it remained in contact with relevant authorities and looked forward to the tournament, noting that Qatar had hosted several international events in recent months.

The United States reached the round of 32 at last year’s edition, also held in Qatar. The country is set to host the tournament annually through 2029.

World.title: Customs intercepts 15,375 litres of petrol in Kwara, warns smugglers
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), through its Operation Whirlwind, has intercepted 15,375 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at N15.37 million, at various border communities along the Niger-Kwara axis.

The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Mahmood Bello Ishidi, disclosed this on Wednesday during a public auction of the seized petroleum products at the Kwara Area Command headquarters of the NCS in Ilorin.

He warned petroleum smugglers that the Service would intensify enforcement operations to curb the illegal movement and diversion of petroleum products across the country’s borders.

The seizure, involving 615 jerrycans of 25 litres each, was recorded during intelligence-led operations targeting smuggling networks and illegal diversion of petroleum products across strategic border locations in Kwara State.

Ishidi, who spoke on behalf of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, identified Kaiama, Shiya, Kenu, Boriya, Luma, Baruten, Ilesha-Baruba, Taberu and Salla-Gwanara as some of the locations where the products were intercepted.

He said the seizures, with a combined Duty Paid Value of N15,375,000, demonstrated the commitment of the Customs Service to protecting Nigeria’s economic interests and preventing the illegal movement of petroleum products across the country’s borders.

Describing petroleum smuggling as economic sabotage, Ishidi warned that the illegal trade undermined government revenue, disrupted domestic supply chains and contributed to artificial scarcity and increased prices of petroleum products.

“Beyond depriving the nation of critical revenue, it distorts the supply chain, leading to scarcity and inflated costs that unfairly burden honest Nigerians,” he said.

He further warned that petroleum smuggling strengthened organised criminal networks, weakened border security and posed wider threats to national security.

The National Coordinator pledged to strengthen intelligence gathering, inter-agency collaboration, operational supervision and enforcement strategies to consolidate the achievements of Operation Whirlwind.

“As the newly appointed National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, I reaffirm my unwavering commitment to providing purposeful and strategic leadership, enhancing operational effectiveness, and consolidating on the gains and achievements already recorded by the operation,” he stated.

Ishidi commended the Comptroller-General of Customs and the management of the Service for their support, while acknowledging the contributions of the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to the fight against petroleum smuggling.

He also praised the Acting Controller of the Kwara Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Najeem Akanmu Ogundeyi, and officers of Operation Whirlwind in the Niger-Kwara axis for their professionalism and dedication.

The Customs chief called on residents of border communities to support security agencies by providing credible and timely information about suspicious movements and activities.

“The fight against smuggling is a collective responsibility, and your support remains indispensable in protecting the nation’s economic stability,” he said.

Earlier, the Acting Area Controller of the Kwara Command, Deputy Comptroller Najeem Akanmu Ogundeyi, stressed the importance of sustained cooperation among security agencies and other stakeholders in tackling smuggling and related economic crimes.

Ogundeyi, who welcomed Ishidi, representatives of sister security agencies, stakeholders and journalists to the Command’s headquarters in Ilorin, described inter-agency collaboration as a major factor in achieving national security and economic objectives.

He commended the sister security agencies for their longstanding partnership with the Customs Service, noting that their presence at the event despite the short notice demonstrated their commitment to shared national interests.

World.title: Judge Tinubu, Chinda by records, not promises — Dike
World.content:
By Daniel Abia

PORT HARCOURT — A member of the Tinubu/Chinda Presidential Campaign Publicity Subcommittee, Princewill Dike, has urged Nigerians to assess President Bola Tinubu and the Rivers State All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Kingsley Chinda, based on their records in public service rather than campaign promises ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Dike spoke to journalists shortly after the inauguration of the APC Presidential/Rivers Rainbow Coalition Candidates Campaign Council in Port Harcourt on Thursday, saying the records of both leaders reflected years of experience in public administration, legislative development and service delivery.

He said Tinubu’s contributions to national development predated his emergence as President in 2023, recalling his eight-year tenure as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007.

Dike particularly cited Tinubu’s role in expanding Lagos State’s internally generated revenue, establishing the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) and laying the foundation for the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) transportation system.

The APC chieftain also highlighted the President’s economic reform initiatives, including the removal of petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), enactment of the Electricity Act 2023 and ongoing tax reforms.

He further mentioned major infrastructure projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Super Highway and the rehabilitation and construction of federal roads, saying they were designed to improve connectivity, trade and economic activities across the country.

On education, Dike described the NELFUND student loan scheme as an important intervention aimed at expanding access to tertiary education by providing financial assistance to eligible students.

He said the Electricity Act 2023 had created opportunities for states to establish and regulate their own electricity markets, while the administration’s tax reforms were intended to simplify taxation, improve revenue generation and strengthen the country’s fiscal system.

While acknowledging the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians, particularly inflation, high transportation costs and the rising cost of living, Dike maintained that the administration’s policies and infrastructure investments should also be assessed against their intended long-term benefits.

On the Rivers APC governorship candidate, Chinda, Dike highlighted his legislative experience, particularly his emergence as Minority Leader of the 10th House of Representatives and his previous chairmanship of the House Committee on Public Accounts.

He said Chinda’s positions in the National Assembly had provided him with opportunities to contribute to legislative oversight, public accountability and the promotion of responsible management of public resources.

Dike also highlighted Chinda’s constituency interventions in Obio/Akpor Federal Constituency, including the provision of a Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) Computer-Based Test Centre to improve students’ access to examination facilities.

Other projects and interventions he mentioned included road construction, classroom development, youth empowerment programmes, skills acquisition and information and communication technology training.

He further cited Chinda’s free medical outreaches as part of his contributions to healthcare delivery and community development, noting that the initiatives had provided medical assistance to residents, particularly those with limited access to healthcare services.

Dike also said Chinda had championed legislative motions and interventions addressing electricity supply, insecurity, environmental protection, infrastructure development, public accountability and improved workers’ wages.

He urged Nigerians, particularly the people of Rivers State, to examine the records, policies and contributions of political leaders before making informed choices in the 2027 elections.

He added that the publicity committee would continue to provide information on the programmes, policies and achievements of the APC candidates to enable voters to make informed decisions.

The APC chieftain also commended the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, for what he described as his grassroots mobilisation, political sagacity and leadership qualities, which he said had strengthened political engagement and coordination in Rivers State.

Dike assured Wike that members of the committee would not disappoint him, expressing appreciation for the confidence reposed in them through their appointment to serve in the APC Presidential Campaign Council of the Rivers Rainbow Coalition.

He pledged that the campaign council would justify the trust by remaining committed, united and focused on communicating the achievements, programmes and political vision of President Tinubu and the Rivers APC governorship candidate ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: 2027: INEC begins deploying non-sensitive materials
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has begun deploying non-sensitive materials to the zones as it prepares for the 2027 general election.

Acting Chairman of the commission, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at a benchmarking meeting with a delegation of Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission IEBC.

“Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now,” Gumus said.

She said the commission had completed nine of its scheduled activities and was preparing for the next phase.

“We are preparing for the election next year and we have activities lined up. So far, we have been able to complete nine activities and we are still preparing for the next level of activities,” she said.

Gumus said the commission’s leadership had just concluded a tour of the country’s six zones to assess their level of preparedness.

“The purpose was to go round the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, their challenges and what to do. We concluded last week and we can see from our tour that we are really going towards the election proper,” she said.

On Permanent Voter Cards PVCs, the acting chairman said production had been completed and distribution to the states was well advanced.

“As of today, we can say that PVCs have been produced and the first, second batches, most of the states have received them. Their PVC collection is ongoing. All those who are supposed to be the voters are supposed to receive their PVCs, and if they don’t have them, it is also another challenge,” Gumus said.

She added that capacity building was under way for staff at the headquarters and in the states, and that the procurement and deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS devices were also ongoing.

On diaspora voting, Gumus said the commission could not proceed for now because the law did not provide for it.

“Here, because we go by the law, in our electoral law, it is not included there, so we cannot go on for the diaspora voting for now until we amend the electoral law,” she said.

The acting chairman said the commission had arranged for its directors to hold an interactive session with the Kenyan team and present papers on the work of their departments.

Leading the delegation, the Kenyan High Commissioner to Nigeria, Isaac Parashina, said the IEBC team was in Nigeria to benchmark ahead of Kenya’s general election in August 2027.

He said the team was studying how Nigeria handled its diaspora population and special voting groups, as Kenya sought to widen voting rights for citizens living abroad.

“Currently we have about 12 of them who voted in the last general election, but there is intention to expand to around, I think, 26,” Parashina said, referring to the countries where Kenyans abroad vote.

He said the expansion was a constitutional requirement backed by Kenyan court rulings, and would be enforced progressively.

Parashina said Nigeria’s election, which he noted would come in two rounds, would be closely watched across Africa. “Everyone is looking at what Nigeria will do because it is the biggest democracy in Africa. The success of Nigeria remains a great success to Kenya and indeed to the continent,” he added.

The High Commissioner thanked INEC for receiving the team despite a tight schedule and wished the commission success.

World.title: APC-PCC condemns attack on NDC Lagos town hall, demands swift arrests
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has condemned the attack on the town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC in Lagos, and called on security agencies to arrest and punish those behind it.

The council also condemned other violent attacks at political gatherings in Edo, Cross River and Gombe states.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the Spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, said the attacks were targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines.

“We have observed the recent spate of violent attacks at political gatherings in parts of the country. The reported attacks in Edo, Cross River, and Gombe, and other violence targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines are condemnable,” the statement said.

On the Lagos incident, it said: “Our campaign strongly condemns the disruption of today’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC in Lagos.”

The council urged political parties, politicians and their supporters to show restraint as the campaign season advances.

“As we proceed with the electioneering campaign, political parties, politicians, and supporters must restrain themselves and avoid acts that could create needless crisis and public disorder.

“We call on the security agencies to be more responsive and alert in preventing political violence of any type and ensure instigators and perpetrators are apprehended and punished in accordance with the law.

“Political parties and candidates are enjoined to campaign on issues that uplift the lives of Nigerians and not to instigate violence at political events,” it said.

World.title: Four UNN Students Die At Off-Campus Party, Varsity Declares Three Days of Mourning
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), has declared three days of mourning following the death of four students at an off-campus party in Nsukka, Enugu State.

The university also dismissed reports that seven students died in the incident, clarifying that four students were confirmed dead, while six others were receiving medical attention at different hospitals.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, disclosed this while addressing journalists on the incident, which occurred on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

He said 10 students were involved in the gathering organised to celebrate one of their friends who had completed his final-year examinations.

According to him, the students reportedly consumed substances suspected to be alcohol and drugs, after which four of them died. The six survivors are currently at various stages of recuperation in hospital.

Describing the incident as “a death too many”, Ortuanya announced three days of mourning, during which all social and academic activities in the university would be suspended.

“Within these three days, all social and academic activities will be suspended in the university,” he said.

The vice-chancellor also announced the suspension of a town hall meeting earlier scheduled between the university community and the Enugu State Governor, thanking the governor for his understanding.

He expressed condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of the deceased students, saying the university community shared in their grief.

Ortuanya also dismissed reports that all the students involved in the incident were from the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, clarifying that they came from different departments.

He reiterated the university’s ban on sign-out celebrations, warning students against activities that could endanger their lives.

He said graduation should be a period of reflection rather than an occasion for reckless celebrations.

The vice-chancellor added that the university was cooperating with security agencies to establish the actual circumstances surrounding the deaths.

World.title: Kwara PDP Guber Candidate, Kawu, Unveils 3-Point Vision, Promises to Establish N100bn Security Fund
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Kwara State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for the 2027 general election, Mr Sulaimon Bolakale Kawu, has unveiled a three-point vision to refix the state for economic prosperity and good governance.

He pledged to establish a N100 billion Security Trust Fund to tackle insecurity, alongside a series of economic interventions aimed at improving the living conditions of residents if elected governor in 2027.

Kawu made the pledge in Ilorin Thursday while unveiling his three-point vision of secure, productive and prosperity titled, ‘My Covenant with Kwara’ manifesto.

He also promised a 13th-month salary for civil servants and N4 billion monthly hardship allowance scheme for teachers serving in underserved, rural and hard-to-reach communities.

He said his proposed security fund would support intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, provide better equipment for security agencies and establish a coordinated system for identifying and responding promptly to security threats.

He described security as the foundation of development, lamenting the devastating impact of insecurity on communities, particularly in Kwara North and South Senatorial Districts.

Recalling his recent visits to rural communities, Kawu said the experience had strengthened his resolve to seek the governorship and address the challenges confronting residents.

“My recent visits to rural communities in the state geared me to more actions because at Kaiama, I saw despair written all over Kwarans. These are the people who lost their loved ones to insecurity,” he said.

He explained that his ambition was driven by the need to provide purposeful leadership rather than personal political considerations.

He added that his experience as a retired senior civil servant and former Director of the Rural Electrification Agency had prepared him for the task of governance.

He stated that the manifesto represents a comprehensive development blueprint designed to ensure that government policies translate into tangible benefits for residents across the state.

“This manifesto is about what government must do, how it must do it and, most importantly, who must benefit from it. It demonstrates that, as governor, I will hit the ground running from day one.

“I assure you that I do not seek to enter government with an empty head or mind, as we have seen in recent times,” he said.

Kawu, who described the document as a covenant with the people, said his proposed administration would be anchored on security, economic productivity and infrastructure development.

On economic empowerment, he promised to establish a N9.6 billion revolving loan scheme for traders and another N9.6 billion single-digit interest loan facility for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

He said the initiative would provide businesses with access to affordable financing, stimulate economic activities, create employment opportunities and strengthen the capacity of local entrepreneurs.

On infrastructure, the PDP candidate pledged to prioritise projects capable of supporting businesses, attracting investments, creating jobs and improving the livelihoods of residents.

He also promised to give qualified and competent indigenous contractors consideration in the award and execution of government projects, provided they meet the required standards.

“This policy will help retain government investments within Kwara, strengthen local businesses, create jobs, develop local capacity and ensure that our people directly benefit from the economic activities generated by government projects,” he said.

In the education sector, Kawu promised to rehabilitate dilapidated schools, improve learning environments, provide teaching and learning materials and strengthen teachers’ welfare.

He said rural schools and communities would receive special attention to address the additional challenges confronting children in underserved areas.

“Every child deserves access to quality education irrespective of where they are born or the economic circumstances of their parents,” he stated.

The former REA director maintained that his proposed government would focus on ensuring equal opportunities for residents, regardless of their locations or economic circumstances.

He said the manifesto was informed by his conviction that Kwara could achieve more through strategic planning, competent administration, transparency and people-oriented policies.

Kawu added that his years of experience in public service, particularly in project conception, design, implementation and monitoring would guide his approach to governance.

The PDP gubernatorial candidate expressed confidence that the proposed blueprint would prevent a situation where an incoming administration assumes office without a clear development plan, insisting that every sector and community in the state had been considered in the document.

Also speaking, the Director General of the PDP Campaign Council, Prince Omar Bolaji Gambari, said: “Today is not just the unveiling of a document. It is the day that will be remembered as a full declaration of intent and the day when our candidate laid out his vision, his plan, his policies and programmes that will benefit every Kwara.

“This manifesto is not a document

of empty promises. It is a solemn compact. It is a blueprint forged from thousands of hours of listening to the citizens, the workers, the students, opinion leaders, community associations, traders, market women, entrepreneurs and many others, all over Kwara.

“Engineer Kawu’s manifesto embodies the hopes and aspirations of our people, as well as the struggles we refuse to accept any longer.

“Across every corner of this great state, the message has been clear. Our people are saying no to insecurity, no to banditry, no to unemployment, and no to.despair”

Gambari therefore urged the people of the state to rally round the party’s governorship candidate and other candidates so as to enable the party implement the manifesto for the overall development of the state come 2027.

World.title: COP31: Nigerian Bank of Agriculture Seeks Climate Funding to Support Agricultural Adaptation Projects
World.content:
Chiemelie Eze in Antalya, Türkiye

The Bank of Agriculture (BOA) has called for increased climate financing from developed countries to support agricultural adaptation projects in Nigeria and across Africa, while unveiling plans to deploy electric cargo tricycles and solar-powered irrigation systems to improve farmers’ productivity.

The BOA Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Ayo Sotinrin, made the call yesterday at the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, where he said Nigeria and other African countries needed more financial support to address the effects of climate change on agriculture.

Sotinrin said the bank was exploring partnerships and financing arrangements to introduce practical climate adaptation solutions, particularly in agricultural transportation and irrigation.

He disclosed that the bank was exploring the introduction of electric cargo tricycles capable of transporting 2,000kg of agricultural produce from farms to farm gates in one trip, compared with fossil-fuel-powered two-wheelers that carry about 50kg.

He said, “We are introducing electric cargo tricycles that can actually move 2,000kg from farms to the farm gate at once, rather than the fossil-fuel-powered two-wheelers that move only 50kg.”

He also said the bank was looking to expand solar-powered irrigation through one-to-five-horsepower pumps and subsurface pumps to enable farmers cultivate their land at least three times annually.

“We’ve also looked at how we increase the adoption of solar irrigation across board, using one-to-five-horsepower pumps or subsurface pumps to ensure that farmers can actually farm three times a year at the minimum.

“This would further increase our productivity by at least 300 per cent,” he said.

According to him, the initiatives would help transform agricultural production and mitigate some of the challenges posed by climate change.

On the outcomes expected from COP31, he called for renewed commitments by world leaders, expressing concern that previous climate financing promises had not been fulfilled.

He said existing commitments were insufficient to keep global warming below 2.5 degrees Celsius, let alone achieve the 2-degree and 1.5-degree targets.

“My takeaway from COP is refreshed commitments from world leaders. Also, the fact that we are all coming to a realisation that all the promises that were made were not kept.

“We are talking about those commitments that were made; they will not even get us below 2.5 degrees, let alone getting to 2 degrees or below 2 degrees, which is 1.5 degrees, where we want to be,” he said.

He called for increased funding from the Global North to Africa through blended financing instruments, including grants, commercial capital and development finance, to support climate adaptation projects.

“We need more capital. The capital stack needs to be explored, especially from the Global North to Africa, where we have different types of blended instruments, including grants, commercial and developmental capital going into adaptation solutions in Nigeria and Africa at large.

“So those are the sorts of things that we are happy have been discussed at COP31 today,” he said.

On access to agricultural financing, Sotinrin said the bank had digitised many of its processes and systems to make funding more accessible to farmers.

He, however, explained that the bank had moved away from providing microcredit directly to individual farmers, preferring to channel loans through cooperatives, farmer aggregation companies, microfinance banks and commercial banks.

He said, “We’ve stopped giving microcredits to individual farmers unless they come under an umbrella of a medium cooperative or a smaller cooperative, or a farmer aggregation company, or even through asset-based financial institutions such as microfinance banks and commercial banks that we blend capital with.”

He explained that the approach was necessary to ensure effective loan recovery, noting that the bank’s 110 branches could not independently manage lending to two million individual farmers.

“If you tell me to finance individual farmers, it’s very difficult because one of the things that scale, and there’s no way the Bank of Agriculture, with 110 branches, can actually finance two million farmers individually and be able to recover those monies.

“And if we don’t recover those monies, we erode our shareholder capital and we’re back to square one,” he said.

World.title: Praises as Abiodun Breaks Ground for 450 Hectares Industrial Park
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta

Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, yesterday performed the groundbreaking of 450 hectares First Lee Group Industrial Park located near Sagamu Interchange on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The governor was joined at the ceremony by the Minister of State for Trade for Industry Trade and Investment, Senator John Enoh, Commissioner for Finance and Chied Economic Adviser to the Ogun State, Hon Dapo Okubadejo, traditional rulers, Ambassador Plenipotentiary of the Peoples Republic of China Yu Dunhai, community leaders and other stakeholders.

Speaking at the ceremony, Abiodun said the industrial park would create opportunities for small and medium-scale enterprises to support the operations of the factory and other factories, with its proposed manufacturing components ranging from personal and home care products to footwear, leather processing, food processing, bakery production, and recycling, demonstrating the breadth of opportunities the project presents.

According to the governor, the establishment of the Aspira flagship factory, the S.F.M. footwear, and all other products in the park, would promote the utilization of locally available raw materials.

Abiodun said he is particularly encouraged by the project’s emphasis on value addition, backward integration, and environmental sustainability, while the proposed integration of leather and footwear accessory production will strengthen local manufacturing linkages.

The governor said beyond the factories and physical infrastructure, the greatest value of the investment will ultimately be measured by its impact on the people.

He noted that the project’s blueprint projects the generation of up to 15,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities upon completion and operation, which is very significant for young people, skilled professionals, artisans, technicians, and the surrounding community.

He said the project is expected to prioritize local employment, deliberate skills development, technology transfer, and the nurturing of home-grown managerial and technical talents.

He noted that people must not merely live around the industrial development but must participate meaningfully in its opportunities and benefits, and assured the leadership of the Lee Group that the Ogun State government remains committed to providing the necessary institutional support and investor-friendly environment for the project to succeed.

Abiodun urged local entrepreneurs, small and medium-scale enterprises, suppliers, and service providers to position themselves to benefit from the extensive business opportunities the project will create, saying Ogun State remains steadfast in its determination to consolidate its position as a leading destination for industrial investment.

He noted that with his administration about six months away from exiting, the Lee Group’s industrial park is a significant vote of confidence and a strong affirmation of the confidence investors continue to repose in the state, as well as a testament to the success of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope economic transformation agenda.

In his remark, the Chairman, Lee Group of Companies, Sheau Fung Lee, said the groundbreaking of the group’s industrial park continues a commitment to Nigeria that began in 1962, when his grandfather established an enamelware factory in Port Harcourt.

He said the firm has grown from that modest beginning into a multi-sector conglomerate that now employs approximately 26,000 workers in Nigeria, with footwear production of around 2 million pairs a day, a tannery in Kano, packaging, bread, bottled water, laundry detergents and personal care products.

He said more than six decades and three generations of leadership, the group has shared in Nigeria’s good times and difficult years, noting that the journey has not been easy but they continue to believe in Nigeria’s future and to invest in its economy.

In his remark, the Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, Sen. John Enoh, commended the Abiodun for his vision and outstanding leadership, which have turned Ogun State into the industrial capital of Nigeria.

Enoh, who said investors is now trooping to Ogun State noted that if there was no good leadership and suitable environment, investors wouldn’t have come to invest in the state.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of

The minister recalled that a project of such nature had been stalled for several years, but it took Abiodun to get it to where it is today.

He also noted that the governor still embarked on laudable projects in spite of just a few months to the end of governor his administration.

He said, “I think that the judgment of history will be fair to this man. It will be fair to him. That’s what leadership is about. Leadership is not about the end of a tenure, not about the next election, it’s about the future generation. Let me thank you, sir. Let me thank you for your leadership.”

He thanked the Lee Group for believing in Nigeria and for the confidence reposed in the country, noting that the group has spent several years in the country and stayed on through tough moments when other companies left the shores of the country.

He appealed to royal fathers and community leaders, who he described as custodians of the project, to give it all the support it requires, stressing that they are ultimately the greatest beneficiaries.

He expressed hope that as the Lee Group and the industrial park grow in leaps and bounds, the fortunes and circumstances of the community will also grow in leaps and bounds.

World.title: Glo Magic Bundles: When Data Becomes A Gift And Connectivity A Reward
World.content:
By Onyema Ohaegbu

What if purchasing data ceased to be a straightforward commercial transaction and became an experience in which certainty meets pleasant surprise, guaranteed value encounters unexpected generosity, and connectivity yields more than the customer originally bargained for? What if every subscription carried within it the possibility of an additional reward, transforming the familiar business of buying data into an invitation to enjoy more, achieve more and experience more?

This is the refreshing proposition behind Globacom’s Magic Data Bundles, an innovative offering that is redefining the conversation around affordability, customer value and digital inclusion in Nigeria’s telecommunications landscape.

At a time when data has become the indispensable currency of contemporary civilisation, powering conversations, commerce, education, entertainment, healthcare, governance and virtually every expression of human enterprise, the importance of affordable and dependable internet access cannot be overstated. Data is no longer merely a technological commodity; it is the invisible infrastructure upon which modern society conducts its business, exchanges knowledge, creates opportunities and sustains relationships.

Globacom’s Magic Bundles recognise this changing reality and respond with a proposition whose central philosophy is beautifully uncomplicated: customers should receive what they pay for, and enjoy something extra.

The ingenuity of the offering resides in its distinctive two-component architecture: a guaranteed main data allocation, complemented by an additional Magic Bonus, automatically credited following a successful subscription.

Available at two accessible price points, ₦1,600 and ₦3,500, the proposition introduces an appealing dimension of reward into the customer’s data experience.

At ₦1,600, subscribers receive a guaranteed 2.5GB main data allocation, alongside a Magic Bonus ranging from 500MB to 7.5GB, bringing the potential total allocation to between 3GB and 10GB. At ₦3,500, customers are assured of 8GB, with an additional bonus ranging from 1GB to 12GB, potentially raising their total data entitlement to between 9GB and 20GB.

Herein lies the magic: the guaranteed allocation remains sacrosanct, while the additional reward introduces an element of delightful anticipation. The bonus is automatically assigned by Globacom’s system, meaning that customers may receive different additional allocations on different subscriptions. The maximum reward is not guaranteed, but an additional bonus accompanies every qualifying purchase.

It is an ingenious marriage of commercial assurance and rewarding spontaneity.

Beyond the attractive numbers, the strategic significance of Magic Bundles becomes even more compelling when examined against the diverse demands of Nigeria’s increasingly data-dependent population.

For entrepreneurs, small businesses, retailers and corporate organisations, data is the oxygen of commercial productivity. It facilitates digital marketing, electronic payments, customer engagement, virtual meetings, inventory management and the expanding universe of online commerce.

Additional data can translate into more opportunities to transact, communicate and serve customers without immediately returning to the marketplace for another subscription.

For students, researchers, lecturers and educational institutions, connectivity is a gateway to intellectual discovery. Online libraries, virtual classrooms, academic journals, educational videos and collaborative learning platforms have made internet access indispensable to contemporary education. More data means greater latitude to explore knowledge and participate in the expanding global classroom.

In healthcare, connectivity strengthens the possibilities of teleconsultation, medical research, professional collaboration, digital health records and public-health communication. Government institutions equally depend on data for administrative efficiency, citizen engagement, electronic services, policy communication and the expanding architecture of digital governance.

Within Nigerian homes, the benefits assume an altogether intimate character. Parents connect with children, families maintain relationships across geographical distances, young people explore opportunities, and households access entertainment, information and digital services.

From video streaming and social networking to online banking and professional development, Magic Bundles offer additional breathing space for everyday digital living.

Another attractive dimension is the flexibility of the proposition. Customers can purchase through the Glo Café application or by dialling *312#. The bundles are also shareable and giftable, subject to applicable conditions, while rollover provisions apply under Globacom’s prevailing policies.

Customers can monitor their main and bonus balances through Glo Café, the web self-service platform or *323#.

Viewed against competing industry propositions, Glo’s offering deserves particular attention.

Other operators provide daily, weekly and monthly subscriptions, promotional bonuses and specialised data packages. However, Magic Bundles distinguish themselves through the deliberate combination of a guaranteed allocation and an automatically awarded additional data reward within one subscription proposition.

This differentiation, rather than any sweeping dismissal of competitors’ offerings, constitutes the product’s strongest competitive argument.

The television commercial currently running on Arise TV provides an important communications platform for this proposition. Its significance extends beyond announcing another data package.

It places the product within a broader conversation about value, aspiration and the changing expectations of Nigerian telecommunications consumers. Arise TV’s national visibility and business-oriented audience offer a useful environment for communicating the proposition to decision-makers, professionals, entrepreneurs and ordinary subscribers alike.

Ultimately, Glo Magic Bundles embodies an attractive commercial philosophy: connectivity should empower, affordability should deliver substance, and customer loyalty should encounter tangible rewards.

In an industry where operators compete for attention, subscription and market share, Globacom is making a persuasive statement by placing additional customer value at the centre of its proposition.

It is a philosophy that resonates naturally with the company’s overarching campaign declaration, Never Settle for Less. Indeed, why should customers settle for the ordinary when their subscriptions can deliver something extra?

With Magic Bundles, Globacom is inviting Nigerians to experience data differently: not simply as megabytes purchased, but as opportunities multiplied, possibilities enlarged and everyday digital experiences enriched.

Because when connectivity comes with a little more magic, the possibilities become considerably greater.

*Pastor Onyema Ohaegbu, Telecoms Enthusiast, writes in from Abuja

World.title: World Toilet Day: Nasarawa to Provide Massive Mobile Toilets
World.content:
Igbawase Ukumba in lafia

The Nasarawa State Government has said it is providing massive mobile toilets in public facilities in its renewed effort to end open defecation in the state.

The state Commissioner for Environment, Solid Minerals and Mining, Princess Margaret Elayo, disclosed this on Thursday in Lafia while briefing journalists at an event to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day.

THISDAY reports that November 19 is set aside every year to celebrate World Toilet Day.

According to her, “The state government has keyed into the plans of the Federal Government to end open defecation by 2030.

​”The word toilet sounds simple and funny to some people, but a toilet is life. A toilet is dignity. A toilet is health. A toilet is safety. A toilet is a peaceful space.

​”Imagine a child who cannot go to school because there is no toilet in the school. Imagine a woman who must wait until nightfall, risking her safety, just to ease herself in a bush.

“Imagine a community where human waste flows in the same water they drink, cook with, and bathe with.

“That is the reality for millions of people across the globe, even here in Nigeria, and Nasarawa State,” she said.

Elayo noted that the Governor Abdullahi Sule-led administration in the state is committed to ending open defecation, providing clean and accessible toilets for all and protecting the environment and water from contamination.

She said that the mobile toilets would be deployed in high-traffic areas including markets, motor parks, schools, and other public places where residents often lack access to toilet facilities.

The commissioner said the initiative is not only about providing toilets, but also about protecting public health, preventing diseases like cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea, and restoring dignity to residents.

Elayo further warned that the state government would no longer tolerate open defecation, noting that the state sanitation law makes it mandatory for every household to have a functional toilet.

The commissioner further disclosed that the government would immediately construct modern toilets at Shinge cattle market and On the Move Park in Lafia due to a recent discovery that those important places do not have toilet facilities.

She, therefore, called on members of the public to make use of the facilities when provided, keep them clean, and support the government’s effort to make Nasarawa open defecation-free.

World.title: Tinubu, APC Leadership Head to Jos for North-central Rally
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will lead the national leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to Jos on Saturday for the North-central leg of the party’s presidential campaign rally.

The rally, scheduled for the Zaria Road Stadium, is expected to attract senior party officials, including Vice-President Kashim Shettima, First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas, APC National Chairman Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, governors and members of the party’s National Working Committee (NWC).

Ahead of the event, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang called for a peaceful atmosphere during the visit, while the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Mr. Samuel Jatau, said preparations had been concluded for security, traffic management, logistics and emergency response.

In a state wide broadcast, Governor Caleb Mutfwang described the visit as significant for Plateau State, noting the state’s longstanding role in Nigeria’s democratic development.

He called on residents to receive the visiting delegation peacefully and use the occasion to promote unity and democratic engagement.

Mutfwang also highlighted ongoing federal and state interventions in key sectors, including road infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and transportation.

Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Jatau, said preparations for the rally had reached an advanced stage, with arrangements covering venue readiness, traffic management, transportation, crowd control, emergency response and security coordination.

According to him, the committee is working with relevant security and emergency agencies to ensure adequate access control, screening procedures and the safety of participants and residents during the event.

Jatau appealed to residents, motorists and business operators to cooperate with authorities, particularly in areas where temporary traffic adjustments may be required.

He said the visit presents an opportunity for Plateau State to host the nation’s political leadership and further strengthen engagement between the state and the Federal Government.

The APC chieftain also pointed to ongoing federal interventions in the state, including road projects, plans for the installation of surveillance cameras and the approval for the recruitment and training of 1,000 forest guards aimed at strengthening community security.

Both Mutfwang and Jatau expressed confidence that the rally would be conducted peacefully and called on party supporters and members of the public to participate responsibly.

The event is expected to attract APC stakeholders and supporters from across Plateau State and other parts of the North-central region.

World.title: From Lab to Market: TETFund to Turn 500 Nigerian Innovations into Businesses, Jobs
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

Nigeria is moving to end decades of research gathering dust on library shelves, as the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) prepares to push between 400 and 500 home-grown innovations from laboratories into the marketplace.

The innovations will headline the 2026 TETFund National Research Fair and Exhibition, scheduled for November 24 to 27 at the Abuja Chamber of Commerce and Industry Trade Fair Complex, along Airport Road.

The Chairman of the Organising Committee, Mr. Umar Bindir, said the fair is no longer about showcasing academic brilliance, but about creating businesses, jobs and wealth from Nigerian knowledge.

“We are actually working. And the working is what will now change Nigeria from a country that is energized with knowledge but consuming other people’s products to a country that is energized technically, that is actually feeding other countries,” Bindir said.

Speaking during the committee’s meeting on Thursday in Abuja, Bindir disclosed that between 4,000 and 5,000 applications were received from universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, research institutions and private inventors across the country.

Only innovations that had attained a reasonable level of development and demonstrated practical, commercial potential survived the screening.

“We have gotten an average of 350 to 400 nationwide from everywhere,” he said. “We deliberately avoided projects that were still at the preliminary research stage or lacked the functionality required for practical application.”

The selected innovations cut across agriculture, healthcare, sanitation, housing, clothing and other critical sectors where Bindir said Nigerian research could directly change the country’s course.

“So that we can be able to bring this on the table for Nigerians to see the power of knowledge and the outputs of our knowledge institutions that can help our country to change its course to become great,” he said.

To ensure the ideas do not die after exhibition, TETFund is bringing the full business ecosystem to the fair: banks, investors, industries, business development experts and intellectual property lawyers.

IP experts in patents, trademarks and industrial designs will offer free services to help innovators protect their inventions, while business experts will guide them on formation, standardisation, registration and scaling for local and international markets.

Bindir said the missing link for most Nigerian inventors was not talent, but funding and business expertise.

“Inventors often possessed technical ideas but lacked the financial resources and business expertise to commercialise them,” he said. “We are bringing together banks, investors, industries and relevant government agencies to bridge the gap.”

The strategy is already yielding results. From the previous edition, between 30 and 40 innovations have reached an advanced stage and are undergoing commercialisation-related activities, while many others are in what Bindir called “halfway houses” — needing further support in business development and product standardisation.

“Yes, we have like 30 to 40 of these matured ones that are actually ongoing. But there are many also that have gone to what we call halfway houses,” he said.

He said TETFund’s partnership with Innovat8 Hub is working to push those intermediate innovations closer to the market.

The previous fair introduced a deal-room that matched inventors directly with financiers. The 2026 edition will go further, involving the business community directly in planning so that Nigerian businesses do not merely observe, but identify, adopt and fund technologies with commercial potential.

The fair will also feature an international symposium starting November 25, with participants from China, India, Canada and Japan, as well as the World Bank, UNESCO and the African Development Bank (AfDB). A Japanese expert is expected to deliver the keynote address.

Bindir said the international component would expose Nigerian innovators to global standards, open opportunities for knowledge exchange and showcase the country’s research capabilities to the world.

He said ministers, state governors, heads of government institutions and other stakeholders have been invited to attend and explore the innovations on display.

He commended TETFund’s Executive Secretary, Mr. Sonny Echono, for providing the administrative and logistical support that has minimised the challenges of organising the national event.

World.title: Why Fernando Da Cruz remains safe at Kaizer Chiefs
World.content:
Fernando Da Cruz remains under pressure despite Kaizer Chiefs’ victory over Siwelele this past weekend.

However, the FIFA international break gives the French coach valuable time to reset, assess his squad and welcome back players who have been sidelined through injury.

Khanyisa Mayo and Langelihle Phili are expected to feature for Amakhosi in the coming weeks after recovering from their respective injuries. Their return will give Da Cruz more attacking options as he looks to get Chiefs’ league campaign back on track.



In the Carling Knockout Cup, Chiefs have looked impressive and secured a place in the semi-finals, where they will face Mamelodi Sundowns.

Da Cruz backed by Chiefs management

Despite the Soweto Derby defeat to Orlando Pirates, Da Cruz continues to enjoy the backing of the Chiefs management.

A potential defeat in the Carling Knockout Cup semi-final against Mamelodi Sundowns is not expected to affect his position, with the club understood to remain confident in his work.

With December fast approaching, Chiefs will also be looking to strengthen their squad during the upcoming transfer window, potentially giving the current coach further resources to improve the team.

The 1-1 draw against Sundowns earlier this season, coupled with a promising first-half performance against Pirates in the Soweto Derby, has offered glimpses of what Da Cruz is trying to build at Naturena.

Since taking charge, Chiefs have lost just two matches. Even in those defeats, Amakhosi showed periods of encouraging football, suggesting that there are positives for the Frenchman to build on.



The coming weeks could therefore prove important for Da Cruz as he looks to turn those promising Chiefs performances into consistent results.

Can Chiefs win the Carling KO?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs coaching change rumour gets a reaction
World.content:
Mngqithi became a free agent after his shock exit from Young Africans SC. The tenure ended after just three months in East Africans.

With Fernando Da Cruz enduring a slow start at Kaizer Chiefs, Mngqithi’s departure from Dar es Salaam quickly sparked rumours of joining the Soweto giants.

Meanwhile, Mngqithi’s super agent, Mike Makaab, has said there is no substance to the reports.



“It’s not true [that Chiefs want to bring in Mngqithi as head coach], and it’s unfair to the current technical staff. You know rumours like this can cause a lot of problems,” Makaab told FARPost.

“Coach Manqoba is a top football coach with great experience, and there will always be rumours, but I can tell you that no formal approach has been made by Kaizer Chiefs.”

The speculation comes amid a difficult start to the 2026/27 campaign for Amakhosi under Fernando Da Cruz.



Chiefs have already missed out on the MTN8 and suffered an early elimination from the CAF Confederation Cup preliminary rounds. Those setbacks have frustrated sections of the club’s supporters, with some calling for the French coach to be dismissed.

Despite the growing pressure, sporting director Kaizer Motaung Jr has publicly reaffirmed the club’s backing for Da Cruz.

Makaab’s comments now offer a clear response to suggestions that Mngqithi could be brought in to replace the current coach.



MNGQITHI’S IMPRESSIVE RECORD BEFORE YOUNG AFRICANS EXIT

Mngqithi’s short spell in Tanzania began positively. He guided Young Africans to the Community Shield in August 2026, beating bitter rivals Simba SC 1-0.

The 55-year-old oversaw 13 matches across all competitions, winning 10, drawing two and losing just once. His team scored 29 goals and conceded seven.

Before moving to East Africa, Mngqithi had returned to Golden Arrows during the previous campaign, guiding the KwaZulu-Natal side to a top-eight finish in the Betway Premiership.



He also enjoyed a trophy-laden spell at Mamelodi Sundowns, where he served in several technical roles over more than a decade. Notably, he was part of Pitso Mosimane’s technical team when the Brazilians won the CAF Champions League in 2016.

World.title: Popular South African retailer’s shares plunge
World.content:
A Woolworths store at Rosebank Mall in Johannesburg. Image: Nick-D / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0; cropped and resized).

Woolworths shares plunged 8.52% on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Wednesday, 11 November, after the retailer reported barely any growth in group sales.

The share price closed at R37.78, marking its steepest one-day fall since March 2020.

The company’s latest trading update showed that group turnover and concession sales rose just 0.2% during the 19 weeks ended 8 November 2026. On a constant-currency basis, growth was 0.1%.



Why did Woolworths shares fall?

Woolworths said high fuel prices, inflation and interest rates continued to limit consumer spending in South Africa and Australia. Shoppers were increasingly favouring essential purchases and promotional offers.

Its South African business recorded turnover and concession sales growth of 1.6%, but results varied considerably between divisions.

Food sales barely grow at existing stores

Woolworths Food reported total sales growth of 1.9%. However, sales at comparable stores increased by only 0.1%, despite average price movement of 3%.



Comparable-store figures help show how existing outlets are performing without the effect of newly opened stores. The gap between sales growth and price movement suggests pressure on the quantity of goods sold, although the trading update does not provide a separate measure of volumes.

Food trading space also increased by 2.7% compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.

Country Road Group struggles in Australia

Woolworths’ Australian Country Road Group recorded a 9.5% drop in sales, including an 8.2% decline at comparable stores.



The retailer pointed to weak consumer sentiment, reduced foot traffic and widespread discounting across Australia’s retail sector.

Uncertainty has also emerged over the group’s relationship with David Jones, the Australian department store chain placed into administration and receivership. Several Country Road brands operate concessions inside David Jones stores.

Woolworths said it was assessing what the development means for their continued trading relationship.



Where is Woolworths still growing?

Online food sales increased by 24.1%, contributing 9.1% of South African food sales during the period.

The retailer has been expanding Woolies Dash, including a dedicated fulfilment centre in Cape Town intended to improve delivery speed and product availability.

Woolworths also completed its acquisition of food manufacturer in2food on 5 November. The company expects the transaction to support food profit margins as it manages higher fuel costs and the expansion of online sales.



Elsewhere, homeware sales rose 6.4% and beauty sales increased 3.1%, although the broader Fashion, Beauty and Home division recorded a 0.3% decline.

The retailer’s financial services business also faced pressure, with its annualised impairment rate rising from 6.7% to 7.3% for the four months ended October.

What happens next for Woolworths?

Group CEO Sam Ngumeni, who succeeded Roy Bagattini after a leadership change this year, is overseeing the retailer’s strategic plans.



Woolworths expects to issue another trading update in mid-January 2027, after the festive shopping period. That announcement should provide a clearer indication of whether sales have improved in South Africa and Australia.

Can Woolworths reverse its sales slowdown?

World.title: Majestic South African town rocked by sudden rise in crime
World.content:
Howick, a town of 42 749 residents, is a bucket-list destination for many South Africans.

Yet today the tourism town is experiencing a sharp rise in crime.

Crime rose 45% in one quarter

As the South African Police Service (SAPS) prepares to release second-quarter data, the first quarter still has unexplored data.



Among the countless pages of spreadsheets is a fascinating discovery: between April and June, crime in Howick rose by 45% compared to the same period last year.

Howick is one of South Africa’s most majestic towns.

The small town is home to Howick Falls on the Umgeni River that descends 95 metres down cliffs.

The town also has plenty of history, being the location where former President and anti-apartheid hero Nelson Mandela was arrested in 1962.

But this history and natural beauty are taking a backseat as Howick falls victim to a rise in crime.

Most police precincts in KwaZulu-Natal’s uMgungundlovu District Municipality experienced a rise in crime, which means Howick is only part of a much larger and more worrying trend.



Yet what makes Howick most notable is that the small town experienced the highest percentage rise in crime.

Very few police districts in the country have encountered such a sharp rise in crime.

But there’s good news for Howick: despite a 45% rise in the first quarter, it still hasn’t returned to its 2019 peak. If this trend continues, that could change when SAPS releases its full-year statistics.

The crimes on the rise in Howick

Nearly every crime category in Howick increased in the first quarter.

But the crimes with the sharpest increase include theft and commercial crime.
