World.title: Prague Adds Special Trams and More Metro Services for Letná Demonstration
World.content:
Prague is preparing for a large demonstration at Letná on Sunday, November 15, with additional public transport services planned to accommodate the expected crowds.

The city will increase the frequency of trains on all three metro lines and introduce two temporary tram routes, numbered 40 and 44, to help transport participants to and from the demonstration.



Organized by the Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek) movement, the event is expected to attract thousands of people from across the Czech Republic. Organizers are anticipating a record turnout.

The additional tram services are intended to ease pressure on regular routes, particularly around Letná and neighbouring districts.

Metro services will run more frequently between 11:30 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Sunday.

Tram 40 will operate from approximately noon until 7 p.m., running every five minutes. It will connect Letná with all three metro lines, travelling from Palmovka through Florenc, Vltavská, Hradčanská and Dejvická before terminating at Červený Vrch.

Tram 44 will also run at five-minute intervals, but only from noon until approximately 3 p.m. Starting at Špejchar, the route will pass through Strossmayerovo náměstí and Výstaviště towards Nádraží Holešovice. It will then continue around Holešovická tržnice, pass Vltavská and return to Letná.

The second route is intended primarily for passengers arriving on Metro Line C.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Milion chvilek pro demokracii (@milionchvilek)

Despite the additional services, transport authorities warn that overcrowding and delays are likely, particularly at Hradčanská, Vltavská and Nádraží Holešovice stations and on connecting tram routes.

According to Prague 7 authorities, the busiest periods are expected shortly before the demonstration starts and immediately after it ends. The greatest pressure on public transport is anticipated before 2 p.m. and at around 4 p.m.

Tram Disruptions Elsewhere in Prague

Passengers should also expect changes to regular tram services in central Prague.

From approximately 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., trams will be temporarily suspended in the area between Palackého náměstí, Národní divadlo, Jiráskovo náměstí and Myslíkova Street.

Tram lines 5 and 17 will be diverted via Karlovo náměstí during this period.

Road Restrictions and Changes to Letná Ice Rink

Drivers heading towards Letná should also expect traffic restrictions and temporary road closures in the surrounding area. The city recommends avoiding car travel to the demonstration and allowing extra time for journeys.

World.title: James Blunt Announces Prague Concert as Part of European Tour
World.content:
British singer-songwriter James Blunt will return to Prague on March 5, 2027, for a concert at O2 universum.

The performance is part of his Airplane Mode Tour, which will see him travel across Europe in support of his upcoming album.

Best known for international hits including “You’re Beautiful,” “Goodbye My Lover” and “Wisemen,” Blunt last performed in Prague three years ago, when he played at Forum Karlín.



His upcoming show will combine songs from his new record with the tracks that established his international career.

Blunt rose to international fame with his debut album, Back to Bedlam, released in 2004 after he left the British Army. Before pursuing music, he had attended the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst and served in Kosovo.

The debut album became a major commercial success, featuring three of his best-known songs: “You’re Beautiful,” “Goodbye My Lover” and “Wisemen.” It went on to rank among the 20 best-selling albums in UK history and earned Blunt several major industry honours, including Brit Awards and MTV Europe Music Awards, as well as five Grammy nominations.

His second album, All the Lost Souls, followed in 2007 and included “1973,” which topped music charts in more than 20 countries.

Titled Airplane Mode, the new album is scheduled for release on November 6, 2026, through Atlantic Records. The 12-track record has been introduced by the single “Tastes Like Summer,” followed by “Weight of It All,” a song addressing the pressures of modern life.

The European tour will run through February, March and April 2027, with Prague among its scheduled stops.

Tickets for the March 5 concert are available through Ticketportal and Ticketmaster.

The concert is organised by Charmenko Czechia.

World.title: Prague to Mark 37 Years Since Velvet Revolution With 160 Events
World.content:
Prague will mark the 37th anniversary of the Velvet Revolution on November 17 with more than 160 events taking place along Národní Street as part of this year’s Korzo Národní celebrations.

Organised by the association Díky, že můžem, the annual event will bring together concerts, theatre performances, public discussions, exhibitions and activities exploring democracy and freedom.



This year’s programme carries the motto “Let’s Not Stand on the Sidelines. Democracy Relies on Each of Us.” The organisers say the message reflects growing concerns about declining trust in society and the challenges facing democratic institutions.

One of the central moments of the celebrations will take place at 17:11, when the traditional song Modlitba pro Martu (A Prayer for Marta) will be performed from the balcony of the Metro Palace.

This year, the performance will form the finale of a theatrical production titled DŮM VŠECH (House for All), which begins at 17:00. Visitors unable to gather directly beneath the balcony will be able to watch the performance on large screens along Národní Street or through a live broadcast.

The day’s programme will begin earlier, with the popular Velvet Brunch, a charity event held directly on the street between 10:00 and 13:00. At 13:00, members of the Czech Radio Children’s Choir will perform the national anthem.

Other events include live podcasts, musical performances and discussions on social issues. Among the scheduled speakers and performers are Markéta Foukalová, Martin Brunner, Václav Kopta and Vietnamese community representative Quang Luong.

Havel, the Vietnamese community and Věra Čáslavská

Several parts of this year’s celebrations will focus on important anniversaries.

The programme will commemorate the 90th anniversary of the birth of Václav Havel, the playwright and former Czech president.

His legacy will be explored through the traditional Václav Havel’s Living Room, titled “For Vašek”, at Platýz Palace. Actors including Vojtěch Vondráček and Taťjana Medvecká will read texts dedicated to Havel.

Another anniversary concerns the Vietnamese community, which marks 70 years in the Czech Republic. The programme will include Lost in Translation, a discussion bringing together three generations of Vietnamese residents to examine questions of identity, belonging and life between cultures.

The celebrations will also remember gymnast Věra Čáslavská, ten years after her death. Her life and the relationship between sport and politics will be examined through a special lecture aboard the Educational Tram and a live recording of the Outsider podcast.

World.title: FlixBus Launches Direct Route Between Prague Florenc and Airport
World.content:
FlixBus will introduce a direct bus connection between Prague’s Florenc Central Bus Station and Václav Havel Airport on November 12.

The new service will operate 13 times a day in each direction, with the journey taking approximately 30 minutes.

The first bus will leave Florenc at 3:40 a.m., while the last departure is scheduled for 10:40 p.m. From the airport, services will run between 4:15 a.m. and 11:15 p.m.



Ticket prices will depend on demand and departure times. According to the FlixBus website, the usual fare is around CZK 79, including the booking fee. The cheapest tickets start at CZK 69, while some departures cost up to CZK 89.

The company expects the route to attract business travellers in particular. Passengers will have access to Wi-Fi and power outlets on board.

BusAir joins the competition

FlixBus is not the only company expanding its airport connections. A separate private service, operating under the name BusAir, began running between Prague’s city centre and the airport in late October.

Operated by UBUS, the service offers eight departures a day in each direction, with buses running every two hours. A ticket costs CZK 125 and remains valid for 24 hours.

Due to renovation work on the ceiling at Prague Main Railway Station and traffic restrictions on the city’s main arterial road, BusAir currently departs from Opletalova Street, close to the station. On the way to the airport, it also stops at Hradčanská metro station on Line A.

Both new services are entering a market where the main competitor is the Airport Express, operated by Prague Public Transit Company (DPP).

The Airport Express runs more frequently than the private alternatives, with departures every 20 to 30 minutes during the day and hourly services overnight. It is also currently the only direct bus connection between the city centre and airport operating throughout the night.

Standard Prague public transport tickets are not valid on the service. A single adult ticket costs CZK 200, although passengers can get a lower fare when purchasing it together with a train ticket.

World.title: Říčany Named Czech Republic’s Best Place to Live for Ninth Year
World.content:
Říčany has been named the best municipality in the Czech Republic for quality of life for the ninth consecutive year, retaining its position at the top of a nationwide ranking ahead of Prague.

The Central Bohemian town, located southeast of the capital, again led the Quality of Life Index compiled by the Obce v datech project. The ranking assesses 206 Czech municipalities with extended administrative powers.

At the other end of the table, Orlová in the Karviná District ranked last, while nearby Karviná finished second from bottom.



The geographical divide remains clear: the 14 highest-ranked municipalities are all located within 50 kilometres of Prague or Brno, while many of those at the bottom are found in former industrial and border regions, particularly in the Moravian-Silesian and Ústí nad Labem regions.

There have nevertheless been signs of improvement in parts of the Moravian-Silesian Region. Over the past eight years, Odry, Kopřivnice and Hlučín have each climbed by around 40 places in the ranking.

The picture is less positive in the Ústí nad Labem Region, where only six of the region’s 16 assessed municipalities have improved their position since 2018. Roudnice nad Labem was the only municipality in the region to record a substantial rise.

Pohořelice Makes the Biggest Leap

Pohořelice, in the Brno-Country District, has recorded one of the most striking improvements since the index was introduced in 2018. The town has climbed from 117th place to fifth this year.

Nepomuk, in the Plzeň Region, has made an equally large jump of 112 places and now ranks 24th. Kuřim has moved up 65 positions to 15th, while Mnichovo Hradiště has risen 46 places to 18th.

According to Jan Havránek of AQE Advisors, which developed the project, municipalities do not need to perform at the top in every category to improve their overall ranking.

For around half of the 30 municipalities that have improved the most, the stronger results were linked to a younger population, population growth and, in many cases, longer life expectancy.

The Quality of Life Index evaluates municipalities across several broad areas, including health and the environment, material security and education, and relationships and public services.

World.title: ROCK THE OPERA Returns to Prague for 25th Anniversary Concert
World.content:
Twenty-five years after conductor Friedemann Riehle helped pioneer the symphonic rock concert format in Prague, he is returning to the Czech capital for a special anniversary performance.

ROCK THE OPERA will take place on Sunday, 13 December 2026, at Smetana Hall in Prague’s Municipal House.

The concert will bring together the Prague Philharmonic Orchestra, rock musicians and vocalists for an evening dedicated to some of the biggest songs in rock history.



The anniversary also marks a full-circle moment for Riehle. On 29 October 2001, he promoted and conducted one of the first symphonic rock shows in Prague, combining a symphony orchestra with rock drummers and vocalists to give legendary songs a new sound.

What began as an experiment has developed into a long-running international project. Over the past 25 years, Riehle has conducted more than 100 symphonic rock concerts across Europe, performing everywhere from Iceland to Istanbul and appearing at venues including the Vienna State Opera, Berlin Philharmonie and Athens’ Odeon of Herodes Atticus.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by RONNIE GRACE | ROCK SINGER ⚡️ (@ronniegrace)

For the Prague anniversary concert, Riehle will be joined by Ronnie Romero, one of the best-known voices in contemporary rock. Romero has performed with several internationally recognised rock musicians and bands and will bring his distinctive vocals to the symphonic arrangements.

The programme will feature music associated with some of rock’s biggest names, including Pink Floyd, Queen, AC/DC, Led Zeppelin and U2.

Alongside Romero, the concert will feature vocalists Lucie Koutniková and Sabina Olijve, guitarist Jiří Rambousek and drummer František Hönig. The Prague Philharmonic Orchestra will perform under the direction of Friedemann Riehle.

Tickets are available via Ticketportal.

World.title: St. Martin’s Day 2026 in Prague: Where to Enjoy Traditional Goose
World.content:
St. Martin’s Day, which Czechs celebrate on November 11, is a holiday of good food and drink. Autumn slowly alternates with winter, and it begins to snow.

In the past, the economic year was ending at this time, and the landowners were preparing a feast for their people as a form of thanks, when they were also paid out their wages.

St. Martin’s Day in restaurants

You can be sure that almost every restaurant around mid-November will be offering its visitors a special St. Martin’s Day menu. What does it feature?

According to a tradition that has lasted for several centuries, geese were always roasted in the autumn, fresh cabbage was processed, and wine or beer was drunk. And today’s restaurants and pubs remain faithful to these basic ingredients.

Typically, you will be served liver pâté as an appetizer, followed by a strong broth with liver dumplings and noodles, which the chefs usually leave to simmer overnight, with the main course being roast goose with red or white cabbage and dumplings.

Where to taste St. Martin’s menu?

Restaurant Salabka (November 6 – 14): Choose from 3 to 5 courses featuring seasonal autumn ingredients and contemporary gastronomy. Available from November 6, alongside the regular autumn tasting menu.

More info here.

Pilsner Urquell Experience: until November 15, here you can find a St. Martin’s Menu for 1,095 Kč including goose liver pâté with cranberries, roast goose leg with red cabbage and Carlsbad dumplings, followed by traditional Czech potato cones with poppy seeds.

More info here.

GARE Restaurants: Celebrate St. Martin’s Day at three GARE Restaurants: La Gare, Les Moules and Pivovar U Supa, each offering its own take on the Czech goose-feast tradition. Highlights include goose pâté, traditional goose kaldoun and confit goose leg with poppy-seed potato dumplings, plums and fermented cabbage.

La Gare serves its festive menu during lunch from November 9–13. Les Moules offers its specialties from November 7 while stocks last, while Pivovar U Supa continues its goose feast until November 15.

La Gare | Les Moules | Pivovar U Supa

Restaurant Masaryčka: Here the highlight is a tender goose leg confit with caraway, served with braised red cabbage, plums and assorted dumplings (499 CZK). Alternatively, guests can enjoy homemade potato lokše filled with pulled goose meat, onion cabbage and apples (359 CZK). To finish on a sweet note, the menu offers apple strudel with vanilla sauce, walnuts, honey and cinnamon crumble (149 CZK).

More info here

Greenhouse – Fairmont Golden Prague

Available for lunch and dinner until November 15, the menu costs 1,480 CZK per person, with individual dishes also available. Guests can enjoy their meal with views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle.

More info here

World.title: All Aboard the Pajama Express: Prague Metro Supports Hospitalised Kids
World.content:
The Prague Metro will host a special pajama-themed journey on Friday, November 13, as part of the Czech Republic’s annual Pajama Day, an initiative supporting families of children undergoing long-term hospital treatment.

For the first time, a dedicated carriage will be reserved for passengers travelling in their pajamas. The special train, known as the Pajama Express, will operate on Metro Line A, with participants invited to board its first carriage at any station along the route.



The journey will begin at Depo Hostivař at 9:13 a.m. and end at Nemocnice Motol, the metro station serving Motol University Hospital. Hospital representatives will welcome participants upon arrival.

The initiative aims to highlight the difficulties faced by children who spend extended periods in hospital, often separated from their usual surroundings, and the importance of having family members close by during treatment.

Several public figures and bloggers are expected to join the journey. Among them will be actress Veronika Arichteva, patron of the project.

Now in its third year, Pajama Day has attracted around 400 registered participants. Schools, businesses, public institutions, theatres, hospitals and individuals across the country have signed up for this year’s edition.

The event is organised by the Ronald McDonald House in the Czech Republic (Dům Ronalda McDonalda Česko), which provides free accommodation for families of seriously ill children at Motol Hospital.

The facility allows parents to stay close to their children throughout lengthy hospital stays, reducing the burden of travelling between the hospital and home.

Passengers wishing to take part in the Prague event do not need to register separately. They simply need to wear their pajamas and board the first carriage of the special train at any station along Line A.

World.title: Budapest Christmas market ranks among world’s top 10 trending festive destinations
World.content:
Budapest’s Advent Bazilika has secured a place among the world’s ten fastest-rising Christmas market destinations for 2026, ranking seventh globally after searches for the popular Hungarian attraction increased by 112% year-on-year.

Budapest outpaces Vienna and Dresden in Christmas market searches

The findings come from new research by travel insurance specialist InsureandGo, which analysed Google search data covering more than 370 Christmas market-related search terms to identify destinations experiencing the biggest growth in online interest.

The ranking comes as the Advent Bazilika prepares to open its doors for the festive season. The Budapest market, which was recently named Europe’s most beautiful, has attracted significantly more search interest than several famous Central European alternatives.

With a 112% increase in searches compared with the same period last year, the Advent Bazilika ranks ahead of Dresden’s famous Striezelmarkt, which recorded a 77% rise, and Vienna’s Rathausplatz Christmas Market, where interest increased by 57%.

Other Central European destinations are also attracting growing attention. Prague’s Old Town Square Christmas Market recorded a particularly impressive 249% increase, placing fourth in the global ranking. The Christmas markets in Olomouc, Czechia, and Poznań, Poland, also made the top ten, with increases of 106% and 104%, respectively.

The figures suggest that travellers are increasingly exploring alternatives to some of Europe’s traditional Christmas market favourites.

Which markets are trending most in 2026?

The research places Lincoln Cathedral Christmas Market in the UK at the top of the global ranking, with searches soaring by 1,833% year-on-year. The event is returning in a smaller, ticketed format after being discontinued in 2023 due to overcrowding concerns. Thessaloniki in Greece comes second, with a 479% increase, while Berlin’s WeihnachtsZauber at Gendarmenmarkt completes the top three with a 311% rise.

Several traditionally popular destinations, meanwhile, have seen declining search interest. Searches for Christmas markets in Paris fell by 42%, Amsterdam by 26%, Brussels by 21% and Nuremberg by 13%. New York City’s Christmas markets also recorded a 70% decrease.

According to Letitia Smith, Head of Communications at InsureandGo, travellers are showing growing interest in lesser-known Christmas market destinations rather than focusing exclusively on the traditional favourites. The company also advises visitors to remain alert in crowded festive attractions, where pickpocketing can be a concern.

The research is based on year-on-year changes in Google search interest rather than actual visitor numbers, meaning the ranking reflects growing online curiosity about these destinations, not necessarily an increase in attendance. The full research is available from InsureandGo.

World.title: Hungarian government to increase minimum wage next year, but most aren’t happy about it
World.content:
Hungary’s government has proposed increasing the national minimum wage and the guaranteed minimum wage from January 2027. However, employers remain opposed to the proposal, meaning negotiations between the government, trade unions and business representatives have yet to produce an agreement.

Tisza government to increase the lowest minimum income

The figures, by 7.5 per cent for the national minimum wage, and 6.5 per cent for the guaranteed minimum wage respectively, were announced following a meeting of the Permanent Consultation Forum of the Competitive Sector and the Government (VKF) on Tuesday.

According to trade union representative Tamás Székely, the proposal would raise the gross monthly minimum wage to approximately HUF 347,000 (EUR 950), while the guaranteed minimum wage would reach around HUF 397,000 (EUR 1,086), writes Klubrádió.

The guaranteed minimum wage applies to employees whose jobs require at least a secondary-level qualification or vocational training. Székely, a board member of the Hungarian Trade Union Confederation (MASZSZ), described the government’s offer as a realistic starting point for a compromise. He suggested that an agreement could be reached relatively soon if employers softened their position.

Take-home pay could rise by more than 10 per cent

Although the proposed gross increase is below 10 per cent, Székely said the rise in employees’ take-home pay could be considerably higher. Planned tax credits for 2027 could mean that the lowest-paid workers see a double-digit increase in their net earnings. He warned, however, that expectations of a double-digit increase in the gross minimum wage were unrealistic given Hungary’s current economic circumstances.

The trade union representative also argued against another multi-year wage agreement. He criticised the previous three-year deal, saying its commitments had not been fulfilled as expected and that it had created significant problems. In his view, an agreement covering only one year would be more appropriate because economic conditions, energy prices and fluctuations in the forint exchange rate make longer-term wage planning particularly uncertain.

Employers remain reluctant to accept the offer

Employers have so far resisted the government’s proposal, despite the negotiating parties reporting some progress in narrowing their differences. Székely urged trade unions to persuade employers that the proposed increases represented an acceptable compromise. He also warned that raising the minimum wage and the guaranteed minimum wage would put pressure on salaries in higher pay brackets, potentially triggering further wage disputes.

The union representative suggested that tensions could intensify if employers offered increases of only zero to 2 per cent to workers earning above the minimum thresholds. Following Tuesday’s talks, the finance minister also confirmed that the parties’ positions had moved significantly closer, but stressed that no agreement had yet been reached.

The government’s stated objective is to ensure a substantial increase in the net minimum wage and guaranteed minimum wage from 1 January 2027. Further negotiations are expected before the parties reach a final decision.

World.title: Pakistan wants to attract more Hungarian tourists: Embassy hosts first tourism promotion event in Budapest
World.content:
Pakistan is looking to attract more Hungarian tourists, with the country’s embassy in Budapest hosting its first dedicated tourism promotion event for Hungary’s travel industry on 10 November. The event brought together representatives of major Hungarian travel agencies and tour operators to introduce them to Pakistan’s diverse attractions, flight connections and travel opportunities.

Titled “Discover Pakistan”, the event was organised by the Embassy of Pakistan in cooperation with Turkish Airlines at the residence of the Pakistani ambassador. Ambassador Asif Hussain Memon opened the programme, followed by a welcome address from the airline’s representative.

From K2 to historic cities: Pakistan’s tourism potential

Pakistan is perhaps best known internationally for its spectacular mountains, particularly K2, the world’s second-highest peak. The country is home to five of the world’s fourteen mountains exceeding 8,000 metres, making it a major destination for mountaineers and trekking enthusiasts.

Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest

However, the embassy’s presentation aimed to show Hungarian travel professionals that Pakistan has much more to offer than high-altitude expeditions.

Shehryar Qaisrani, the embassy’s Trade and Investment Attaché, introduced the country’s varied attractions, including the mountain valleys of Hunza, Skardu and Swat, Lahore’s Mughal architecture, archaeological sites, coastline and culinary traditions.

Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest

The presentation covered several types of tourism, from adventure and trekking to cultural, religious, culinary and coastal holidays, highlighting the potential for a wide range of travel itineraries.

Turkish Airlines explains flight connections

Accessibility was another key topic for the travel professionals attending the event. Turkish Airlines presented its flight connections to Pakistan via Istanbul, explaining transfer times and the options available to passengers during longer stopovers.

These include Touristanbul, a complimentary city tour for eligible transit passengers, as well as accommodation arrangements for longer layovers and lounge facilities at Istanbul Airport.

Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

Hungarian mountaineer shares his Pakistan experiences

One of the highlights of the afternoon was the presentation by Hungarian mountaineer Dávid Klein, who has climbed four of Pakistan’s five eight-thousand-metre peaks without supplementary oxygen.

Having visited Pakistan 14 times, Klein described the country as his second home. However, his presentation focused on much more than mountaineering achievements.

He spoke about the relationships he had built over more than a decade with local porters, guides, drivers and families in northern Pakistan. According to Klein, the hospitality and genuine generosity he has experienced there are among the main reasons he continues to return.

Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest

He also discussed his approach to mountaineering, including his decision to climb without bottled oxygen, and the personal and ethical considerations behind it.

His first-hand experiences offered Hungarian travel professionals a personal perspective on what visitors can expect beyond the country’s famous mountain ranges.

Pakistani food and a prize draw round off the event

The formal programme concluded with a raffle, in which two prizes were awarded: a Turkish Airlines model aircraft and a flight ticket to Pakistan.

Guests then enjoyed a Pakistani lunch and had the opportunity to exchange contacts and discuss potential travel packages for Hungarian customers.

Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest Photo: Embassy of Pakistan in Budapest

The event followed another recent initiative by the Pakistani Embassy to introduce the country’s culture and products to Hungary. In October, it organised Hungary’s first Pakistan Rice Festival, bringing Pakistani basmati rice to the attention of Hungarian chefs and importers.

Through these events, the embassy is seeking to build stronger connections between the two countries while encouraging Hungarians to discover more of what Pakistan has to offer.

World.title: Hungary’s housing market cools as property price growth slows and rents decline
World.content:
Hungary’s housing market is showing clear signs of cooling, with property price growth slowing nationwide and rents recording their sharpest monthly decline in almost six years, according to the latest figures published by property portal ingatlan.com.

Price growth close to stopping

In October, residential property prices rose by just 0.2 per cent month on month across Hungary, while prices in Budapest remained virtually unchanged. Annual price growth slowed from 8.2 per cent in September to 6.9 per cent nationally, its lowest rate in more than two years. In the capital, annual growth fell to 1.8 per cent, the weakest increase since December 2023.

László Balogh, chief economic expert for ingatlan.com, said the previous upward trend had lost momentum, particularly in Budapest, where prices had not increased for three consecutive months. The median asking price per square metre for second-hand homes in the capital was around the same as a year earlier.

Wide differences across Budapest

At the beginning of November, the median asking price for second-hand homes in Budapest stood at HUF 1.4 million (EUR 3,830) per square metre. The most expensive district was the fifth, at almost HUF 2 million, followed by the first at HUF 1.9 million (EUR 5,200) and the twelfth at HUF 1.74 million (EUR 4,760). The cheapest was the twenty-third district, where the median was HUF 940,000 (EUR 2,575).

New-build properties remained considerably more expensive, with a median of HUF 1.72 million (EUR 4,710) per square metre, 4.5 per cent higher than a year earlier. The supply of newly built homes advertised in Budapest increased by 52 per cent year on year.

Outside the capital, second-hand property prices varied significantly. Among county seats with the largest housing markets, Debrecen recorded a median of HUF 1.02 million (EUR 2,790) per square metre, followed by Szeged at HUF 960,000 (EUR 2,630) and Győr at HUF 950,000 (EUR 2,600).

Rents fall despite shrinking supply

The rental market also weakened in October. According to the joint rent index compiled by the Hungarian Central Statistical Office (KSH) and ingatlan.com, rents fell by 1.1 per cent nationally and 1.3 per cent in Budapest compared with September. Similar monthly declines had not been recorded since December 2020.

Despite the fall, rents remained higher than a year earlier, with annual growth slowing to 5.5 per cent nationwide and 5 per cent in the capital.

The median advertised monthly rent in Budapest was HUF 255,000 (EUR 698) at the beginning of November, down from HUF 260,000 (EUR 711) a year earlier. The second district was the most expensive, at HUF 364,000 (EUR 996), while the twenty-third was the cheapest, at HUF 160,000 (EUR 438). Across county seats, the median rent was HUF 185,000 (EUR 506).

There is less property available

The number of available rental properties has also declined. Budapest had 9,331 advertised homes at the beginning of November, 9.4 per cent fewer than a year earlier. In county seats, supply was down 16.9 per cent year on year.

Balogh attributed the softer rental market partly to weaker returns on property investments and tenants’ limited purchasing power. Government-backed home-buying loans may also have encouraged some renters to purchase their own homes, easing rental demand.

World.title: Hungary to ratify Istanbul Convention as government unveils women’s rights reforms
World.content:
Hungary’s government will seek parliamentary approval to ratify the Istanbul Convention as part of a wide-ranging package of measures aimed at tackling violence against women and improving women’s rights, Prime Minister Péter Magyar has announced.

Hungarian government to ratify the Istanbul Convention

In a video posted on Facebook on Thursday, Péter Magyar said the government wanted to address what he described as years of neglect, during which women experiencing abuse had often been left without adequate support.

He said the measures were intended to protect Hungarian women’s safety and dignity, adding that the state must prevent violence, protect victims and hold perpetrators accountable.

The proposed package includes stricter restraining orders and the introduction of a separate criminal offence covering the misuse of intimate images. The government also plans to strengthen protections for sexual autonomy, making clear that sexual activity must take place with the voluntary consent of both parties.

Tougher penalties and stronger protection for victims

Victims of domestic violence would receive special treatment during criminal proceedings, Magyar said. He cited expert estimates that around 50 women die each year in Hungary as a result of intimate-partner violence.

The government also plans to change the so-called foetal heartbeat regulation, introduced under the previous administration. Under the proposed amendment, women would be able to decide whether to listen to the foetal heartbeat after receiving appropriate medical information and assistance.

Other measures include making emergency contraception available without a prescription, improving support for pregnant women and launching initiatives to tackle period poverty by helping women and girls who cannot afford essential menstrual products.

A long-delayed international commitment

Magyar described the planned ratification of the Istanbul Convention as one of the most important elements of the package and a long-standing obligation for Hungary.

The Council of Europe treaty aims to prevent and combat violence against women and domestic violence. It requires signatory states to take action to protect victims, prosecute perpetrators and prevent abuse. It also recognises violence against women as a human rights violation and a form of discrimination.

Hungary signed the convention in 2014 under the previous Fidesz government but never ratified it. In May 2020, parliament adopted a resolution rejecting ratification, following an initiative by the Christian Democratic People’s Party (KDNP).

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

PM Magyar changed his mind

Supporters of the resolution argued that Hungary’s existing legal framework already provided sufficient protection, while also criticising what they described as the treaty’s approach to gender issues and migration.

The prime minister’s latest announcement shows a big change in his previously stated position. In a February 2026 interview, Magyar said he did not believe ratifying the Istanbul Convention alone would improve women’s lives, although he promised that his government would examine the issue and consult experts and the public.

Magyar said the new package had been developed with specialists and through wider public dialogue. The Justice Ministry also held talks with women’s rights organisations in October on restraining orders and measures to combat violence against women.

World.title: Canadian lobster brings a taste of Nova Scotia to Budapest at annual business dinner
World.content:
The Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary, chaired by Nicholas Sarvari, held its 32nd Annual Canadian Lobster Dinner on Saturday, 7 November, bringing together around 200 guests from the Hungarian and international business communities at the InterContinental Budapest.

The Chamber’s largest annual event welcomed company leaders, decision-makers and business partners, including Ambassador Judith Gelbman and guest of honour Dr Judit Zolnay.

As the name suggests, the highlight of the evening was a special dinner featuring whole lobsters brought from Nova Scotia, giving guests a taste of Canada’s Atlantic coast in the Hungarian capital.

Nicholas Sarvari. Photo: Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary Dr Judit Zolnay. Photo: Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary

Live entertainment, auction and raffle

Beyond the dinner itself, the programme included live music and entertainment, exhibitors, a silent auction and a raffle. Guests had the opportunity to browse the auction items throughout the evening, while Renault provided a dedicated shuttle service for attendees.

The event offered an opportunity for Chamber members, business partners and other guests to meet representatives of different companies and industries, reconnect with familiar faces and establish new professional contacts.

With a more relaxed atmosphere than a traditional business meeting, the dinner allowed guests to continue earlier conversations and build new connections over food and entertainment.

Photo: Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary Photo: Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary

A long-standing fixture of the Canadian business community

Now in its 32nd edition, the Canadian Lobster Dinner is one of the highlights of the Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary’s annual calendar.

For the Hungarian and international business representatives who attended, the evening was not only a chance to enjoy a distinctive Canadian culinary experience but also an opportunity to strengthen professional relationships. The Chamber’s upcoming events will provide further occasions for members and partners to stay connected in the months ahead.

World.title: Road to Budapest Airport set for major upgrade and expansion
World.content:
Hungary’s transport and investment minister, Dávid Vitézy, has announced plans to renovate and expand the main road connecting Budapest with Ferenc Liszt International Airport, but major construction work expected to begin in the end of this decade.

Government approves long-awaited renovation and expansion

The government has approved the revival of the long-delayed project, which aims to improve traffic flow, make journeys to the airport more reliable and strengthen connections between the capital’s southern districts and surrounding settlements.

Vitézy said previous governments had promised to rebuild the airport expressway for more than a decade but had repeatedly postponed the work. The current administration has now authorised further preparations, including land acquisition and the completion of detailed designs.

The existing road has only one lane in each direction, meaning a single accident can bring traffic to a complete standstill. This affects not only motorists and taxis heading to the airport but also the 100E airport bus service and commuters travelling from the Vecsés area.

Nearly 11 kilometres of roads and junctions to be upgraded in Budapest

The project covers almost 11 kilometres between Határ Road and Vecsés, including improvements to the airport road and the parallel Gyömrői Road. The plans include expanding key sections, replacing outdated bridges and underpasses, and introducing additional junctions.

A new dual-carriageway bridge is planned between Kőbánya-Kispest and Hangár Street, with one of its outer lanes reserved for buses. Further sections would feature up to three lanes in each direction, including dedicated bus lanes, while the current arrangement separating traffic in the central lanes would be removed.

The scheme also includes upgrading Kőér Street, building a grade-separated crossing of the Budapest–Cegléd–Szolnok railway line, and improving connections for pedestrians and cyclists. A dangerous level crossing at the end of Üllői Road is also due to be replaced by a separate-level road and rail connection. Noise barriers covering more than 45,000 square metres are planned along a combined length of 10.8 kilometres to protect nearby residential areas.

Land acquisition and preparation to begin

The government has allocated HUF 24.5 billion for preparatory work and land acquisition in 2027 and 2028. More than 300 properties are expected to be affected by the acquisitions required for the project. According to Vitézy, the final construction plans could be completed in the second half of 2027, allowing the public procurement process to begin around the same time. Preliminary construction work could start in 2028, with the main building phase expected in 2029.

The minister said the development would improve access to the airport while creating better links between neighbourhoods currently divided by the expressway. The project is also intended to improve the first impression of Budapest for visitors arriving by road.

World.title: Budapest commuters to get new travel options as BKK launches regional service and 2027 company passes
World.content:
Budapest is preparing changes to public transport that could make life easier for commuters, including foreign employees living or working in the capital and its surrounding towns. From January 2027, a new regional BKK system will coordinate public transport between Budapest and its agglomeration, while companies can start ordering employee travel passes for next year as early as 1 December.

BKK bus service to be extended to Érd

Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony announced that the regional BKK system will launch on 1 January 2027, with funding shared equally between the capital and the Hungarian state.

One of the first practical changes will affect bus route 133E, which is to be extended beyond Budapest to Érd, a town south-west of the capital. The move is intended to improve public transport connections for people commuting between the agglomeration and Budapest.

Karácsony argued that transport planning should not stop at the city boundary, as Budapest and neighbouring settlements have a shared interest in faster and more convenient journeys. He also said that commuters from the surrounding towns account for 40–50% of traffic congestion in the capital, with an estimated 15,000–20,000 people travelling by car from Érd alone.

The new system aims to bring Budapest and suburban public transport closer together rather than treating them as separate networks. Further details of the changes are expected as the launch approaches.

Bus 133E. Photo: BKK

Companies can order 2027 BKK passes from December

Employers in Budapest will also have a new opportunity to organise public transport benefits for their staff. The Budapest Transport Centre (BKK) will open orders for 2027 company travel passes on 1 December through its renewed online business customer platform.

Businesses and institutions can purchase monthly or annual Pest County and Hungary Passes, as well as monthly, quarterly or annual Budapest Passes. The tickets are available in both traditional paper form and digitally through the BudapestGO app.

Companies that pay for their confirmed orders by bank transfer by 21 December can collect the purchased passes before the end of 2026. Paper tickets can be collected in person, while BKK also offers delivery by courier within Budapest for orders above a specified quantity.

Employers can find information about the available passes and registration requirements at BKK’s business customer website. Companies that would first like to discuss their options can contact BKK’s sales team without registering.

For foreign employees, the scheme may be worth asking their HR departments about when discussing workplace benefits, particularly if they regularly use public transport to travel between Budapest and the surrounding towns.

World.title: Bosnian Court Convicts Three of Wartime Abuses of Civilian Prisoners
World.content:
Bosanski Novi. Photo: BIRN.

The Bosnian state court on Thursday sentenced Mira Bosancic to 17 years in prison, and Simo Licina and Zarko Kalinic to 12 years each, for crimes against civilians who were detained in the fire station building in Bosanski Novi during the Bosnian war in ​​1992.

In the first-instance verdict, the court found Bosancic, Licina and Kalinic guilty of committing crimes against humanity – persecution by murder, enforced disappearance and physical abuse.

They committed the crimes while serving as military policemen with the Bosnian Serb Army’s Light Novograd Brigade.

“The judging panel has determined that during the relevant period, a widespread and systematic attack by the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, now Republika Srpska, took place,” presiding judge Halil Lagumdzija said.

Bosancic was found guilty on three counts of participating in the beating of detained civilians in the basement of the fire station building, as well seizing several people who have been missing ever since.

Licina and Kalinic were found guilty of tying up and stripping a prisoner, cutting him with a knife and then pouring salt on him. The prisoner died of his injuries.

“His body was taken away and has not been found to this day,” said Lagumdzija.

However, the judges found that it had not been proven that Bosancic participated in the forced disappearance of two civilians and the killing of another. Due to lack of evidence, the defendants were acquitted of beating and taking away two men.

Four other defendants in the trial – Nedjeljko Pilipovic and Bogdan, Zarko and Jovan Grab – were acquitted of all charges.

The verdict can be appealed.

World.title: Greek Deputy Minister Quits Over Allegations About Daughter’s University Admission
World.content:
Deputy Minister of Development Lazaros Tsavdaridis. Photo: Greek Ministry of Development .

Deputy Minister of Development Lazaros Tsavdaridis has resigned following allegations that his daughter only nominally joined a handball team, without actually participating, in order to secure extra points for her university admission requirements.

A report by MEGA TV on November 11 alleged that 17-year-old registered with the youth handball team of Pylaia, Thessaloniki, and travelled to the Panhellenic Youth Championship with the team, but did not actrually play.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis accepted the Deputy Minister’s resignation on Thursday morning. Pavlos Marinakis, the government spokesperson, said that the explanations provided for the incident “were not sufficient”.

Marinakis said the government was reviewing the system for awarding academic points to athletes, with an emphasis on actual participation and the duration of their involvement in sports, adding that the Ministry of Education will re-examine the current framework in place since 1999.

Tsavdaridis denied wrongdoing. “My daughter never made use of additional points to gain entry into any Greek university department,” he stated on November 11.

He said his daughter sat for the entrance exams and gained admission to the School of Agriculture in Larissa on her own merit, without using any points derived from the handball team she played for.

He also noted that she did not attend the School of Agriculture, choosing instead to pursue her studies at a university in Cyprus.

The Greek Handball Federation in a press release issued on November 11 said no competition regulations had been violated.

“According to official competition records, [the teenager] had a valid athlete registration card and was physically present on her team’s bench during the matches for which she was registered,” it stated.

“There is no evidence of any violation of competition regulations that would constitute an unlawful or irregular participation of the athlete in the tournament,” it added.

The government said Deputy Interior Minister Vasilis Spanakis is taking on the position of Deputy Minister of Development.

World.title: North Macedonia Opposition Accuses Govt Over Subsidiary of Failed Serbian Bank
World.content:
Venko Filipce, head of North Macedonia’s main opposition Social Democrats, SDSM. Photo: SDSM.

The opposition Social Democrats, SDSM, on Thursday accused the government of trying to silence it and protect the local subsidiary of Serbia’s failed Alta Banka.

The claim came after North Macedonia’s National Bank filed criminal complaints against four senior SDSM party officials over their statements about the bank’s condition.

The SDSM said the bank’s criminal complaints against party leader Venko Filipce and three others were intended to put pressure on the party, accusing Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski of acting “in a panic to protect Alta Banka”.

Filipce wrote on Facebook that his party would file its own criminal complaints over Alta Banka’s entry into North Macedonia and its handling of citizens’ and public enterprises’ funds.

On Wednesday, North Macedonia’s National Bank confirmed that it had filed criminal complaints over statements made by senior SDSM members containing “serious and unfounded accusations” about Alta Banka Bitola, the North Macedonia subsidiary of the recently bankrupted Serbian Alta Banka. The National Bank did not specify the alleged criminal offences.

On November 5, Mickoski called for prosecutors to investigate the SDSM for the “criminal offence of sabotage”, accusing it of spreading lies and putting citizens in a state of unjustified insecurity and fear.

Serbia’s central bank revoked the operating licence of Alta Banka in Belgrade on October 31, citing the deterioration in its financial position. Bankruptcy proceedings followed.

Its North Macedonia subsidiary, in which the Belgrade bank holds a 95.17 per cent stake, was placed under temporary administration by North Macedonia’s central bank on November 1.

This was intended to protect the local bank’s assets and depositors while its ownership situation is resolved. It has resulted in temporary restrictions on customers’ access to their money, triggering concern among savers and queues at ATMs.

The SDSM has questioned how and why Alta Banka was given a permit to enter the North Macedonia market in 2025, and whether the origin of its capital was properly checked.

Filipce has alleged links between the bank’s Serbian owner, businessman Davor Macura, and Serbian ex-President Aleksandar Vucic’s political and business circles.

He raised suspicions that the bank could have been used for money laundering, involving Russian and other questionable capital. His party has also questioned whether the bank’s reported financial assets actually exist and whether political influence affected the National Bank’s decisions.

Filipce has claimed that as much as 150 to 180 million euros could be at stake, questioning whether customers, including pensioners receiving payments through the bank, would be able to access their money.

On Wednesday, in parliament, Central Bank Governor Trajko Slaveski insisted Alta Banka Bitola was financially sound, and should be offered to another potential buyer.

He refused to disclose how many big corporate clients, including state-owned companies and public enterprises, hold accounts with Alta Banka Bitola, which could shed more light on the extent of the problem, calling it a “banking secret”.

Chief Public Prosecutor Nenad Saveski at the same hearing declined to answer whether the Prosecutor’s Office had opened an initial investigation into the bank, insisting that, too, was confidential.

Despite the political storm surrounding it, Alta Banka Bitola is a relatively small player in North Macedonia’s banking sector.

It ranked in 12th place among the country’s 14 banks in terms of total assets in 2025, with assets of around 11.3 billion denars [about 184 million euros], representing just 1.21 per cent of the banking market.

World.title: Why Poland Has Spent a Decade Fighting Over Its Constitutional Tribunal
World.content:
The opposition, particularly the populist-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, denounced the move as a “coup”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government portrayed it as another step towards restoring the rule of law.

It was the latest round in a decade-long fight that has drawn in the European Court of Human Rights, the Court of Justice of the European Union (ECJ) and the Council of Europe’s Venice Commission, all of which have questioned how the Tribunal is composed.

Most EU countries have a similar court; few treat it as a spectator sport. In a 2025 study of awareness of judicial independence in Germany, Poland, Hungary and the US, nearly half of German respondents said they were not very aware of their Federal Constitutional Court, despite its considerable power, compared with more than 80 per cent of Poles who said they were somewhat or very aware of theirs.

“I know this is shocking to people from other countries,” Anna Wojcik, a constitutional law researcher and journalist, tells BIRN. “I can’t think of another example of such a fierce political battle over a Constitutional Tribunal. Even in Hungary, disputes over the court have been more technical and legal in nature, rather than spilling into protests outside its doors.”

Part of the explanation lies in what the court can do in the very polarised politics of Poland: being able to rule on whether laws are compatible with the constitution, it is one of the few institutions able to overrule a parliamentary majority. Whoever controls it, or can stop it working, escapes one of the main checks on their power. Furthermore, it became central to the culture wars being fought in the country when it was the tool used by the previous PiS government in 2020 to further restrict abortion rights.

Anna Materska-Sosnowska, a political scientist at the University of Warsaw, sees two things converging in the current crisis: the long erosion of constitutional review, and everyday party rivalry.

“Electoral calculations matter, but reducing the whole conflict to a fight for votes obscures what is really at stake: who can effectively limit political power, and on what terms,” she tells BIRN.

Wojcik puts it more bluntly. “I think there is a strong sense in Polish politics of ‘it’s our turn now’ – a majoritarian view of democracy,” she says. “Ultimately, it’s all about power.”

World.title: Turkey ‘Hiding Weak Climate Record’ Behind Hosting of COP31
World.content:
“The time for words is over. Now is the time for implementation,” declared Turkey’s Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Minister Murat Kurum, who is heading this year’s United Nations climate conference, presenting COP31 as a moment to turn years of pledges into action.

But as the world’s biggest climate-related gathering takes place in Antalya this week, Turkey’s own environmental record raises questions.

Turkey became Europe’s largest producer of coal-fired electricity in 2024 and remains a major destination for European plastic waste. It continues to pursue fossil-fuel projects, including new petroleum and natural-gas infrastructure in Antalya itself.

The contrast has sharpened scrutiny of whether Turkey’s COP31 presidency reflects a genuine shift in its climate policy or is primarily an exercise in winning international prestige.

Environmental expert and climate activist Koray Dogan Urbarli says the contrast between Turkey’s climate diplomacy and domestic policies goes to the heart of its COP31 presidency.

World.title: From Behind Bars, Tirana Mayor Turns on Albania’s PM Rama
World.content:
On October 26, the day after Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led movement in a momentous election, Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj took a veiled swipe at Albania’s own leader, in power for almost as long as Vucic.

“Congratulations to the students for toppling the Machiavellian and populist from Belgrade!” Veliaj wrote on Facebook from behind bars.

“Student movements and protests do not signify the ‘end of the world’ but rather the end of ‘a world’. The sooner we as citizens and policymakers grasp this, the better equipped we will be to respond to the needs and expectations of this generation.”

Veliaj’s message, written from the prison cell where he awaits trial on corruption, money laundering and concealment of wealth charges, was widely interpreted as a dig at Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama, who is facing down daily anti-government protests in which students have assumed a prominent role.

World.title: Serbian Ex-Minister Arrested for Suspected Abuse of Office
World.content:
Former Serbian Economy Minister Rade Basta. Photo: Serbian Economy Ministry.

Former Economy Minister Rade Basta was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of defrauding public utility company Beogradske Elektrane (Belgrade Powerplants) of around 120,000 euros during his tenure as its director, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade confirmed.

It is claimed that the money was improperly channeled to various sports clubs and associations while he headed Beogradske Elektrane from 2020 to 2022. Basta has not commented publicly on the allegations so far.

Basta was Serbia’s Economy Minister in the government led by Aleksandar Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party from 2022 to 2023. He was dismissed after calling on the government to impose sanctions on Russia because of “its aggression against Ukraine”. He subsequently founded the European Way movement.

He had been appointed minister as a member of United Serbia, a party that subsequently demanded his removal from all positions to which it had nominated him following his remarks on Russia.

Basta recently applauded the Serbian Progressive Party’s defeat in last month’s parliamentary elections. He told Serbian Times that he has long believed that “the moment would come when citizens would no longer accept a policy of fear, pressure and control over institutions”.

According to the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office, the other suspects in the case against Basta include the executive director of Beogradske Elektrane and legal representatives of various sports clubs to which the money was allegedly channelled.

The prosecutor’s office said Basta was charged with abuse of his official position while the Beogradske Elektrane director was charged with abuse of official position in aiding and abetting the offence. The other suspects were charged with money laundering.

“The suspects will be held in custody for up to 48 hours, during which time they will be brought in for questioning,” the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office said.

World.title: Croatian MP Seeks to Ban Anti-Abortion Prayers Near Hospitals
World.content:
Anka Mrak Taritas. Photo: Anka Mrak Taritas/Facebook.

Parliamentarian Anka Mrak Taritas, from the Civic Liberal Alliance, GLAS, said on Wednesday that she is seeking amendments to the Public Assembly Act to prohibit gatherings of people praying outside hospitals, which have become a common occurrence in Croatia.

She said the proposed ban would apply to all gatherings, regardless of size, including a single person, within 100 metres of a hospital entrance.

Taritas explained that the ban would apply to all forms of expression, “when such acts attempt to influence a female patient’s freedom of choice, exert pressure on individuals seeking healthcare services or on healthcare professionals, infringe upon patients’ privacy, or hinder free and unimpeded access to healthcare”.

The ban would protect women from pressure, harassment and violations of their dignity and privacy at a particularly vulnerable moment, specifically when they arrive at hospitals for pregnancy termination, she said.

Taritas noted that several European countries, including Ireland, have already introduced such bans. Spain, she added, had gone further by introducing a specific criminal offence of the harassment of women and medical staff outside clinics where pregnancy terminations are performed.

“The situation in Croatia is somewhat different because, unfortunately, a culture of violence against women is fostered here. Therefore, we do not expect this proposal to be met with any receptiveness,” she said.

She said the “public call by those praying for the subjugation of women, taking place on the first Saturday of every month”, constitutes institutional violence by a state that fails to protect women from violence.

She was referencing the gatherings held on the first Saturday of every month, when ultra-conservative Catholics meet in city squares to pray for “the restoration of male authority within the family”.

Taritas argued that these meetings expose vulnerable women to further trauma.

“All of this is part of that culture of violence and is an everyday reality for women in Croatia – a reality that persists under the auspices of the government,” Taritas said.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic sees women as “insignificant”, she claimed. “They only become ‘important’ in the lead-up to elections, even though they should be considered important all the time,” she added.

World.title: November 15 is the statutory deadline to fit vehicles with tyres suitable for winter conditions
World.content:
From November 15 to March 1, motor vehicles in Bulgaria must by law be fitted with tyres suitable for winter conditions.

According to the law, approved by Bulgaria’s Parliament in 2016, cars must have tyres designed for winter conditions or that have a tread depth of no less than or equal to four millimetres, the Interior Ministry said.

The Road Traffic Act allows the use of all-season or even summer tyres if they meet the grip requirement, but experts strongly recommend winter tyres for better safety in cold weather.

The traditional Interior Ministry “Winter” campaign, which aims to increase drivers’ attention to preparing their cars for the upcoming winter season, started on November 1.

(Photo: Clive Leviev-Sawyer)

World.title: Bulgaria issues weather warnings over strong winds forecast for November 13
World.content:
Bulgaria’s national meteorological bureau has issued the Code Orange warning of dangerous weather for several districts for November 13 because of forecast strong winds.

The districts subject to the Code Orange warning are Montana, Vratsa, Dobrich, Varna, Bourgas, Shoumen, Yambol, Stara Zagora and Haskovo.

All the remaining districts, with two exceptions, are subject to the lesser Code Yellow warning of potentially dangerous weather, also because of forecast strong winds.

The exceptions are the districts of Blagoevgrad and Smolyan, which are classified Code Green for November 13, meaning that no weather warning is in place.

In Bulgaria on November 13, minimum temperatures will be between 11° and 16° Celsius, in the Sofia region, about 12°.

There will be variable cloudiness on Friday. In the evening, from the northwest, the cloudiness will increase and thicken, and rain will begin.

It will be warm for the period with maximum temperatures between 20° and 25° Celsius, in places subject to southerly winds up to 27°-28°, and in Sofia, about 21°.

In the mountains, light rain will fall in places. A strong, stormy wind will blow from the west-southwest on the highlands and northern slopes. The maximum temperature at an altitude of 1200 metres will be about 14°, at 2000 metres, about 9°.

Over the Black Sea coast, the cloudiness will be variable. In the morning, mainly along the southern coast, there will be low layered clouds and reduced visibility. There will be a strong to stormy southwest wind. Maximum temperatures will be 21°-23°, the meteorological bureau said.

World.title: Bulgaria’s government proposes complete ban on advertising gambling games
World.content:
Bulgaria’s Cabinet approved on November 11 proposed amendments to the Gambling Act that, if approved by Parliament, will see a complete ban on the advertising of gambling games.

“The aim is to strengthen the prevention of the development or deepening of addiction, as well as to have a positive impact on the most vulnerable groups of people,” the government information service said.

A limited presence of trademarks of organisers of gambling would be allowed only in sponsorships of sports clubs, federations, associations and organisations, as well as in support of activities in the fields of culture, healthcare and education, the statement said.

The amendments propose that the activities of affiliate operators be suspended. This ensures consistency between the ban on advertising gambling games and the regime applicable to persons who promote them.

A one-time state fee is introduced for maintaining a licence for organising the activities of production, distribution and service of gaming equipment and import, distribution and service of gaming equipment.

A five-year licence would cost 50 000 euro and a 10-year licence would cost 100 000 euro.

The alternative tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act (CITA) for land-based casinos and gaming halls is increasing in 2027. From 2028, this tax will be eliminated from the CITA and will be replaced by a two-component state tax provided for in the Gambling Act.

A minimum of 100 000 euro per month will be the variable part of the two-component state fee for issuing and maintaining an online betting licence.

The amendments are also related to an increase in the one-time fees for maintaining a licence to organise gambling games, the amount of contributions for socially responsible behaviour, and fines and property sanctions.

Activities are also planned to expand the prevention of gambling addiction among individuals in the education system, including through the implementation of information campaigns, preventive programmes and the development of appropriate teaching materials, the government information service said.

The amendments introduce a new requirement, that a foreign legal entity organising online betting must have a place of business in Bulgaria.

“This creates an additional mechanism for tracking financial flows, helping to detect discrepancies between the declared activity, the amount of bets, the paid out winnings, the income and expenses, and the corporate tax due,” the statement said.

A mandatory cash contribution is also introduced for payment institutions, banks and electronic money companies that carry out payment transactions related to participation in gambling games and the payment of winnings.

The bill also proposes a complete ban on cash payments between construction companies, contractors and subcontractors under contracts, construction activities, supplies of materials and provision of services.

It is envisaged that payments will be made by bank transfer or through other traceable electronic payment instruments.

“The measure will contribute to limiting the shadow economy, increasing financial discipline and creating a level playing field for construction companies that comply with the legislation,” the statement said.

(Photo: Daniel Alther/ freeimages.com)

World.title: European Parliament demands that Russia returns deported Ukrainian children
World.content:
In a resolution adopted on November 13, members of the European Parliament said that perpetrators responsible for the deportation or forced transfer of Ukrainian children during the war must be held to account.

Strongly condemning Russia’s systematic deportation, forcible transfer, illegal adoption, forced Russification, indoctrination and militarisation of Ukrainian children during the war, the text – adopted by 536 votes in favour, eight against and 37 abstentions – demands the immediate cessation of these practices and reiterates Russia’s full responsibility for respecting the rights of children under its control.

MEPs are calling on Russia to immediately, safely and unconditionally return all deported and forcibly transferred Ukrainian children back from Russian-controlled territory to unoccupied Ukraine.

They are insisting that the return of children is an obligation under international law and must never be used as a bargaining instrument or made conditional upon territorial concessions, prisoner exchanges, or other political agreements.

According to the resolution, as of September 2026, a total of 20 651 cases of the deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children by Russia have been verified, whereas approximately 1.6 million Ukrainian children are estimated to remain under Russian occupation.

It also states that, as of October 28 2026, a total of 2752 Ukrainian children deported, forcibly transported or rescued from Russian-occupied territories have so far been returned.

MEPs firmly insist that the safe and unconditional return of all unlawfully deported and forcibly transferred Ukrainian children constitutes not only an urgent humanitarian necessity but also remains a centrepiece of international efforts to establish accountability for Russian crimes committed during the war.

It must, they argue, be a central priority in all diplomatic initiatives and negotiations concerning any genuine peace agreement ending Russia’s war of aggression.

MEPs emphasise that no lasting peace can disregard the rights of these children or the accountability of those responsible for violating their rights.

The European Parliament also calls on EU member states to strengthen their practical cooperation with Ukraine, international partners, and organisations to accelerate the identification, documentation, tracing and return of all missing and deported Ukrainian children, as well as to further expand existing EU sanctions against officials and entities identified as being responsible for child deportations.

The European Parliament reiterated its full support for the International Criminal Court, the court’s unhindered activity, and its arrest warrants issued against Russian President Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, Children’s Rights Commissioner for the President of Russia, for the war crime of the unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children.

MEPs emphasise, however, that accountability must extend beyond Russia’s upper leadership to encompass the entire chain of perpetrators and enablers responsible for the execution of these crimes .

The resolution also supports the close collaboration between different stakeholders, including Europol and Eurojust, and the Ukrainian Ombudsman, for information gathering and locating illegally transferred children.
