World.title: Iraq discusses reforms with IMF to support economy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Finance, Falih Sari, and officials from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) discussed a reform path designed to enhance financial sustainability and support the Iraqi economy.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi Finance Ministry, Sari and IMF representatives wrapped up their discussions in Amman, Jordan, after making progress in negotiations for a reform program that the international organization will support in the coming years.

The reform program aims to improve the performance of Iraq’s public finances. It also aims to provide a clear monetary framework to sustain monetary policies, increase their effectiveness, and have a more favorable influence on economic activity.

The discussions covered plans to develop the banking sector—including both state-owned and private banks—and enhance efforts to combat money laundering and terrorism financing.

According to Sari, the talks centered on developing a medium-term reform program for the coming three years with the goal of improving fiscal sustainability and strengthening the Iraqi economy’s ability to face potential challenges.

Sari indicated that expert-level conversations will continue in the near future to develop a joint document between Iraq and the IMF.

The document will provide a framework for budgetary changes and a timeline for implementation over the next three years.

World.title: Iraq’s oil production surges to 4.88 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil output rose by 489,000 barrels per day in October 2026 compared to September, according to data from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) based on official Iraqi estimates.

Iraq’s oil production rose from 4.39 million barrels per day in September to 4.88 million barrels per day in October, a monthly increase of approximately 11.1 percent.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said recently that Iraq seeks to negotiate with OPEC to raise its oil output and obtain a larger export cap.

The Iraqi minister indicated that Iraq deserves a rise in output to secure the financial revenues needed to expand infrastructure and implement government goals.

Additionally, Khudair reiterated Iraq’s commitment to the 4.43 million barrels per day production cap set by OPEC.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

World.title: Iraqi, Iranian leaders meet at COP31 in Turkey
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi President Nizar Amidi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey.

The two leaders reviewed recent developments in Baghdad-Tehran relations and emphasized the need to enhance constructive engagement and expand joint cooperation in different areas.

Amidi emphasized the significance of coordinating regional and global efforts to address current challenges in the Middle East, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Presidency.

During his participation in COP31, Amidi delivered Iraq’s national message, emphasizing that the country has lost more than 50 percent of its agricultural area due to desertification and climate change.

During his stay in Antalya, Amidi held additional bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Held between November 9 and November 20, 2026, COP31 brings together heads of state, government officials, and international leaders, though notable leaders from several G7 and European nations are absent.

The summit centers on climate change financing and adaptation for vulnerable nations, loss and damage funding, and clean energy transitions rather than just new targets.

World.title: Protests in Northern Basra: Oil wealth vs. service deprivation trigger renewed unrest
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) – Widespread popular demonstrations and open-ended sit-ins have swept across the northern districts of Iraq’s oil-rich Basra Governorate—spanning Al-Sadiq, Al-Qurna, Al-Dair, Al-Nashwa, Al-Suwaib, and Al-Thaghr—since late October and early November 2026.

Residents, tribal figures, and local clerics have mobilized near the gates of major strategic oilfields, including West Qurna 1 and Majnoon, demanding immediate public service delivery, infrastructure rehabilitation, local employment quotas, and environmental remediation.

Despite sitting atop some of Iraq’s largest crude oil reserves, northern Basra communities cite severe developmental neglect, broken promises, and deteriorating living standards. Protesters—organized largely under the Al-Sadiq Movement alongside coordinated community sit-ins—have framed their demands around several urgent priorities:

Infrastructure and Public Utilities: Residents demand the immediate completion of stalled public works, including paving neglected roads, rehabilitating the Qurna–Basra highway, completing the Al-Sadiq–Izz al-Din Salim bridge, expanding potable water and sewage networks, and addressing acute shortages in schools and primary healthcare clinics.

Petrodollar and Social Benefit Allocations: Protesters are calling for transparent disbursement of Basra’s statutory petrodollar revenues, border-crossing tariffs, and the mandatory “Social Benefits” (al-Manafi al-Ijtima’iya) funds paid by international oil companies (IOCs) to develop communities hosting extraction operations.

Employment and Local Hiring: Facing high youth unemployment, residents are demanding priority hiring for local graduates and laborers within foreign and national oil companies operating in Majnoon and West Qurna.

Environmental and Health Crisis: Communities surrounding the fields have raised urgent alarms over rising rates of cancer and kidney failure linked to gas flaring, industrial pollution, and the confiscation of agricultural and tribal lands for oil expansion without adequate environmental safeguards or compensation.

The current wave of unrest reignited in late October when the Al-Sadiq Movement re-established sit-in tents outside the entrance of the West Qurna 1 oilfield, protesting the government’s failure to fulfill prior pledges to maintain service-effort machinery (al-Juhd al-Khadami).

By November 7 and 8, demonstrations expanded into Al-Dair district, where hundreds of residents led by local clerics including Sheikh Muthanna Al-Rubaie declared an open-ended sit-in. Simultaneously, residents from Al-Jazeera, Al-Nashwa, Al-Suwaib, and Al-Thaghr staged demonstrations directly outside the Majnoon oilfield perimeter on November 9, warning against continued administrative procrastination.

In response to mounting pressure near vital export arteries, Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi dispatched a high-level ministerial delegation on November 9—headed by the Minister of Oil alongside the Ministers of Construction and Housing, and Planning—instructing them to conduct on-the-ground inspections across northern Basra districts and submit an actionable report within 48 hours.

Following negotiations between protest representatives and federal officials on November 7, organizers in Al-Sadiq agreed to suspend escalatory blockades around oil installations and maintain peaceful sit-ins in exchange for the immediate reactivation of municipal service machinery and street paving operations.

Meanwhile, on November 12, Parliament’s Finance Committee convened an oversight session to audit Basra’s withheld petrodollar dues and border-crossing revenue shares, pledging to establish a clear funding roadmap prioritizing strategic development projects across northern Basra districts.

World.title: US dollar approaches 170,000 dinars across Baghdad and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued its incremental climb across major domestic parallel markets on Thursday morning, November 12, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling in Baghdad and Basra after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures across primary commercial hubs, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,000 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks recorded slightly softer retail sales at 169,200 IQD, with purchasing bids holding firmer at 169,000 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices matched the capital’s pricing spread, quoting selling rates at 169,500 IQD and buying offers at 168,000 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure widens the spread between secondary physical cash markets and the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate—fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar) since October 7, 2026.

The divergence reflects ongoing friction between formal customs/tariff disclosures and informal trade financing, keeping physical greenback demand elevated outside official electronic transfer channels.

World.title: Iraqi, Syrian leaders meet at COP31 in Turkey
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi President Nizar Amidi met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on Wednesday on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey.

The meeting addressed efforts to strengthen bilateral ties, increase security coordination, and foster regional stability, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Presidency.

Amidi stressed the importance of enhancing security cooperation between Baghdad and Damascus, which includes sharing intelligence and expertise to tackle common challenges.

The two leaders discussed recent regional and international developments, stressing the importance of easing tensions, prioritizing dialogue, and pursuing peaceful resolutions to regional crises.

Both sides emphasized the necessity of aligning their stances on environmental matters and ensuring that the recommendations from the summit regarding climate issues are actively pursued.

Al-Sharaa expressed appreciation for Iraq’s stance and reaffirmed Syria’s commitment to expanding cooperation across various sectors to serve mutual interests.

Amidi also met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres during the summit to discuss regional cooperation and climate change impacts on Iraq.

World.title: FIFA to fund 80% of new Baghdad sports city, says Younis Mahmoud
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Football Association (IFA) President Younis Mahmoud announced on Thursday, November 12, 2026, key operational and financing details for a planned multi-facility Sports City in Baghdad, backed primarily by FIFA, which is slated for completion within one year of securing the designated land plot.

In statements to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Mahmoud confirmed that architectural blueprints and engineering specifications for the integrated complex are finalized, leaving municipal land allocation as the sole remaining prerequisite before construction begins.

World.title: Crude oil from northern Iraq smuggled to Iran, Afghanistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Crude oil and major petroleum products are being smuggled from the Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah fields into Iran via the Bashmaq and Parviz Khan border crossings, according to an Iraqi intelligence investigation.

After being mixed and repackaged to avoid international sanctions, the illicit oil eventually finds its way to markets in Afghanistan and Iran.

According to intelligence findings reported by Al Arabiya News, the network uses what investigators call the “eastern route.”

Operators use official papers to secure oil quotas assigned to areas in Sulaymaniyah before diverting some of the supply to smuggling networks.

Crude oil and main derivatives are transported to the Iranian border by small and medium-sized tanker trucks. The supplies enter Iran through Iraqi Kurdistan’s Bashmaq and Parviz Khan border crossings.

The smuggled Iraqi oil is processed and combined with Iranian petroleum products at small refineries once it enters Iran.

The mixed gasoline is sold under false origin certificates to get over international restrictions, with Afghanistan being the main destination for the re-exported products.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi established a multi-agency investigating group to confront larger oil smuggling networks.

Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity opened an investigation targeting the oil smuggling network.

World.title: NCPCR set to finalise guidelines for responsible, safe use of social media by children
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid increasing use of digital platforms by children and concerns around child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is working to finalise the draft of the first set of comprehensive guidelines on âresponsible, safe and age-appropriate use of social media by childrenâ. Expected to be ready in December, the commission will put up the draft thereafter for public suggestions.As part of the ongoing consultations, the commission led by its chairperson Valeti Premchand held a final stakeholder meeting with representatives of social media platforms and online gaming platforms on Thursday where representatives of Meta, Google, X, Snapchat, ShareChat and Reddit among others were present.NCPCR member secretary Sanjeev Sharma shared that the meeting focused on reviewing the existing child safety measures adopted by digital platforms and deliberating upon the recommendations contained in the child safety implementation matrix.According to the commission the participating platforms shared their inputs against each proposed child safety safeguard under three heads: measures already implemented, future plans for implementation and any other comments.They also made brief presentations highlighting their existing child safety measures, awareness initiatives for children, parents and caregivers, and planned initiatives to further strengthen online safety.The initiative assumes significance in view of the concerns relating to exposure to harmful and age-inappropriate content, cyberbullying, online grooming, CSEAM, privacy violations and other forms of online exploitation.As part of this initiative, NCPCR held its first meeting with social media platforms and technology companies, where they deliberated upon existing child safety mechanisms, content moderation, reporting and grievance redressal systems, prevention of online exploitation and awareness measures. Another round of consultation was held with these tech companies on an individual basis.Subsequently, NCPCR held a consultation with civil society organisations (CSOs) in July. These inputs were examined and consolidated into a âchild safety implementation matrixâ which included the principles like safety by design, age assurance and age appropriate experience, child data protection, CSEAM detection and enforcement, anti-addictive design and digital wellbeing, reporting and time bound redressal and empowerment of children and parents.The consultative process was further extended to online gaming platforms, with a separate meeting held with them in October.On the way forward, the NCPCR member secretary said that with the final stakeholders meeting done, now all views gathered will be put together and the commission was hopeful that the final draft guidelines will be ready next month and then they will put it up for public suggestions for a specific period. The new guidelines will be notified thereafter to enable implementation.

World.title: 39 Discoms come under CAG scanner to ringfence projected Central investment of Rs 3 lakh cr
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the Centre projecting an investment of Rs 50 lakh crore in power sector in the next six years, by 2032, the CAG has started a special audit of 39 state-run power distribution companies (Discoms) and five other state govt departments for previous five years to identify gaps and give a holistic picture to the govt on policy formulations and prepare an integrated plan for Centre-State investment flows.The central investment flows to this sector alone are estimated to be around Rs 3 lakh crore during the next six years, a senior official said. The first of its kind CAG report will cover 27 states/UTs and its reports will be tabled separately in each of these assemblies. The audit framework has been prepared with the help of IIM Ahmedabad and after consultations with all power secretaries of state and central departments earlier this year.This time, the federal auditor is also conducting a consumer satisfaction survey of at least 10,000 users to address grievances of electricity consumers given that any stress on Discoms ultimately affect the reliability and affordability of power supply and spills over into state finances, sources said.The audit is likely to be completed by May 2027 and to be followed with four other similar audits: a special audit next year on transmission companies (Transcos), followed by an audit of renewables and generation companies, and RDSS (revamped distribution sector schemes).âDiscoms data indicated that the financial stress is primarily rooted in weaknesses in procurement, demand forecasting, metering, regulatory accounting and consumer service,â the officer pointed out. As of March 2025, about 23 Discoms had losses of Rs 30,000 crore, and 24 Discoms reported negative net worth, with accumulated losses at Rs 3.4 lakh crore.The outstanding debt of these Discoms are Rs 7.3 lakh crore with interest burden Rs 77,653 crore, making any future investment in the power sector vulnerable. âGovt support is increasingly meeting the cost of losses, debt and interest rather than investment,â the official said, adding that the revenue grants have increased from Rs 55,500 crore in 2020-21 to Rs 94,100 crore in 2024-25.The auditor had carried out data analysis of every Discoms at micro and regional level to assess the possible leakages and policy flaws. This will be part of the audit process before being shared with the Centre and states for policy actions.The auditor, source said, will also assess the power purchase agreements of states and UTs and evaluate against best industry practices to check their robustness as power trading and pricing ultimately affects the consumers and reliability of the electricity supply in the long run. Electricity theft and transmission and distribution losses will be surveyed in each of these states.

World.title: ‘Don't care if they bulldoze me’: Abhishek Banerjee on demolition of structure outside his residence

The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), along with police and the administration, carried out a demolition drive outside the TMC leader's residence, removing a temporary bamboo shed erected on the footpath and dismantling an iron gate allegedly obstructing pedestrian movement, news agency ANI reported.



The civic action came amid a political confrontation between the TMC and the BJP, days after clashes broke out outside Banerjee's residence on November 7.

The demolition came a day after Banerjee also accused surveillance around his residence using official vehicles. He shared a video on X to support his claim, alleging that police personnel were carrying out reconnaissance near his house and keeping him under surveillance.

On Wednesday, Banerjee said he had âserious reasons to believe another attack is being plannedâ and questioned whether the alleged surveillance was intended to intimidate him.

World.title: Indians top list again: 9.25 lakh acquired citizenship of OECD countries over past five years
World.content:
9.25 lakh Indians acquired citizenship in rich nations in 5 years, up 41%: OECD

Acquisitions of citizenship in

OECD countries

by former nationality

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the âInternational Migration Outlook â 2026â report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015â2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico, whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in these countries each during the five-year period 2020â2024. Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-2024 as compared to the previous five-year period.OECD comprises 38 member countries â notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.According to additional data shared with TOI, during the five-year period 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens â Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens. In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country â once again the composition of Indians was 10%.OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.30 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), the US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.25 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.The report attributes the increase in Indian citizenship in OECD member countries to the growth of Indian communities in several member countries, particularly Canada. A total of 2.61 lakh Indians became Canadian citizens during 2020â2024, an increase of 150% compared with the preceding five-year period. The numbers were also high in the US, the UK and Australia.The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.The OECD's latest report also records a rise in new citizenships from various nationalities across its member countries. Around 3 million (30 lakh) people acquired the nationality of an OECD country in 2025. The US accounted for almost 9 lakh new citizens â a rise of 9% over 2024, followed by Germany and Spain with 3 lakh new citizens each registering a rise of 9% and 6% over the previous year. Canada ranked only fourth in 2025, due to a 22% drop, and registered nearly 3 lakh new citizens. However, India's strong showing is particularly evident in Canada, which has been a major destination for Indian migrants over the past decade, with established communities contributing to the pool of people eligible to apply for citizenship.Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.07 lakh in 2023 to 4.94 lakh in 2024.âMigration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,â Mathias Cormann, OECD Secretary-General said. âWith ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring. That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,â he added.Immigrants accounted for 12% of the OECD member countries population in 2025, up from 9% in 2015. In just over half of OECD countries, immigrants contributed at least 50% of employment growth between 2014 and 2024.One in five STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity firms and sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrantâs contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills and support investment and innovation â many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers.International student inflows to OECD member countries fell from 19 lakh in 2024 to 16 lakh in 2025, with the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations. In contrast, European countries continued to attract growing numbers of international students, especially Austria, Germany and Italy. China and India remained the largest source countries.The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.50 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.With restrictive immigration policies being introduced in several OECD member countries such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia, immigration experts believe that the number of temporary workers and students could show a decline over the next few years. However, it is likely that Indians will continue to top the charts in citizenship acquisition and their foray overseas for work and study.Permanent migration to OECD member countries declined by 1.6% in 2025, falling for the second consecutive year, but remained historically high at nearly 60 lakh new permanent immigrants. Permanent migration covers people moving for family reunification, work or humanitarian reasons with a long term right to stay. With restrictive policies in major destination countries, this has shown a decline.

World.title: After back-to-back failures, Isro successfully tests modified PSLV 3rd stage
World.content:
BENGALURU: In an important step towards restoring the reliability of its workhorse Polar

Vehicle (PSLV),

Thursday said it successfully conducted a ground static test of the rocketâs modified third stage (PS3) at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) in Sriharikota.

The test, conducted on Thursday, follows two consecutive PSLV mission failures in which anomalies were observed in the rocketâs third stage. Isro said it had comprehensively reviewed the stageâs design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures and quality checks before introducing modifications to strengthen the system.

Isro said the modified PS3 solid motor incorporates improvements to its nozzle configuration and mechanical interfaces, along with additional redundancy in its sealing systems.



The space agency has also revised procedures for accepting raw materials, assembling the motor and conducting non-destructive tests (NDT) during integration and transportation.

The mechanical interfaces have also been strengthened, with redundancy introduced in the sealing systems. Isro said the adequacy of design margins had been verified and updated non-destructive testing procedures had been implemented at different stages of integration and transportation.





The modifications follow setbacks involving PSLV-C61/EOS-09 in May 2025 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 in Jan 2026. Both missions encountered problems during the third stage, raising concerns about the reliability of a launch vehicle that has been central to Indiaâs satellite launch programme.

On May 18, 2025, PSLV-C61, carrying the 1,696-kg EOS-09 Earth observation satellite, lifted off from Sriharikota. While the first two stages performed normally, Isro detected a fall in chamber pressure during the third-stage burn, preventing the rocket from completing its mission.

A national-level committee was subsequently constituted to investigate the failure and recommend corrective measures.

The second setback came on Jan 12, 2026, when PSLV-C62, carrying the EOS-N1 Earth observation satellite and 15 co-passenger payloads, encountered an anomaly towards the end of its third stage. The vehicle experienced disturbances in its roll rates, followed by a deviation in its flight path, and could not place the satellites in their intended orbits.

While both failures involved the third stage, the specific circumstances reported were different. The latest modifications, Isro said, followed a comprehensive review of the PS3 configuration and were aimed at improving its design margins and manufacturing and quality-control processes.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The space agency said the performance of the modified solid motor and its subsystems would now be assessed through a detailed analysis of the test data.

Further tests are planned based on the findings.

The PSLV, a four-stage launch vehicle, has been a mainstay of India's space programme, undertaking missions ranging from Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission to Aditya-L1. Its return to dependable flight operations is important not only for Isro's own missions but also for India's commercial satellite launch commitments.

World.title: Tanker with 19 Indian seafarers on board attacked off UAE; all safe: Shipping minister
World.content:
NEW DELHI: All 19 Indian seafarers on board a Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker were safe after the vessel was targeted in a projectile attack off Mina Saqr in the UAE on Wednesday, Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said on Thursday.

The tanker, MT DOMINICA PROSPERITY, was carrying 19 Indian nationals when it came under attack while drifting off Mina Saqr, Sonowal said in a post on X.

"The entire 22-member crew was swiftly and safely evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard, and all 19 of our Indian nationals are completely safe with no injuries," he said.

The minister added that the government was in regular contact with the ship management company to ensure the crew's safety and provide logistical support.



"We remain in continuous contact with the ship management company to ensure their ongoing safety, welfare and logistical support," Sonowal said.

This is the latest in a series of incidents involving vessels carrying Indian seafarers in the region. On Wednesday, Sonowal said that all three Indian crew members aboard Saudi Arabia-flagged oil tanker NCC FAJR were safe after the vessel was involved in a possible attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on November 11.





"All 3 Indian nationals, along with the entire crew, are safe," he said, adding that the situation was being monitored and authorities were in contact with the ship management company.

Earlier, on November 10, Liberia-flagged tanker MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY, which was carrying six Indian seafarers, was hit by a projectile while travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai through the Persian Gulf. Four crew members were injured, including one Indian national who suffered minor injuries and was taken ashore for medical examination.

The remaining 18 crew members, including five other Indian seafarers, were safe, Sonowal had said.

India has called for safe and unimpeded navigation through the Strait of Hormuz amid rising regional tensions. External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said New Delhi was in touch with concerned parties to prevent attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers.

World.title: India will remain a trusted partner for global investors, assures Union Minister Piyush Goyal
World.content:
VISAKHAPATNAM

Seeking to assuage fears over the safety of Foreign Direct Investments (FDI) due to the likely impact of global uncertainties, Union Minister for Commerce & Industry Piyush Goyal said India had been and would remain a trusted partner and a reliable destination for investors even as wars raged in other parts of the world.

The ongoing conflicts cast their shadow on international trade, but India was an exception, with its stable policies and governance that would never let the investors down, he asserted.

Participating as the chief guest in the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam on Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Goyal said the world was witnessing multiple crises, challenges and intense competition, but India was committed to standing by investors during these tough times.

He recalled that centuries ago, Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva, who governed the Andhra region, issued inscriptions assuring foreign investors of confidence and security.

The investor community could be assured of the business environment even during the present times, as the Government of India was doing all it could to ensure the safety of the money they were pumping into various projects, he asserted.

Mr. Goyal said India would fully respect and protect Intellectual Property Rights and extend cooperation to innovators and investors. India would never steal technology, he stated, promising industries full support in manufacturing high-quality products at competitive costs and at a greater speed.

While foreign investments poured in, India’s skilled youth were making a significant contribution to the country’s GDP growth by leveraging on their skills and capabilities to a phenomenal effect.

He went on to invite entrepreneurs to invest in India and Andhra Pradesh, saying they were offering tremendous opportunities in manufacturing, tourism and several other sectors.

Visakhapatnam was transforming from a ‘Steel City’ into a ‘Silicon City’ and regions like Orvakal and Pudimadaka were emerging as green energy hubs, Mr. Goyal observed.

Praise for Naidu

Further, Mr. Goyal said Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was a visionary leader who thinks ahead of his time and recognises the potential of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Quantum Technologies.

While the world was talking about ‘Ease of Doing Business’, the Chief Minister shifted to the concept of ‘Speed of Doing Business’, which was evident from the operationalisation of the escrow account mechanism for making time-bound payment of industries incentives, in a record time, Mr. Goyal added.

World.title: No compromise with Ukraine, Putin indicates to U.S. envoys during talks
World.content:
Vladimir Putin indicated on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that Russia will not compromise on its hardline demands to end the Ukraine offensive but offered a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk during a Kremlin meeting with U.S. envoys.

The Russian President said he would not water down his territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops being stationed in Ukraine — a deployment that he said would be a “continuation of war”.

Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were in Moscow after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi searching for a way to end Europe’s worst conflict since the Second World War.

Mr. Putin’s comments appeared to douse hopes that a deal to end the war could be within grasp, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to achieve “a result” before 2027.

The Americans, meanwhile, urged Mr. Putin to allow European representatives to sit at the table for the next round of talks.

Moscow has successfully managed to reframe the discussions on the war as part of a wider discussion about European security.

But Kyiv and European leaders have urged against a new “Yalta” — a reference to the post-Second World War deal to carve the continent into spheres of influence — and said talks must be focused on ending the Ukraine war first.

Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff will travel to Dublin, where a European summit is taking place, to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later on Thursday.

‘No grey zones’

Usually held behind closed doors, the Kremlin chose to televise a lengthy opening exchange between Mr. Putin and the U.S. envoys.

The Russian leader also rejected talk of a possible territorial settlement involving “grey” — or demilitarised — zones between Ukrainian and Russian positions.

World.title: CPI(M) seeks withdrawal of proposed Water Regulatory Commission
World.content:
The Communist Party of India(Marxist) Andhra Pradesh committee has demanded immediate withdrawal of the State government's proposal to establish a Water Regulatory Commission, alleging that it would privatise drinking and irrigation water, impose an additional financial burden on people and adversely affect agriculture.

CPI(M) State secretary V. Srinivasa Rao, in a press release, alleged that the government was planning to introduce the commission immediately after the local body elections, contrary to public opinion. He said the Electricity Regulatory Commission had failed to protect consumers and instead provided cover for successive increases in power tariffs, approval of questionable power purchase agreements and additional true-up charges.

The proposed water regulator would turn drinking and irrigation water into a commercial commodity, allowing private and multinational companies to gain control over rivers and reservoirs, he alleged. Mr. Srinivasa Rao said the World Bank and the Union government had been pressuring Andhra Pradesh for several years to introduce reforms in the water sector, but successive governments had hesitated due to strong opposition from farmers.

He also criticised the State government's G.O. 160, issued during the local body election period, proposing meters for rural drinking water schemes and collection of user charges based on consumption. He alleged that the order was subsequently removed from the government website following criticism.

The CPI(M) leader urged people to oppose the proposed commission, demanding that the government should instead provide relief amid drought concerns, successive cyclones and rising prices of essential commodities.

World.title: There is nothing axiomatic or eternal about one’s OBC status: Madras HC
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Thursday said factual assertions regarding lack of objective data, explicit disregard for recommendations of expert commissions, and arbitrary nature of classifications raised serious doubts about the constitutional validity of the impugned entries in Schedule I of Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016.

The court said this while hearing a petition filed by G. Kodeeswaran of Melur taluk in Madurai district, seeking a direction to declare Schedule I to the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, (Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 2016), so far as it includes Christian Nadar, Christian Shanar and Christian Gramani communities and to the extent it includes converts to Christianity in Meenavar, Parvatharajakulam, Pattanavar and Sembadavar, and Mukkuvar or Mukayar, was ultra vires the Constitution and direct the authorities to delete these communities from the Schedule and from the list of Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities.

A Division Bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and M.D. Sumathi said there was nothing axiomatic or eternal about one’s OBC status. A clear case had to be made out for inclusion or retention in the OBC list.

“Merely because some entities had enjoyed the privilege of reservation for a few decades, would that necessarily mean that the original inclusion was constitutionally justified.? We answer in the negative. As and when a challenge is mounted, the government is obliged to demonstrate to the court’s satisfaction that inclusion or retention of the concerned entity in the OBC list is constitutionally warranted or justified,” the court said.

The court said the petition raised profound constitutional questions that struck at the very foundation of the reservations jurisprudence in Tamil Nadu. The petitioner from Kallar community, a notified BC, had applied for the Combined Civil Services Examination IV (Group IV Services) .

Competing for the turns reserved for BCs, the petitioner approached the court with a concrete and immediate grievance. He contended that the reservation pool meant for genuinely BCs was being diluted by the inclusion of various Christian denominations and converts, who had never been subjected to any empirical test of social and educational backwardness as mandated by Article 16(4) of the Constitution, the court said.

The court said the petitioner highlighted the glaring anomaly found in the differential treatment meted out to different convert categories. A Scheduled Caste person who converted to Christianity was deemed a BC. The 2016 Act itself acknowledged that a person professing Christianity could not be deemed an SC.

However, certain MBCs (such as Meenavar, Parvatharajakulam, and Mukkuvar) who converted to Christianity were permitted to retain that status, the court said.

The court said it was the petitioner’s case that the fundamental right to equality of opportunity guaranteed under Article 16 (1) of the Constitution to genuine BCs could not be sacrificed at the altar of political expediency. “We are satisfied that the petitioner has established a prima facie case that warrants deep constitutional scrutiny”, the court said, and ordered notice to the State.

World.title: DRDL Director highlights importance of indigenous research
World.content:
Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education Deemed-to-be-University, Vijayawada, has inked a pact with the Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL), Hyderabad, on Thursday to provide opportunities for academic interaction, research engagement and knowledge sharing.

The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between DRDL Director Ankitha Raju and Siddhartha University Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao.

Speaking about the contributions made by the DRDL to the country’s defence research and technological advancement, Mr. Ankitha Raju said the DRDL plays a crucial role in the design and development of advanced missile systems and strategic defence technologies, including aerodynamics, propulsion systems, navigation, guidance, control systems and other indigenous technologies that strengthen India’s national security and self-reliance.

He highlighted the importance of indigenous research, technological innovation and collaboration between premier research organisations and academic institutions and urged students and faculty to actively take up research activities, innovation and technology development to contribute towards national missions.

The programme was attended by the deans of all schools, heads of various departments and representatives of different academic and administrative units of the university.

World.title: No need for Opposition approval to launch strikes, says Israel’s Katz
World.content:
Israeli caretaker Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that the outgoing coalition does not need permission from the opposition to decide on fresh military operations, following calls to show restraint.

“We do not need approval from the opposition or any legal authority” for the army to carry out strikes in any of the arenas where it operates, Mr. Katz wrote on X.

The leader of the opposition bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, has called on caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to show restraint, warning that the use of force without a “direct and immediate threat” could have “disastrous consequences for Israeli democracy and for citizens’ trust”.

Mr. Netanyahu repeatedly threatened to resume the Iran war on the campaign trail for elections last month, warning of threats and even posting an image of a nuclear bomb destroying Tel Aviv.

Mr. Katz said Thursday (November 12, 2026) that the outgoing coalition had “demonstrated resolve and sound judgment in dealing with Iran, in full coordination with the IDF — and that will remain the case now, as circumstances require”.

Mr. Netanyahu agreed to meet Thursday (November 12, 2026) with Mr. Eisenkot to discuss national security following the row over whether the outgoing government can resume the conflict.

In a short joint statement, Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Netanyahu said they would meet at the Prime Minister’s office for a briefing attended by Mr. Netanyahu’s military aide.

The announcement came a day after Mr. Eisenkot, who has a mandate to try to form a new government, accused Mr. Netanyahu of refusing to brief him, in what he called a deviation from protocol.

Avigdor Liberman, a key member of Mr. Eisenkot’s political bloc who has been named head of a parliamentary committee on foreign and defence affairs, also criticised Mr. Netanyahu on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

“I warn you: a caretaker government is not allowed to make decisions that could drag Israel into war without parliamentary oversight and without the full consent of all security agencies,” said Liberman, a hawkish former aide to Mr. Netanyahu who has become a strident critic.

Neither Liberman nor Mr. Eisenkot mentioned Iran directly.

Mr. Netanyahu’s office has hit back, saying on Wednesday that Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, was politicising national security.

Editorial | Point of no return: On Israel’s next government

Since last year Mr. Netanyahu has twice ordered major bombing campaigns against Iran in partnership with U.S. President Donald Trump.

Both leaders said afterwards that they had severely set back Iran’s efforts to build nuclear weapons, which the clerical state denies pursuing.

Trump has allied himself with Mr. Netanyahu but in recent days has said the focus is on diplomacy, after he also suffered a setback in elections, partly due to the war.

Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, although President Isaac Herzog can give him an extension until December 20.

Both Mr. Eisenkot’s broad left-to-right coalition and Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc of hard-right and religious parties fell short of a majority in Israel’s October polls.

Mr. Eisenkot is exploring options to form a government, with Liberman demanding he not work with Israeli-Arab lawmakers, whose numbers soared in the elections on the back of anger over Mr. Netanyahu.

World.title: When the village becomes an art gallery: 26 homes open their doors to creativity
World.content:
What if an art gallery had no white walls, no ticket counter and no imposing entrance? What if, instead, visitors had to walk through a village, step into its homes and discover paintings displayed on verandas and in domestic spaces? In Enkakkad, art is finding an unconventional home. Twenty-six houses in the village have opened their doors to host ‘10.26’ (Paththu irupathaaru), an exhibition that brings together selected works from the 10-year artistic journey of Niracharthu. Here, the village itself becomes a gallery, and its homes offer an alternative setting for experiencing visual art.

Moving away from the familiar gallery format, the exhibition seeks to dissolve the boundaries between art, architecture and everyday life. Instead of asking villagers to travel to urban galleries, it brings art to their doorsteps, placing the domestic veranda in the spotlight as a space for artistic engagement.

More than 50 works by 45 artists who have participated in Niracharthu’s art camps are on display. The exhibition traces a decade of artistic exploration while offering visitors an opportunity to encounter art in spaces that are part of the village’s lived experience.

The exhibition was formally opened through a walk-through of all 26 venues. Manoj Vailoor, principal of the Mavelikkara College of Fine Arts, and curator Megha V. Sreyus led the walk-through, accompanied by children attending the art workshop, local residents and members of the Niracharthu team.

For curator Megha V. Sreyus, the idea goes beyond changing the location of an exhibition. It is about changing the way people encounter and experience art. “This exhibition invites the viewer to abandon the passive, sterile walking patterns of the gallery hall. To navigate this curated spatiality is to inhabit an itinerary of collective memory, domestic architecture and situated visuality — proving that the most urgent critical engagements of our time can emerge directly from the communal porch. Thus, this exhibition transforms the veranda as an alternate threshold of a visuality reimagined,” she says.

By turning familiar homes into exhibition spaces, ‘10.26’ also creates an opportunity for residents to engage with artworks in an informal setting. The experience is as much about discovering the village as it is about discovering art. The exhibition will continue until December 6. Visitors can explore the 26 venues between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.

World.title: Ladakh civil society group begins protest over Home Ministry failure to hold talks
World.content:
Ladakh’s civil society group, the Leh Apex Body (LAB), on Thursday (November 12, 2026) organised an indefinite sit-in in Leh over the failure of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to resume talks with the civil society bodies of the region and holding of hill council elections at the peak of winter. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was put under house arrest and disallowed to join the protest.

Scores of protesters, both men and women, assembled at the Nawang Dorjay Stobdan (NDS) Memorial Park in Leh. It is the same site where a major demonstration broke out in September 2025. The protesters raised six demands, which included opposition to simultaneous elections, convening of the MHA Sub-Committee meeting, release of the Judicial Enquiry Commission report on the September 24 incident, unconditional withdrawal of all cases, constituting an independent Delimitation Commission and complete roll back of the new liquor policy.

“Our indefinite dharna is over the MHA’s failure to resume talks with Ladakh groups and holding of hill council elections at the peak of winter. Already 25% of the population has left Ladakh. This is not the right time to hold elections,” said LAB co-chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook.

Vote chori fears

For the first time, the LAB also highlighted fears over the fairness of upcoming elections. “We fear these elections will be rigged. We have apprehensions of vote ‘chori’. Several voters, mostly Gen Z voters, have been deleted from the electoral rolls. They can’t enrol now. We see a conspiracy behind holding of these elections,” said Mr. Lakrook.

The State Election Commission (SEC) in Ladakh has announced panchayat and municipal elections on November 21 and hill council elections in eight districts on December 4. Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature, and these hill councils are the main platform for public representatives to operate from. However, the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) oppose council elections in December and demand postponement by six months.

“We are going to intensify our protests. The LAB and the KDA are in touch with each other. We also face issues such as liquor licence, Nautor land issue etc.,” said Mr. Lakrook.

He said people of trans-Himalayas were unhappy. “Arunachal Pradesh is witnessing protests over land. Ladakh is observing protests over rights. People of these regions are the first to support the Army in case of any threat. Is this good for national security?” asked Mr. Lakrook.

Meanwhile, the L-G administration stopped Mr. Wangchuk from joining these protests. “It is sad Mr. Wangchuk, who is an important member of the LAB, was placed under house arrest on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). He was having food with us when he was asked to shift to his home. This exposes the administration. All he does is support our demands,” said Mr. Lakrook.

Invoking Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, the District Magistrate, Leh, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) imposed restrictions on Mr. Wangchuk on his movement, “to refrain from engaging in any activity, organising or participating in any unauthorised rally, procession or public gathering or conduct that is likely to cause a breach of public peace, disturbance of public tranquillity or obstruction to the peaceful conduct of the ongoing electoral processes within the territorial jurisdiction of Leh”.

“This order shall come into force with immediate effect and shall remain in force for a period of 60 days, unless rescinded or modified earlier in accordance with law,” it said.

According to an official order, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Leh, was directed to issue preventive orders and imposition of restrictions upon Mr. Wangchuk “on the grounds that his activities, previous antecedents, and alleged attempts to mobilise and instigate the general public have affected public order in the district before”.

BJP backs polls

Meanwhile, BJP leader and ex-Member of Parliament Thupstan Chhewang extended support to the upcoming elections and appealed to the people of Ladakh “to participate wholeheartedly and peacefully in the forthcoming December 4 hill council elections”.

Describing these elections as “a historic opportunity to strengthen grassroots democracy and secure the region’s future”, Mr. Chhewang said, “The 33% reservation for women has been introduced for the first time. I urge Ladakhi women to seize this opportunity to participate actively in political leadership and decision-making.”

He also welcomed the creation of six new districts. Referring to the struggle for Ladakh’s autonomy and Union Territory status, Mr. Chhewang said, “These achievements were secured through patience, unity, perseverance and collective determination. The hard-won democratic rights and institutions of Ladakh must be protected and strengthened rather than allowed to weaken”.

He underlined Ladakh’s unwavering commitment to India’s unity and territorial integrity and emphasised the need to safeguard the region’s distinct cultural identity, fragile environment and deeply cherished Buddhist spiritual heritage.

“I appeal to the younger generation not to let this historic opportunity go to waste. This is a path-breaking moment, and no one should stand in its way,” said Mr. Chhewang.

World.title: Naqvi suggests referendum as 'solution' to debate on new administrative units
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday suggested that political parties hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on the creation of new administrative units or provinces, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate.

The security czar has whipped up a political storm over the past few months since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Replying to a media query at the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in Lahore on Thursday, Naqvi noted that each political party had a right to disagree with another party or individual.

At the same time, he observed that all parties stressed democracy and the supremacy of the people. Therefore, he said: “My only request to all political parties is that this is such an issue […] so they should hold a referendum.

“Whatever the public’s opinion in the referendum is; if the public says [new units] should not be created, I am 100 per cent with them that they should not be created. [But], if the public says they should be made, then they should.”

Naqvi noted that political parties had varying stances on the debate, with the PPP “having its own stance [and] some parties having their own stance while not saying anything officially”.

He again stressed that the solution was to take public opinion into account, suggesting that if there was a proposal for a “better solution”, that should also be presented to the people.

Acknowledging the importance of allies in the ruling coalition, he said: “Everyone is a part of this government, and nothing will happen against their will. And if something does happen, then it will be after taking everyone’s consensus.”

“My only recommendation is that if we were to conclude this debate, then we should just take the people’s opinion,” he said.

The minister had also affirmed in September that any new administrative units would only be formed with the public’s consent, while also doubling down on his call for new provinces.

Naqvi claims he and Bilawal ‘nearly on same page’

Responding to another question, Naqvi recalled recent remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, wherein he had called for a “political reset” and encouraged unity among political parties.

The security czar contended that he and Bilawal were “nearly on the same page”.

“He (Bilawal) said that political matters are about to be reset, while my suggestion is that overall matters are about to be reset,” Naqvi elaborated.

In his remarks on Tuesday, the Bhutto scion had called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”.

His call for political unity followed exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between federal ministers and veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has now decided to strengthen his ties with the opposition.

The PPP chairman also questioned the need for “new experiments” when the country was confronted with much bigger challenges, particularly the economic crisis arising from the Middle East tensions.

The same day, PPP’s Punjab chapter also strongly rejected any move towards the creation of new provinces, asserting that doing so will neither address soaring inflation nor rampant unemployment.

While Naqvi said he and Bilawal largely shared the same views, the PPP chairman in September had called for a parliamentary debate on the creation of new provinces.

“So instead of [speaking at] business forums, Mohsin Naqvi should visit [Parliament],” he had remarked, an apparent reference to the first instance of Naqvi stressing the need for more administrative units while speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 in July.

PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the creation of a new province within Sindh. It has also maintained that any decision on the subject must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary processes with political consensus.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s recent statement regarding the creation of 12 more provinces has also added to the debate on administrative units started by Naqvi.

‘Corruption exists across entire Pakistan’

In his talk with reporters, Naqvi was also asked about federal minister Chaudhry Salik’s recent remarks over alleged corruption in Punjab.

In response, he said: “If someone is saying that no corruption is taking place in Pakistan, then apologies but corruption exists across the entire country and it is our responsibility to end it.”

The interior minister stressed the importance of highlighting corruption where it was present.

The conversation on corruption started after PML-Q’s Salik criticised the incumbent Punjab government led by PML-N, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption.

Incensed by his remarks, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Salik for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks.

Naqvi was also asked about a Capital Development Authority (CDA) notice issued in relation to the residence of the JUI-F chief, which he defended, stating, “This (CDA) campaign has been ongoing for months, and it is not against a certain individual.”

World.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after reports of extramarital affairs
World.content:
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China.

The company’s board said Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia.

“Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump, who was close to Huang, said on his Truth Social network.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 per cent, will exit the board as well.

Nvidia shares fell more than 10pc in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.

Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.

“The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap … that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

“In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.”

Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.

Trump said on Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.

Huang’s rockstar status

For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company.

That turned Huang into a rockstar CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.

But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.

Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.

The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

World.title: Canadian mining company signs MoU with Mari Energies in South Asia push
World.content:
Ivanhoe Mines signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Mari Energies on Thursday, the Canadian company’s chairman Robert Friedland said on the sidelines of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum.

Friedland said Ivanhoe is in the early stages of setting up a local office in Pakistan and will sign another MoU on Friday.

Mari Energies’ mining unit, Mari Minerals, has multiple mineral exploration projects, including copper and gold in Pakistan.

The partnership marks the Canadian miner’s entry into South Asia, expanding its presence beyond its major mineral projects in southern Africa.

“We’re excited to be here in Pakistan,” Friedland said.

‘Significant evidence’ of placer gold in Punjab rivers, says CM Maryam

At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said that there was “significant evidence” of “sufficient quantities” of placer gold flowing in the province’s five rivers.

Maryam said Punjab was the land of five rivers and that gold was “literally flowing” in all five, particularly in the areas of Mianwali and Attock.

Describing Pakistan as a “pot of gold”, she said its wealth lay both above and beneath the ground and needed to be explored and converted into tangible wealth.

“The wealth beneath Punjab was never a problem, never a problem, just like the whole of Pakistan, just like all four provinces and the federating units. The chaos above ground was the actual problem,” she said.

Maryam said the provincial mines and minerals department’s revenue stood at around Rs10 billion two and a half years ago but had since increased to Rs40bn.

“And it is just the beginning,” she added.

She also highlighted the province’s iron ore reserves, saying Chiniot had 261.5 million tonnes of iron ore.

She said the provincial government was taking steps to facilitate investment in the mining sector and create an enabling environment for investors.

The Punjab chief minister said her role as chief executive of the country’s most populous province was to facilitate investors and create an enabling environment by eliminating red tape, bureaucratic delays and unnecessary hurdles.

The provincial government was offering one-window facilitation to ensure investors did not have to run from pillar to post to complete the necessary procedures, she added.

Maryam said the government was also making substantial capital investments to reduce investors’ capital expenditure and prevent them from having to tie up funds in purchasing expensive land.

Additionally, the government was offering concessional financing of up to Rs5 billion and would provide solar-powered energy solutions to investors to help offset high energy and fuel costs.

Dar says provincial partnership vital for mineral development

Dar said Pakistan’s constitutional framework made provincial partnership indispensable, adding that the provinces were essential partners in the national undertaking and that their constitutional authority and ownership of mineral resources must be respected.

Addressing the event, he said the federal government was working alongside provincial governments and their leadership through national coordination, investment facilitation, policy alignment and international engagement.

Dar said Pakistan’s mineral resources were central to the next phase of the country’s economic transformation, stressing the need to diversify exports, strengthen the industrial base and attract long-term investment.

He said Pakistan possessed substantial and diverse mineral resources, including significant copper and gold potential along the Tethyan metallogenic belt in the west of the country. The country also had deposits of iron ore, chromite, lead, zinc, coal, rock salt, marble, gypsum, gemstones and other industrial minerals.

The deputy PM said the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan demonstrated the potential of international expertise, national participation and provincial ownership in attracting major long-term investment.

He stressed that Pakistan’s ambition should extend beyond extracting minerals and exporting them in raw form, saying the country needed to develop the capacity to process and refine them, as well as manufacture mineral-based products domestically.

Dar said Balochistan was central to Pakistan’s mineral future, adding that the development of its resources should contribute meaningfully to the provincial economy and the well-being of its people.

He also emphasised the importance of local employment, skills development and the participation of Pakistani companies, saying local communities must be active participants in and beneficiaries of mineral development.

The deputy prime minister further stated that environmental protection, workers’ safety and the rehabilitation of mining sites were essential to a successful minerals industry.

The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper.

Designed as an open-pit mining and processing operation, the project will initially process 45 million tonnes of ore annually, with capacity expected to double to 90m tonnes after the completion of Phase 2.

The mine has an estimated operational life of 37 years, which could potentially extend to 80 years through further exploration and resource development.

World.title: Imran's key message from jail is to 'stick firmly to the ideology': PTI secretary general
World.content:
Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan wants his party leaders to “stick firmly to the ideology” of the party, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Thursday.

Following the Islamabad High Court’s order to jail authorities to facilitate meetings for legal consultation, lawyers Barrister Salman Safdar and Advocate Latif Khosa were able to meet Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail on Wednesday.

According to both lawyers, the meeting lasted at least three hours and mainly focused on the couple’s legal and health issues. However, they did not divulge further details; the government often objects to lawyers using such meetings to make political statements.

Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’ on Thursday, Raja said that he had multiple detailed conversations with Barrister Safdar following the latter’s meeting with Imran.

“Imran Khan’s fundamental message was to stick firmly to the ideology,” the PTI secretary general said, conveying details he heard from Safdar.

“I have also been directed to stick to [our] ideology,” Raja added, noting that Imran’s “fundamental message is not to bow”.

He further said Imran reiterated his support for National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, whom the PTI founder had picked for their respective roles.

He quoted Imran as saying that Achakzai and Abbas were not individuals who would “bow down or be sold”, and he had nominated them after deep contemplation.

“Imran Khan sahib’s directives will be acted upon,” the PTI secretary general declared.

He added that Imran had also issued instructions on the issue of the formation of new provinces during his meetings with Safdar, including the one on Nov 2.

“Imran Khan is not ready to step back from his ideology of democracy and public welfare […] the rule of the people is the foremost priority of Imran Khan,” Raja stated.

He said that Imran considered concerns related to his well-being as unnecessary; however, the party was concerned about his health, as Imran’s blood pressure was not stable.

Raja claimed that Imran had also reported in yesterday’s meeting about his blood pressure “reaching 193 on Saturday”.

Asked whether this message could be considered political and thereby hinder chances of future jail meetings, Raja contended that although a handful of matters were discussed during the three-hour-long huddle, everything was monitored and recorded via microphones.

He noted that Khosa, who was also an MNA, has made several statements after the meeting, which “compelled Safdar to clarify matters”.

Regarding himself, the PTI secretary general said Imran had issued instructions to him regarding standing with the principles and reorganisation of the party.

He acknowledged that there was a small faction in the PTI which is displeased with him. However, he emphasised that Imran’s directives conveyed to him were different.

“Imran Khan’s message for me is to create space while upholding the principles and move forward,” Raja said, denying other notions coming from different circles within the PTI.

Regarding directives issued by Imran on a possible 28th constitutional amendment, the PTI secretary general said he would put this matter before the party leadership first.

The directions were related to standing with democratic principles and the rights of small provinces, he said, adding that the PTI founder had always supported the creation of new administrative units.

However, Raja noted that there had been some concerns related to the “context” behind the formation of new administrative units and stressed the importance of the public’s opinion.

World.title: High-speed diesel price dips by Rs4 per litre, petrol by Rs3
World.content:
The government on Thursday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4, marking the eighth consecutive decrease.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs332 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs360 on Nov 13 (Friday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday after earlier losses, as persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Russia offset pressure from rising crude output.

Brent futures were up 65 cents at $93.40 a barrel at 7:25pm PKT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 1 cent to $86.54; both contracts fell more than $1 per barrel in early Asian trading. They were also headed for a weekly fall.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: CEC Raja alleges federal govt wants to 'sabotage' Islamabad local govt polls
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja on Thursday accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad, clarifying that the polls would be held as scheduled.

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has scheduled the polls for Dec 20. The last LG term expired in Feb 2021, and the ECP was supposed to conduct elections within 120 days. However, the federal government and the ECP spent the last several years carrying out delimitations and announcing election schedules, only to postpone the polls later.

On Thursday, a three-member bench headed by the CEC heard the case about alleged violations of the electoral code in the NA-77 by-election.

During the hearing, Raja mentioned that the federal government has ordered that teachers would not be assigned duty in the Islamabad LG polls.

“Where will the [ECP] bring staff from?” asked Raja, who remains the CEC by virtue of the 26th Amendment, though his constitutionally mandated five-year term ended on Jan 26, 2025.

“The [ECP] issues directions to the prime minister and the government; directions do not come from them to us,” the election commissioner said.

Taking notice of the Centre’s order, he claimed: “The federal government wants to sabotage the Islamabad local government elections.

“I make it clear that local government elections will be held in Islamabad,” Raja clarified.
