World.title: GECO, Jan De Nul sign MoU on Green Energy Corridor's subsea component
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 12. Green Energy Corridor (GECO) and the Belgian firm Jan De Nul Group have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on the subsea component of the Green Energy Corridor project, GECO reported.

According to the report, the General Director of GECO, Yusif Gayibov, visited the headquarters of Jan De Nul Group, where the document was signed in the presence of the company’s owner, Jan Pieter De Nul.

The memorandum establishes a framework for cooperation on the subsea portion of the project, which aims to transmit electricity generated from renewable sources in the Caspian region and Georgia to Europe via the Black Sea.

GECO noted that Jan De Nul Group’s expertise in executing long-distance subsea cable-laying projects will be leveraged as the initiative moves forward.

During the visit, Gayibov also toured one of the company’s cable-laying vessels, the Isaac Newton, which is capable of transporting and installing up to 10,700 tons of cable in a single voyage.

According to the report, the vessel has previously been deployed for cable-laying projects related to the transmission of renewable energy in the Netherlands, Greece, Germany, and Iceland.

GECO has expressed its interest in continued collaboration with Jan De Nul Group to connect the renewable energy potential of Azerbaijan and Georgia with European markets.

The Caspian-Black Sea-Europe Green Energy Corridor is a cross-border electricity transmission project involving Azerbaijan, Georgia, Romania and Hungary. It was established under a strategic partnership agreement signed in Bucharest on Dec. 17, 2022, with the participation of the European Commission. It envisages a transmission corridor with a total capacity of 3.9 gigawatts (GW), comprising three lines, each with a capacity of 1.3 GW.

The project is being developed by Green Energy Corridor Power Company (GECO), a Bucharest-registered joint venture owned by the national transmission system operators of the four countries. Azerbaijan's Azerenerji, Georgia's Georgian State Electrosystem, Romania's Transelectrica and Hungary's MVM each hold a 25% stake in the company.

The project is included in the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity's (ENTSO-E) Ten-Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) for 2026 under project numbers 1248 and 1244.

Total investment in the project is estimated at €22 billion, including €14.3 billion for electricity transmission infrastructure and €7.8 billion for renewable energy generation capacity.

The corridor is expected to reach its full transmission capacity by 2040. The results of the feasibility study were presented in Baku on Oct. 22, 2026.

World.title: Azerbaijan a significant factor for stability - North Macedonia's president
World.content:
DUBLIN, Ireland, November 12. Azerbaijan is a major factor in regional stability, and the decision to hold the European Political Community (EPC) summit in the country in 2028 demonstrates confidence in Baku and recognition of its role in regional and international processes, the President of North Macedonia, Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova said in response to Trend’s question on the sidelines of the European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin.

According to her, the participation of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev, in the current summit and the hosting of the upcoming 12th summit in Azerbaijan reflect the European Union’s growing interest in expanding relations with the countries of Eurasia and Asia.

“This is a positive step. It signifies a certain level of trust. It means that Azerbaijan is also viewed as a significant factor in stability,” she said.

Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova noted that against the backdrop of the energy crisis, European countries are increasingly turning their attention to nations with significant energy resources.

“During a serious energy crisis, all roads lead to countries known as energy producers,” she emphasized.

Speaking about the prospects for future visits to Azerbaijan, the President of North Macedonia spoke highly of the country, noting not only the high level of organization of international events, including the COP, but also its rich cultural and historical heritage.

She particularly highlighted her interest in the legacy of Nizami Ganjavi, emphasizing its significance for the culture, history, and people of Azerbaijan.

“I learned so much about him. I understand how important he is to your culture, your history, and your people. There were wonderful discussions there that I will never forget,” she added.

The 9th summit of the European Political Community (EPC) is being held in Dublin, the capital of Ireland. The event brings together leaders from nearly 50 European countries and other partner states.

The meeting is taking place at the Dublin Convention Centre, co-chaired by European Council President António Costa and Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin. The summit is being held under the motto "Europe – strong, secure and connected".

European security, Russia's war against Ukraine, economic competitiveness, energy security, transport infrastructure development and stronger regional connectivity are among the key topics on the agenda.

Particular attention will be paid to Europe's defense capabilities, efforts to counter cyberattacks, disinformation and other hybrid threats, as well as the division of responsibility for ensuring European security between European countries and the United States.

The economic agenda includes developing innovation and digital infrastructure, strengthening transport links, ensuring affordable and reliable energy supplies, and improving the resilience of the European economy to external shocks.

The European Political Community was established in 2022, following the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine war, as a platform for political dialogue and coordination among European countries.

For Azerbaijan, participation in the summit is particularly important in terms of energy cooperation, the peace process in the South Caucasus and the development of transport connectivity.

Azerbaijan is set to host the 12th EPC summit in May 2028, following the 10th and 11th summits in Switzerland and Greece, respectively, in 2027. The event will provide Baku with an opportunity to welcome European leaders and advance dialogue on regional and wider European issues.

Following the conclusion of the EPC summit in Dublin, a separate informal meeting of the leaders of the 27 EU member states will be held on November 13.

World.title: Azerbaijan, World Bank discuss priority areas of cooperation (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 12. Azerbaijan and the World Bank discussed priority areas for cooperation, the Ministry of Finance reported.

The discussion took place during a meeting between the Minister of Finance of Azerbaijan, Sahil Babayev, and a delegation that included the World Bank’s Regional Director for the South Caucasus, Rolande Pryce, and the Regional Practice Director for Prosperity in Europe and the Central Asian region, Abebe Adugna, held on November 12.

According to the information, the current state and future prospects of cooperation between Azerbaijan and the World Bank were discussed, covering topics such as macroeconomic stability and fiscal sustainability, economic diversification, public financial management, and reforms in state-owned enterprises, as well as other issues of mutual interest.

Babayev emphasized that Azerbaijan attaches special importance to its long-term partnership with the World Bank, highly valuing the Bank’s contribution to the country’s economic development, institutional reforms, and the modernization of the public sector. He noted that the Country Partnership Framework, covering the period 2025–2029, creates new opportunities for expanding cooperation in areas such as economic diversification, private sector development, productivity enhancement, and sustainable economic growth.

Noting that maintaining macroeconomic stability and strengthening fiscal sustainability are among the government’s key priorities, Babayev provided an overview of measures being taken to ensure the efficient management of public finances, reinforce fiscal discipline, improve the efficiency of budget expenditures, and gradually reduce dependence on oil and gas revenues. The importance of developing the non-oil sector, promoting private investment, and expanding export potential for long-term economic growth was also underscored.

Addressing reforms in the field of public financial management, Babayev highlighted initiatives such as the creation of the Digital Public Finance information system (DPFIS), which integrates budget planning, execution, treasury operations, and financial reporting into a unified digital environment, the expansion of program- and results-based budgeting mechanisms, and the digitalization of public procurement. The importance of continuing cooperation with the World Bank in these areas was noted.

Reforms in the financial management and oversight of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) were also a key focus of the meeting. The discussions covered potential cooperation with the World Bank to improve financial discipline, corporate governance, and dividend policies within SOEs, as well as to manage potential fiscal risks.

In this context, preparations for the Global Conference on State-Owned Enterprises, planned to be held in Baku in April 2027 in collaboration with the World Bank Group, were also addressed. During the meeting, it was noted that the conference would serve as an important platform for exchanging international experience on the management and financial sustainability of state-owned enterprises.

Furthermore, the parties reviewed the draft Report on the Observance of Standards and Codes (ROSC) in the areas of accounting and auditing, prepared with the support of the World Bank, along with its recommendations. The importance of improving relevant legislation, enhancing the quality and transparency of financial reporting, strengthening audit oversight mechanisms, and continuing the dialogue on issues requiring further discussion was emphasized.

During the meeting, views were also exchanged regarding the next phase of the World Bank’s analytical work on economic growth and diversification, as well as potential investment projects in the sectors of agriculture, water resource management, transport, and urban infrastructure.

Highly valuing the development of the partnership with Azerbaijan, World Bank representatives expressed their interest in continuing technical, analytical, and financial cooperation to support the country’s economic and institutional reforms, public financial management, and the state-owned enterprise sector.

World.title: President Ilham Aliyev meets with Prime Minister of Armenia in Dublin (PHOTO)
World.content:
Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

DUBLIN, Ireland, November 12. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev met with Prime Minister of the Republic of Armenia Nikol Pashinyan on the margins of the 9th European Political Community Summit in Dublin, Ireland on November 12, 2026, Trend's special correspondent reports.

The leaders exchanged views on advancing the peace agenda between Azerbaijan and Armenia, building on the outcomes of the Washington Peace Summit of August 8, 2025, and the Washington Joint Declaration signed on that occasion.

The discussions focused on practical steps towards further consolidating peace between the two countries, including the development of transport and transit connectivity, economic and trade relations, border delimitation, and the implementation of confidence-building measures.

In this context, the leaders discussed progress in the development of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), including the planning and design of its railway and highway components, as well as prospects for transit connectivity along the TRIPP route.

The transit of goods to and from Armenia through the territory of Azerbaijan was noted as a positive development. Since November of last year, a total of 105,000 tonnes of cargo have been transported to Armenia through the territory of Azerbaijan.

The sides also exchanged views on opportunities for further developing economic and trade relations between Azerbaijan and Armenia, including the forthcoming interconnection of electricity grids.

The leaders emphasized the importance of environmental and transboundary water cooperation and welcomed the establishment of working groups on the management of transboundary rivers.

The leaders reaffirmed the importance of maintaining positive momentum in the peace process and continuing dialogue aimed at strengthening peace, stability, and prosperity in the region.

World.title: Five shot, one killed, at Washington DC gym
World.content:
One person has been killed and four others injured after a man opened fire inside a gym in a central Washington DC neighbourhood.

Police said the suspected gunman had been located with a gunshot wound, believed to be self-inflicted, after he barricaded himself inside a nearby apartment building.

Negotiators had been communicating with the man for more than an hour before forcing their way inside the seventh-floor apartment. His condition is unknown.

The area is about 1.5 kilometres north of the White House.

Panic spread through the area after the man opened fire in the Vida gym on 15th St Northwest, in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, about 8am, local time.

Some officers were seen on nearby rooftops as local and federal law enforcement responded to the shooting. (AP: Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

Local area councillor Brooke Pinto said she believed the victim was targeted by the suspect over an apartment dispute.

Washington DC's acting police chief, Jeffery Carroll, earlier said the suspect had been involved in a "conflict" with the home-owners' association of the building.

"The suspect, in fleeing the scene, also shot others," Councillor Pinto told local television.

Mr Carroll said victims were shot at multiple locations.

One of the victims was in a critical condition, police said. The three other surviving victims had non-life-threatening injuries.

Gym-goers ran into a nearby bagel shop to shelter after the man started shooting, witnesses told reporters at the scene.

Residents watched from rooftops as police surrounded a nearby apartment building (Reuters: Aaron Schwartz)

One woman said she was on a treadmill when she heard a gunshot and saw a victim on the ground.

"It was, like, chaos. It was horrific," said said.

"We exited and then had to tell the police what was happening, and that's when more shots were happening, and that's when we all ran into Call Your Mother [bagel shop] around the corner," she said.

Buildings in the area were placed in lockdown as authorities surrounded the apartment complex and negotiated with the suspect.

Dozens of police vehicles were at the scene, which was cordoned off during the morning peak.

Members of the National Guard, who have been present in Washington DC as part of a crime crackdown ordered by US President Donald Trump, were also at the scene.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink communications disrupted as US envoys meet Putin
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian military units recorded significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service for several days, affecting the entire front line and Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

Starshield is the military version of Elon Musk's SpaceX's Starlink satellite communications service.

In a post on Telegram, Mr Zelenskyy said that systemic restrictions were limiting the speed at which Starshield could be used to 161 kph.

Ukrainian military units have recorded significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service, affecting the entire front line. (Reuters: Inna Varenytsia)

As a result of the restrictions, Ukrainian interceptors could not reach sufficient speed to down Russian jet-powered drones, with some hits already occurring, Mr Zelenskyy said.

"This helps Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes on Ukraine," he said, adding that Ukraine was trying to clarify the reasons for the restriction with the US side.

In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said SpaceX had abruptly capped the speed of Starlink and Starshield, cutting off drones and other equipment moving faster than about 160 kph amid tensions with the Trump administration over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Service was restored on October 24.

Mr Zelenskyy's comments came as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow for talks aimed at ending the conflict.

After the meeting had concluded, the Kremlin said it had agreed to continue talks.

A Ukrainian official said there was no mention of the disruptions during separate US-brokered talks earlier this week in Abu Dhabi and it was unclear who had made the decision over Starlink.

Starlink slowdown in Ukraine Ukraine says people will die as a result of throttled Starlink services in the country. Here's how its armed forces rely on the crucial service.

Ukraine has carried out a series of strikes against Russian refineries and energy installations in recent weeks, as Moscow has continued to pummel Ukrainian electricity infrastructure and cities with drones and missiles.

"So far we know very little," Mr Zelenskyy said, addressing European leaders in Dublin.

"But some things are already clear: if someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then it tells us where things are going."

Europe presents new sanctions against Russia

The European Commission will present a new sanctions package against Russia and proposals on Ukraine-related financial measures before the next European Council, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Thursday.

The next European Council is a special summit on November 26-27.

Inside Russia's prison system Russia's FSB snatched US journalist Evan Gershkovich in a Yekaterinburg restaurant. What followed was life in a Russian jail cell and being part of a prisoner swap for an assassin.

The package will be the EU's 22nd against Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

Among the measures, the package is expected to include new restrictions on banks, cryptocurrencies and crypto platforms, and measures to close circumvention loopholes through third countries, EU diplomats said.

The package may also include a ban on Belarusian and Russian athletes competing in international meets in the EU, the diplomats said.

Car bomb kills Russian military member

A member of the Russian military was killed after the car he was driving was blown up in St Petersburg, investigators said, in what appeared to be the latest in a series of targeted killings that Russia has blamed on Ukraine.

Video showed that military police had sealed off the area in the Pushkinsky District of the city as investigators and forensic scientists worked at the scene.

Ukraine and Russia agree to large prisoner swap Following two days of US-mediated talks, Ukraine and Russia have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war.

A bomb-damaged dark blue SUV stood on a road littered with blast debris next to what looked like an empty passenger bus, which appeared to have also suffered damage.

Russia has blamed Ukraine for previous assassinations of senior military officials and people linked to Moscow's war effort.

Ukrainian sources have claimed responsibility in some cases, while denying others.

There was no immediate comment from Ukraine on Thursday.

Another serviceman was killed in a car explosion in the same district of Russia's second largest city on August 27.

Other car bomb attacks have occurred in Moscow and Crimea, which Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014, in recent months.

Reuters

World.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits after affair with alleged Chinese spy
World.content:
Jensen Huang, the co-founder of global artificial intelligence giant Nvidia, has resigned as chief executive effective immediately.

The news comes days after the California-based company launched an independent investigation following Mr Huang's acknowledgement that he had an affair with a Chinese business associate.

According to The New York Times, US intelligence determined that the woman — former Megaspeed managing director Alice Huang — was gathering information for China.

Beijing has denied the spying allegations and Nvidia has said it had "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.

Nvidia's board of directors held an emergency meeting that reportedly continued into the early hours of Thursday morning, local time.

Following the meeting, the company released a statement saying Mr Huang had resigned as president, chief executive officer and as a member of the board.

Colette Kress will serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer for NVIDIA. (Nvidia via Reuters)

The company's Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who has worked for Nvidia since 2013, will serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent replacement is found.

“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Ms Kress said in a statement.

The company thanked Mr Huang for his "immeasurable contributions" to not only Nvidia but the wider industry.

Nvidia's new board chair Harvey Jones said he expected "the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption".

US President Donald Trump weighed in saying Mr Huang had "done a fantastic job" and should be replaced by "a legend".

"There is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," he wrote on Truth Social.

"A legend replaces a legend."

Jensen Huang has become the focus of an independent investigation into an affair he had with a suspected Chinese spy.

The company and Mr Huang are also facing a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Mr Huang's ties with Ms Huang — a Chinese citizen and former executive at the Singapore-based data centre company.

US President Donald Trump earlier this week confirmed the FBI was looking into the affair, and described Mr Huang as a "very honourable man".

House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said he expected Mr Huang to testify to Congress sometime within the next week.

Nvidia has become the top supplier of AI chips at the centre of the global AI boom and US-China technology rivalry.

US House Speaker Mike Johnson said he was "in favour" of limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China.

"And I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take. Especially in the light of recent developments, it makes sense," he said.

'Dark day' for US tech industry

Mr Huang's departure could leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly $US4 trillion ($5.8 trillion) chipmaker he co-founded and built over more than three decades.

Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy The chief executive of the world's most valuable company and a close ally of Donald Trump admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Here's what we know.

Mr Huang, 63, has no obvious successor and owns about 3.6 per cent of Nvidia's stock.

Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 13 per cent in early Wall Street trading following the announcement, which dragged the broader stock market lower.

Asian shares also fell on Thursday as investors kept a nervous eye on what action Nvidia's board would take.

Nvidia stock has shed at least 24 per cent of its value over the past month, wiping around $US1.4 trillion ($2 trillion) off its market capitalisation.

US voters overwhelmingly rejected data centres The US midterms cemented the issue of data centres as politically toxic. But now the industry will be looking for a new place to call home.

Nvidia has been a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom.

While some analysts believe Mr Huang's departure will not affect AI projects already in the works, others think it will.

Adam Sarhan, of 50 Park Investments, said Mr Huang's resignation comes amid a period of weakness in AI stocks due in part to worries about overbuilding capacity and exacerbated by US elections that showed public anger towards data centres.

"Why would I invest more in AI until we figure out what's going on?" he said.

Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives called it "a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry" but said the company's board needed to "rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him".

Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments, said Nvidia now risked losing its "technology roadmap".

"That roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," he said.

"In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself."

Singapore bans Alice Huang over 'possible offences'

An image shared by software company Net Thunder on LinkedIn in 2024, which it says shows Megaspeed's Alice Huang sitting alongside Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang at an event in Taiwan. (Supplied: NetThunder/LinkedIn)

Alice Huang was banned from re-entering Singapore after she left the country in February, Singapore's home affairs ministry has confirmed.

The ministry said Ms Huang was investigated for possible offences including buying servers that were exported via Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market.

But the ministry said there was insufficient evidence to find Ms Huang had committed any offences and she was issued a warning.

In its first statement since the scandal broke, Singapore-headquartered Megaspeed International said on Thursday that it took its obligation to comply with US export control laws "extremely seriously" and was "committed to working constructively and transparently" with the US government.

World.title: With club in drop zone, Manchester United sacks manager Michael Carrick
World.content:
Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United manager, becoming the latest casualty of the English Premier League giant's revolving door of coaches.

The club has ​won only three ​of its 15 matches in all ‌competitions ⁠under Carrick this season — including just one league victory — to sit in the relegation zone.

Despite a massive budget and a star-studded squad, the Red Devils are in 18th spot on eight points after 10 games, ​one point from ​the ⁠bottom.

With Manchester United not in action again until November 22 due to the international break, the club issued a statement on Thursday morning.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," it said on its website.

Sky Sports is reporting that former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino, the current United States head coach, is set to take over following a verbal agreement in principle, but United is still negotiating terms for his backroom staff.

Manchester United's shocking run of results leaves the club in the Premier League relegation zone. (Getty Images: Marc Atkins)

45-year-old Carrick's departure after just 10 months in charge continues a period of instability at Old Trafford, with United having appointed seven permanent managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 following 26 years at the helm.

The final nail in the coffin may have been a 4-4 draw ​at home to Aston Villa ⁠over the weekend, ​even though United scored twice in added time to salvage a point.

The former midfielder, who made 316 Premier League appearances for the club between 2006 and 2018, took over in January 2026, initially as interim manager.

He received a permanent contract in May after guiding United to third place in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.

His early success included victories over Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool.

After a promising start as Manchester United manager, Michael Carrick has lost his way this season. (Getty Images: Marco Luzzani)

But results deteriorated dramatically this season, leaving him with a winning percentage of just 46.9 per cent.

Carrick came under mounting pressure after a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth last month, with the former England international carrying the air of someone awaiting the inevitable after the defeat when fans chanted his name but booed the players off the pitch.

He had dropped captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench against Bournemouth and did not bring him on even when United were desperate for inspiration in midfield, but the struggling club gave Carrick another chance to revive its season.

The Red Devils have not won a Premier League title since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. (Reuters)

To that point, United had gone eight matches without a win in all competitions.

Manchester United share the record of 20 English top-flight league titles with Liverpool.

But United has not won the Premier League since 2012-13, Sir Alex Ferguson's final season in charge, with its title drought now extending into a 14th season.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Floreat gunman inadvertently recorded himself during shooting, inquest hears
World.content:
A gunman who murdered a mother and daughter in their Perth home inadvertently recorded himself firing the fatal shots on one of the victims' phones, a coronial inquest has heard.

WARNING: This story contains details that may distress some readers.

The shocking detail emerged at the inquest into the murders of Jennifer Petelcyzc and her 18-year-old daughter Gretl, who were killed by Mark Bombara before he took his own life.

Bombara forced his way into their Floreat home while searching for his estranged wife.

There was a heavy police presence the day after the shooting. (ABC News: Julian Robins)

Senior Sergeant Nathan Carbone from the WA Police Homicide Squad investigated the deaths.

He told the court Bombara shot Jennifer Petelcyzc, then Gretyl, after which he grabbed Jennifer's phone and "inadvertently" recorded himself firing two more shots.

The gunman killed Jennifer and Gretl Petelczyc in their home in 2024. (Supplied)

It is not known if it is an audio or video recording.

Jennifer Petelcyzc and Rowena Bombara were best friends, and Bombara mistakenly believed his estranged wife was staying at the Floreat home.

Gunman 'manipulative'

The court heard Rowena Bombara and her daughter Ariel had moved out of the family home in April 2024, just weeks before the murders, and had sought police assistance to move their belongings from the house.

When police arrived at the house, Bombara's son opened the door and appeared nervous, saying his father had "all the [gun] licences you can possibly imagine".

Questions over police response before Floreat murders The coroner in the Floreat murder-suicide inquest questions why a desperate call to Triple Zero stating someone had been shot in a family violence situation was initially marked as a priority two situation.

"I don't know if there are any firearms in [the safe] … there may be firearms in other locations," Issac Bombara is heard to say on the body-worn camera footage.

Constable Shaun King called for a second police car to attend and told the arriving officers to make sure they had "their plates in", referring to their protective vests.

But when he entered the house and met Bombara, he was the "opposite" of what he was expecting.

"I hate to say it, but he seemed like a nice man," Constable King told the court.

Constable Shaun King says he should have looked at Bombara's gun safe, in hindsight. (ABC News)

Bombara was accommodating, offering refreshments and allowing the officer to inspect his gun safe.

Constable King turned him down as he "did not want to escalate the situation" but admitted in hindsight he "should have" looked at the safe.

The coroner's court heard the conversation was an attempt by Bombara to "groom" the junior officers into thinking he was not a threat, despite his access to firearms.

"I believe it was manipulative … calculated … in an effort to place seeds of doubt in the attending officers' minds," said Superintendent Andrew Wilson, who reviewed the body-worn camera footage.

"In my opinion he was quite determined to find out what would happen to his guns … I believe he took the opportunity to try and manage that conversation."

Superintendent Wilson agreed this was common behaviour in a family violence situation.

He said police policy had changed since the Floreat murders.

Superintendent Andrew Wilson describes the gunman's demeanor as "manipulative" to officers.

Firearms are seized, and domestic violence perpetrators are removed from the home before family enter to retrieve their belongings.

World.title: Putin kills many enemies, one convicted of espionage has a different story
World.content:
Yekaterinburg, Russia, 2023. American journalist Evan Gershkovich is sitting in a restaurant talking to a source.

A number of masked men enter.

They inform the American that he is being arrested by Russia's main intelligence agency, the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation.

Known as the FSB, it's the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, where Russian President Vladimir Putin previously worked.

Gershkovich is now the first US journalist to be arrested in Russia since the Cold War. He is hooded and thrown in a van before the agents get to work.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, who as a Russian secret service KGB served in the German Democratic Republic, was equipped with a house card of the responsible Ministry of State Security service. (Supplied: BSTU)

Vladimir Putin's details are seen on the Stasi identification card found in Germany.

"The hood gets ripped off at one point," Gershkovich told 7.30.

"There's operatives sitting next to me and a man across from me in a suit. He asks, 'Who do you work for?' I say the Wall Street Journal.

" The hood goes back on [and] fists pummel my midsection and the hood comes back off again. "

The question is repeated before Gershkovich arrives at a station and is charged with espionage.

Lefortovo pre-trial detention centre in Moscow, Russia. (Reuters: Shamil Zhumatov)

The charge strikes fear into the foreign correspondent. He knows Russia under Putin has a reputation for doing whatever it takes to silence enemies of the state.

In 2018, former Russian spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter, Yulia, were targeted in an assassination attempt with deadly nerve agent Novichok. They would ultimately survive the poisoning.

Former Putin opponent Alexei Navalny survived an attempt on his life undertaken with Novichok before his eventual death in February 2024, in one of Russia's harshest prisons.

And in August 2023 former Putin ally Yevgeny Prigozhin perished in a plane crash, while a number of other former allies have disappeared.

Gershkovich told 7.30 that his main fear was torture.

City view of Yekaterinburg in Russia where Evan Gershkovich was initially detained. (Reuters: Evgenia Novozhenina)

"I've reported on cases where somebody's brought to a station, strapped to a chair, electrodes are attached to various parts of their body, and they're electrocuted, simply for the fact of trying to get them to sign papers that attest to the fact that they're guilty in a fabricated case," he said.

Life in the 'exchange bank'

The fear was real but for Gershkovich, the torture would not come. The FSB and Russian authorities had something else in mind.

Gershkovich realised he had been set up as Russia looked to replenish its "exchange bank".

That "bank", Gershkovich says, is all about Russia having a number of foreigners it can use in exchange to get some of its own incarcerated back.

In his case, the main target was Russian hitman Vadim Krasikov, who was serving jail time in Germany, having been convicted in 2019 over the brazen daylight murder of a former Chechen militant in a Berlin park in 2018.

The judge called the killing of Georgian citizen Zelimkhan Khangoshvili "state terrorism", adding that the order had almost certainly come from Putin himself.

Among the evidence he cited for Russian state involvement were Krasikov's official Russian papers containing a false identity, and the fact that Russian law empowered Putin to order the murder of state enemies abroad.

The IK-3 penal colony, where Russian opposition politician Alexei Navalny served his jail term. (Reuters)

Gershkovich said he knew almost immediately prisoner exchange would be the case once he had arrived in his "really tiny" prison cell that measured 2.4 metres by 3 metres by 3.7 metres.

"It has a bed running on one wall, a bed at the end perpendicular at the window, a desk running down the other, and it's so thin that only one person can fit walking up and down that space, and you eventually have a cellmate," he told 7.30.

"So there are two of you living in the cell, and you can only walk up and down six or seven steps.

"On my second night in prison on TV, I'm watching the main evening news show and one of the hosts says to the other host 'we've replenished our exchange fund'.

"The Russians use that as a catch-all for the foreigners that they hold to be swapped."

Gershkovich says he was treated relatively well compared to other prisoners he knew about.

"I've been reporting obviously on stories of Ukrainian civilians, Ukrainian POWs, Russian political prisoners," he said.

"[They] were tortured, deprived of hot food, hot showers, told they're never gonna see their families again, that's not happening to me.

"Really early on, my mattress is thicker than my cellmate's. Before the US ambassador comes to visit, the prison warden comes and checks in on me, asks how I'm doing.

"Eventually, there's even a moment where I say 'I'm surprised how much you're checking in on me'. He says, 'Of course, we care about your health.'

" I joke, 'Well, the package has to be whole and undamaged or its value will go down,'" and he checks [over] his shoulder, gets all serious and says, 'I didn't tell you this, but yes.' "

While it had become clear to Gershkovich that he was waiting for a swap, the death of Navalny was a blow and he remembers it as a moment that was likely intended to strike fear.

Russian opposition politician Alexei Navalny was a major opponent of Putin. (Reuters: Shamil Zhumatov)

He heard the news while he was on his one hour a day on the jail's roof, his only time outside the tiny cell.

"We're on this walk and suddenly the radio, which never happens, switches to the news and we hear that Alexei Navalny has died, and then it switches back," he said.

"I think they did that for the Ukrainians who were being held in the prison, the Russian political prisoners, perhaps myself too, very deliberately to send a message to us."

Before his death, there had been reports Navalny could form part of a prisoner swap deal in exchange for Russian assassin Krasikov.

But six months later, the swap happened in Türkiye, and the journalist was released alongside fellow Americans Paul Whelan and Alsu Kurmasheva.

What Russians think of Putin

Gershkovich used his 16 months in prison to learn more about Putin's Russia and what people really thought of a leader he said was growing more authoritarian while the war in Ukraine rolled on.

Vladimir Putin in Red Square in Moscow. (Sputnik: Yuri Kochetkov/Pool via Reuters)

"When Putin came to power it coincided with this big oil and gas boom," Gershkovich said of his May 2000 inauguration as president for the first time.

"At the same time, he made really clear what would happen politically if you tried to challenge him.

"The social contract that was essentially developed was your life will get better, money is pouring in as long as you stay out of politics.

"That is essentially the logic of the regime over the next 20, 25 years, except that it gets more and more repressive.

"By the time I go to prison, what I, and I think the best sociologists and researchers working on Russia will tell you, is that 15 per cent of people really support Putin in the war, 15 per cent really are anti-Putin and anti-war."

He said the rest would abstain from making any comment on the war, such was the fear Putin wielded on either side of the prison walls.

Evan Gershkovich reunites with his mother while US President Joe Biden looks on after a successful prisoner swap between the US and Russia. (Reuters: Kevin Mohatt)

Gershkovich said one prison guard perfectly encapsulated the example, telling him: "The news is so bad, I try not to follow it. I go to my dacha, my country house, I fish."

"So I asked him what he thought about the war," Gershkovich said.

"He smiled and zippered his mouth shut, put a finger to his mouth and kind of shrugged his shoulders. And what he was telling me is, I think, 'I don't support the war, but I can't talk about it.'

" I think the vast majority of Russians are somewhere in that camp. "

World.title: Marsh dodges Sandpapergate questions in testy press conference exchange
World.content:
Australia's one-day captain, Mitch Marsh, has refused to address key aspects of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal as journalists peppered him with questions at a press conference.

Marsh, who was bowling when Cameron Bancroft was spotted hiding a piece of sandpaper in his pants during the 2018 series, spent most of the 12-minute press conference straight-batting questions about the infamous South Africa tour and Usman Khawaja's explosive allegations.

The very first question put to Marsh was: "Did you know that sandpaper was being used to tamper with cricket balls in South Africa?"

"Jeez, you hit a six off the first ball there, mate. Well done," Marsh replied.

Loading Instagram content

"I respect that certain people have told their stories, but I'm not here to share mine.

"I know that might sound weird, but it's a big week for us, and it's an important time for this one-day group.

"I really respect that Uzzy has told his story. He's written his book, and my focus is really on tomorrow."

Marsh was continually peppered with questions about why he was not willing to speak on the topic.

"I've personally moved on," he said.

Mitch Marsh says he has no ill feelings towards Usman Khawaja for the allegations made in his book. (Getty Images: Paul Kane)

"I respect that others probably haven't, but I have, and I hope that's respected.

"This is my choice to not go back there. Who knows? Maybe I'll write a book one day."

Marsh insisted he held no grudges against Khawaja.

"I respect Uzzy for telling his story and for writing his book, and I don't sit here coming from a place of judgement," Marsh said.

"Everyone's got their story. Some will be willing to share it, and others might not, purely on the basis of the fact that they've moved on.

"It's really important that at some stage we do."

Australia's Test captain, Pat Cummins, is set to front a press conference in Sydney tomorrow morning and has promised to answer "any and all media".

AAP

World.title: Surgeon among six killed in Israeli air strike on Gaza hospital
World.content:
Palestinian health authorities say a surgeon is one of at least six people who have been killed in an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza.

The attack happened in the early hours of Thursday morning, local time. Video from the scene shows extensive damage to one of the compound's buildings.

Gaza's Civil Defense agency said the surgery department was hit and that at least 20 people were injured in the blast.

Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza, medics say Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.

Hours after the strike, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said a "senior Hamas terrorist and additional terrorists" had been using the hospital as a command centre.

"Targeting a medical facility that includes patients receiving treatment and teams performing their humanitarian and professional duty represents a serious attack on the health system and a flagrant violation of international laws and conventions that ensure the protection of medical facilities, employees and patients," Gaza's health ministry said in a statement.

"The ministry confirms that the continued targeting of hospitals and their medical facilities exacerbates the suffering of the sick and wounded, and threatens what remains of the ability of the health sector to provide its services, in light of the catastrophic conditions in the Gaza Strip."

Rizk Abu Shaira was the surgeon who was killed, the ministry said.

"He never hesitated to provide service to his patients," the head of Nasser Hospital, Dr Ahmed al-Farra said.

"He was on top of his work. He was in his room, between following up cases, treatments and preparing cases for surgery, but it was God's will and he was martyred in this treacherous strike.

"There are also doctors who were wounded in this attack."

Hamas labelled the strike a "fully fledged war crime".

At least six people have been killed in an Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza. (Reuters: Ramadan Abed)

Israeli group condemns attacks on health system

Israel regularly justifies attacks on medical and humanitarian facilities by insisting they lose their protections under international law if they are used by Hamas for terrorist activities.

In this instance, the IDF said Hamas had been using Nasser Hospital as a command centre and claimed the buildings were being used to store weapons and conduct interrogations.

Israeli forces revealed the identity of their target, Muhammad Abu Ismail, hours after their first acknowledgement of the attack.

"Muhammad Abu Ismail was responsible for overseeing the activities of the brigade’s terrorists and directing them to advance and carry out terrorist plots against IDF troops and Israeli civilians.

"He was also responsible for holding numerous hostages captive throughout the war."

Earlier, the IDF released graphics showing the building it hit, but did not provide any further evidence to back up its claims about its use by Hamas.

Measuring Israel's expansion across the Middle East ABC analysis reveals the extent of Israel's expansion on four fronts: Lebanon, the West Bank, Gaza and Syria.

"The IDF and the [Israel Security Agency] strongly condemn the Hamas terrorist organisation's cynical exploitation of civilian and medical infrastructure for military purposes, while endangering the lives of patients, medical personnel, and civilians," it said in a statement.

"Prior to and during the strike, steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance."

The IDF also released audio of what it said was a warning issued to the health ministry for Hamas to cease using hospitals across the strip, or risk further action by the military.

"Israel's genocide in Gaza continues under the guise of a ceasefire," Israeli advocacy group Physicians for Human Rights Israel said.

"Repeated attacks on hospitals and healthcare workers are further devastating an already shattered healthcare system, denying Palestinians in Gaza access to essential medical care and the ability to recover and live in dignity.

"The international community's inaction and continued impunity enable these attacks on Gaza's healthcare system. As long as those responsible are not held accountable, the attacks will continue."

Nasser Hospital targeted multiple times

Palestinian health authorities say more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since the October 2025 ceasefire, many of them civilians, including women and children.

The death toll in Gaza now stands at more than 74,600 people.

Nasser Hospital has been targeted a number of times during the three-year long war in Gaza, triggered by Hamas's deadly attacks on Israel in October 2023.

UN inquiry on Gaza and the West Bank Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since last October's ceasefire, according to a report from UN-commissioned experts. Israel has rejected the findings as "misinformation".

On August 25 last year, the hospital was the scene of a "double-tap" strike by Israeli forces.

The IDF claimed it was targeting a Hamas terrorist when it opened fire on a camera operator who had placed his camera on the outside of the hospital to film the Khan Younis skyline.

Minutes later, as emergency workers and fellow journalists were crawling over the site of the attack, another strike hit the building.

Twenty-two Palestinians were killed that day, including five journalists.

Among them were journalists working for the Associated Press and Reuters. The agencies and other media outlets condemned the strikes.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu labelled that incident a "tragic mishap" and the IDF said it had launched an investigation into the matter.

Its findings are yet to be released.

Gaza's health ministry says the strike on Nasser Hospital was a "flagrant violation of international laws". (Reuters)

Israeli attacks across Gaza have reportedly increased in recent days, despite the ceasefire being in place.

Progress towards the next stage of the ceasefire remains stalled, with Hamas saying it will lay down its weapons only if Israel stops launching strikes and withdraws from territory.

Israel says it will only stop once Hamas demilitarises and no longer poses a threat to the country.

Both sides have been criticised for the delays, although the Trump administration-backed Board of Peace has ratcheted up its rhetoric against the Israeli government in recent months, accusing it of avoiding holding up its side of the bargain.

World.content:
Updated WorldNorth AmericaMass shooting One dead, four injured after gunman opens fire in Washington DC Michael Koziol Updated November 13, 2026 — 4:05am ,first published 2:11am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Warning: Graphic content The Australian embassy in Washington DC was in lockdown on Thursday (US time) after a gunman killed a man at a nearby gym and shot four others before barricading himself in an apartment. The shooting took place at about 8am in and around Vida Fitness in the trendy Logan Circle neighbourhood, just north of the city centre. Emergency services at the scene. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson After shooting the man inside the gym, the gunman left the premises and shot four other people at a nearby construction site and in the lobby of the apartment building above the gym, police said.



He then barricaded himself inside a unit on the seventh floor, believed to be his home. At one point a small fire broke out in the building and was contained. Police said the man later shot himself during negotiations, and died from his injuries. Jeffery Carroll, the intern chief of DC Metro police, said the gunman was involved in a conflict with his building management. “We do know there was a conflict between him and the homeowners association of that building,” Carroll said. “We’re continuing to look into that.” Police said the shooter had barricaded themselves inside a building. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson



Much of the block around the shooting site was cordoned off by police tape on Thursday morning (US time). Schools near the scene were placed on lockdown. Staff at the nearby Australian embassy on 16th Street were also ordered to shelter in place. The lockdown was later lifted. DC Mayor Muriel Bowser said the White House had been briefed. The shootings occurred about 1.5km north of the White House. James Spellman was at the gym a little after 8am (midnight AEDT) when he heard shots being fired. He said there were about 50 people in the gym at the time. “Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” he said. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”



Spellman said he and other gym members ran out of the gym, and he said he heard more gunfire in the area of 15th Street. He said he heard about two shots fired in the gym and about five or six fired outside. Witness Ryan Dubicki was in his nearby apartment around 8am when, he said, he “heard about five bangs”. “They were really spread out so I thought it was construction,” he said. It was only a short time later that he looked out “and there were cops everywhere”. Vida Fitness emailed members to say the Logan Circle location was closed until further notice. “Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this incident. We understand that this news may be deeply concerning to our VIDA community,” the gym said.

World.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair scandal
World.content:
TechnologyExecutive shake-up Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair scandal Kelvin Chan Updated November 13, 2026 — 2:20am ,first published 1:05am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing. His troubles compounded late on Wednesday (US time) after media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reported to him. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson Nvidia said Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and a member of the board was “effective immediately”. The ouster sets off a scramble to find a permanent replacement to lead Nvidia, which did not have a succession plan. The board will consider candidates from both inside and outside the company, Nvidia said in a statement.



The company named Colette Kress, the executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim chief executive. She became CFO in 2013, overseeing the company’s global finance operations. Before that, she worked for three years at Cisco and spent 13 years at Microsoft. Related Article Updated

Technology & democracy ‘I was unfaithful to my wife’: Nvidia boss admits to affair with suspected Chinese spy In a statement on Thursday, Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. The board of directors also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Jones, an entrepreneur and venture investor. Shares of Nvidia tumbled 14 per cent at the opening bell on Thursday, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq slid 1.5 per cent. The company is due to report earnings on Tuesday.



Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations about his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The two are not related. Alice Huang with Jensen Huang in June 2024 in Taipei. In its first statement since the scandal broke, Megaspeed said on Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with US export control laws “extremely seriously”. The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.



Last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang – and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. On Sunday, US President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating. Related Article Analysis

AI Jensen Huang once told me his two golden rules. He may have broken one of them Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singaporean authorities said Thursday that they questioned Alice Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed. They concluded last year that there wasn’t enough evidence that she had committed a crime but barred her from returning to the country. China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. In January, he won Trump’s approval for selling to China its H200 chips.



Megaspeed said on Thursday that it has cooperated with the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on exports of technology, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant US government authority”. Related Article Billionaires Nvidia billionaire’s affair scandal drags his wife of 41 years into the spotlight It said it has hired a US law firm to handle a “comprehensive census” of its computer chips and to verify its export controls. “Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable US laws,” it said. Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed’s finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost $US3 billion, according to Singapore corporate records.



Revenue surged to over $US294 million in 2024 from none in 2023. AP Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.content:
Exclusive BusinessConsumer affairsMiddle East tensions Bowser relief: Petrol prices tumble as global oil cost falls Nick Toscano November 13, 2026 — 12:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Australian motorists are finally seeing some relief at the petrol pump, new analysis shows, as steep falls in global oil prices start flowing through to service stations, wiping roughly 20¢ a litre off local fuel costs so far this month. For the first time since August, average petrol and diesel prices have started to tumble nationwide, driven by a sharp 20 per cent drop in the cost of Tapis Crude, Australia’s regional oil benchmark, over the past fortnight. World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaTragedy Death toll rises to eight after New York apartment block collapse Yuki Iwamura Updated November 12, 2026 — 11:48pm ,first published 2:14pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. New York: At least eight people have died after a three-storey building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site, New York City’s mayor said, as firefighters continue to dig through the rubble to find others who may be trapped beneath the wreckage. The building came down about 4pm on Wednesday (8am Thursday AEDT) in the Flatbush area. At least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said as he confirmed the death toll had risen to eight on Thursday. Loading “There are no words for a loss of this magnitude,” Mamdani said. Scores of firefighters and police officers wielding pickaxes and power saws clambered over the rubble pile overnight, punching holes through the ruins to pull dust-covered people from beneath piles of twisted wood and brick.



Rescuers used dogs to sniff for survivors. Firefighters used orange buckets as they removed debris from the rubble piles trying to reach people who may be trapped. View post on X Heavy rain was forecast for the city on Thursday afternoon. It wasn’t immediately known how that would affect search efforts. The cause of the collapse was under investigation, but New York City’s buildings commissioner, Ahmed Tigani, noted that when the building fell, construction workers were excavating an empty lot next door for a new building. First responders work at the scene of the building collapse in Brooklyn. AP



Much of the rubble from the collapsed building – a mixed-use structure with apartments sitting atop ground-floor commercial space – wound up in a huge pile inside the construction pit. Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing. About 250 firefighters were working the scene, Mamdani said. On Wednesday night (New York time), firefighters pulled a woman – still alive and moving – out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting her up on a stretcher and rushing to a waiting ambulance. Additional people were pulled from beneath the pile as the night went on. A woman is rescued from the rubble. AP Photo/Ryan Murphy It is not known how many people were inside the building when it collapsed. AP



Seven of the casualties were children, authorities said, without specifying whether any were among the dead. FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said the rescue teams were performing “dangerous and perilous” work. “Every move is choreographed,” she said. One firefighter sustained minor injuries, fire officials said. Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.



One resident of the collapsed building, Anderson Velez, told the New York Post he was at work when his wife called and said she and their two kids, aged seven and two, were trapped in the wreckage. “She called me when the building collapsed while she was inside with rubble on top of her. She was screaming for someone to help get my son out and then the call cut off,” he said. Velez said he later learned that his family had been pulled from the rubble alive. World.title: Meta reinstates page dedicated to tracking the murder of women in Australia
World.content:
Updated PoliticsFederalDomestic violence Meta reinstates page dedicated to tracking the murder of women in Australia Brittany Busch Updated November 12, 2026 — 11:24pm ,first published 6:02pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Meta has reinstated a social media account that tracks women murdered in Australia after a leading anti-violence campaigner accused the tech giant of censorship. On Thursday, researcher and journalist Sherele Moody called for her Australian Femicide Watch page on Instagram to be restored, after the platform claimed she had breached its community standards, without specifying which content was outside its guidelines. “Why is talking about women’s safety so offensive?” Moody said. Sherele Moody is an activist and writer known for her work on femicide and violence against women. Breeana Dunbar Femicide Watch counts every woman killed in Australia, and has become an important resource for advocates because governments do not publish real-time data. The project reported earlier this week that the number of women killed this year reached 61, after Victorian woman Baljit Kaur was allegedly stabbed to death.



As the federal government takes on big tech with its Digital Duty of Care – and sparked a debate about free speech in Australia – Moody questioned why her advocacy was being hampered, but no one was held accountable for the rape and death threats she regularly received online. “I’ve reported ... comments and posts and messages where people have made threats to end my life, and Meta has ruled them not against community standards,” she said. “However, women talking about violence against women are being censored, and our conversations are being removed.” Meta, Instagram’s parent company, was contacted for comment, and on Thursday night a spokesperson said it had corrected the error and restored the account. “Enforcing our policies at scale means our systems sometimes make mistakes, which is why we give people the ability to appeal our decisions. We acknowledge the important work Ms Moody does to raise awareness of violence against women and children in Australia,” they said, adding the guidelines were in place to protect people, particularly children, from harmful content.



Moody has been campaigning against violence against women for more than a decade, organising rallies, creating the popular She Matters mural in Melbourne, and has criticised the prime minister for dismissing her call for a royal commission into femicide – the petition for which has hit nearly 180,000 signatures. A campaign to reinstate Moody’s account had been mobilising online, with advocacy groups including Change.org, which hosts the royal commission petition, and GetUp swinging in behind her. Minister for Social Services Tanya Plibersek said on Thursday that Moody did important work raising awareness about domestic and sexual violence in Australia. “The tech bros should be focusing on cracking down on the filth being force-fed to our kids online, not silencing advocates,” she said. Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek. Alex Ellinghausen



Community Strong MP Zali Steggall called for the page to be reinstated, saying documenting the murder of Australian women and children was a vital public service. “What is a real breach of community standards is the violence perpetrated against women and children and the continued lack of effective government action,” she said. Moody said she appealed the decision on Sunday when she was notified her account was closed. She did not receive a response from Meta, which notified her the account would be permanently disabled if found to violate Meta’s community standards, until the publication of this story. The platform polices violent threats and sexualised content, but says it does not “prohibit threats when shared in awareness-raising or condemning context”. Moody said her posts did not glorify violence nor sexualise people, but called out misogyny. She said she had been repeatedly subjected to campaigns to remove her content.



“It’s just unbelievable that a page that exists to keep women alive is removed because it’s caused offence to, I don’t know, AI or some random crew of people who’ve reported it,” she said. “There’s a guy who’s been convicted of child sex abuse, who’s been reporting my posts as breaching copyright, and Meta’s allowed those reports to stand and has removed the material.” National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732). World.title: ‘Even a snail would agree’: Greta Thunberg slams Australia’s net zero pace
World.content:
PoliticsFederalClimate policy ‘Even a snail would agree’: Greta Thunberg slams Australia’s net zero pace Natassia Chrysanthos November 12, 2026 — 9:40pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Antalya, Turkey: Swedish activist Greta Thunberg has compared Australia’s pace of action on climate change to that of a snail, breaking her recent boycott of COP conferences to denounce this year’s leadership for losing control of rising temperatures. Thunberg made the remarks while standing next to an Indigenous advocate from the Northern Territory, Rikki Dank, who called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to “stop speaking and start listening” to calls to phase out fossil fuels during a press conference on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey on Thursday. Activist Greta Thunberg and Rikki Dank, a Gudanji and Wakaya Traditional Owner, rebuke Australia at their press conference. Getty Images Asked whether she agreed with Dank’s remarks about Australia’s record on climate change, Thunberg said: “I think even a snail would agree with that. It’s common sense. It doesn’t get more clear than that.” The pair were speaking on a panel of activists, including a volunteer in Nepal’s recent flash floods, who fronted a packed media scrum to rebel against the “implementation” focus of this year’s event.



Hosts Turkey and Australia, led by Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, are encouraging the rapid uptake of electrification rather than securing commitment to phasing out fossil fuels, which both countries export. The world is on track to overshoot its Paris Agreement of limiting global temperature rises to 1.5 degrees. Albanese defended Australia’s record as a climate leader on Tuesday, as United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres also challenged the hosts to be more ambitious in sending fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs”. The prime minister pointed to Australia’s doubling of renewable energy generation in six years, as well as the country’s significant uptake of rooftop solar. He will present alongside Pacific leaders later on Thursday to encourage investment in a resilience fund to help the region deal with climate change. Anthony Albanese, prime minister of Australia, speaks at the COP31 UN Climate Summit, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. AP Photo/Khalil Hamra Thunberg, who became famous at age 15 for her school strike for climate, spoke at COP conferences in 2018 and 2019. She has since boycotted most recent summits, citing the presence of fossil fuel lobbyists and the hosting of talks in oil-exporting states as evidence of hypocrisy.



Her appearance on Wednesday attracted more than 100 reporters and supporters, and she was escorted out by several security guards. Thunberg continued her criticism of COP from its sidelines, saying the people “least responsible for this crisis are being hit hardest and fastest”. “We are heading towards a future … where basic necessities become luxury, and it is more clear than ever in spaces like these that the situation could not be less under control,” she said. “The planet is not dying; it is being killed, and we know by who. And is being killed by the very same people often thought to come to our rescue.” Greta Thunberg at 15, when her school strike made international news. Anders Hellberg “We are all here because we know that the climate crisis is already here and now, and it is already a matter of life and death, and these disastrous trends that we are seeing unfolding all over the world are going to continue to exponentially get worse and worse,” Thunberg said. “We have to start acting accordingly. The actions from those in power here are completely detached from reality.”



Related Article Climate policy Albanese defends Australia as climate leader after being pushed on world stage to do more Dank, a Gudanji and Wakaya woman, spoke after Thunberg to directly challenge Albanese. The prime minister spoke at the opening ceremony of the COP31 leaders summit on Wednesday, where he said Australia was taking the concerns of the Pacific to the world stage. “Yesterday, my prime minister said he wanted to speak for the people of the world who needed urgent action,” Dank said. “Whilst yes, we do need urgent action… we don’t need him to speak for us. We can speak for ourselves, and I am here today to speak. “[Our prime minister] needs to stop speaking and start listening to our brothers and sisters across the world when they say they don’t want us to export coal, oil or gas, and the climate harms that they bring with them.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: One dead, four injured after gunman opens fire in Washington DC
World.content:
Updated WorldNorth AmericaMass shooting One dead, four injured after gunman opens fire in Washington DC Michael Koziol Updated November 13, 2026 — 4:05am ,first published 2:11am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Warning: Graphic content The Australian embassy in Washington DC was in lockdown on Thursday (US time) after a gunman killed a man at a nearby gym and shot four others before barricading himself in an apartment. The shooting took place at about 8am in and around Vida Fitness in the trendy Logan Circle neighbourhood, just north of the city centre. Emergency services at the scene. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson After shooting the man inside the gym, the gunman left the premises and shot four other people at a nearby construction site and in the lobby of the apartment building above the gym, police said.



He then barricaded himself inside a unit on the seventh floor, believed to be his home. At one point a small fire broke out in the building and was contained. Police said the man later shot himself during negotiations, and died from his injuries. Jeffery Carroll, the intern chief of DC Metro police, said the gunman was involved in a conflict with his building management. “We do know there was a conflict between him and the homeowners association of that building,” Carroll said. “We’re continuing to look into that.” Police said the shooter had barricaded themselves inside a building. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson



Much of the block around the shooting site was cordoned off by police tape on Thursday morning (US time). Schools near the scene were placed on lockdown. Staff at the nearby Australian embassy on 16th Street were also ordered to shelter in place. The lockdown was later lifted. DC Mayor Muriel Bowser said the White House had been briefed. The shootings occurred about 1.5km north of the White House. James Spellman was at the gym a little after 8am (midnight AEDT) when he heard shots being fired. He said there were about 50 people in the gym at the time. “Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” he said. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”



Spellman said he and other gym members ran out of the gym, and he said he heard more gunfire in the area of 15th Street. He said he heard about two shots fired in the gym and about five or six fired outside. Witness Ryan Dubicki was in his nearby apartment around 8am when, he said, he “heard about five bangs”. “They were really spread out so I thought it was construction,” he said. It was only a short time later that he looked out “and there were cops everywhere”. Vida Fitness emailed members to say the Logan Circle location was closed until further notice. “Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this incident. We understand that this news may be deeply concerning to our VIDA community,” the gym said.
